title: Eagles omitted Lane Johnson from public list of inactive players for Sunday
summary: The Eagles' decision to keep retired right tackle Lane Johnson on the 53-man roster for the rest of the season could create more than a little confusion.
full_text: The Eagles' decision to keep retired right tackle Lane Johnson on the 53-man roster for the rest of the season could create more than a little confusion. On Sunday morning, it already created some. When the team posted its “full list” of inactive players for the Week 5 game against the Jaguars, Johnson's name wasn't mentioned. Which implied to the world that Johnson was officially active for the game, despite his announced retirement. Per the Eagles, Johnson is one of inactive players. Per the league, Johnson was specifically listed as inactive for the game in the team's communications with the league, in compliance with all rules. So why not put him on the list of inactive players? As we understand it, the Eagles coordinated their overall approach to Johnson with the league office. He has declared to the word his retirement. He wasn't listed on the injury report on Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday. It's nevertheless something to watch with each upcoming game. If the Eagles are going to keep Johnson on the roster despite his retirement, the Eagles and the league should ensure that the public is aware of his status at all times. Think of it this way — if he continues to not be listed on the public injury report or among the publicly-announced inactives, he could (in theory) show up out of the blue to play on a Sunday, with no prior notice.
author: Mike Florio

title: Caleb Williams officially inactive for Bears, Tyson Bagent set to start against Packers
summary: Caleb Williams returned to practice for the Bears this week, but the quarterback's return to game action will have to wait at least one more week.
full_text: '' Caleb Williams returned to practice for the Bears this week, but the quarterback's return to game action will have to wait at least one more week. The Bears listed Williams as questionable, but the expectation was always that Williams would miss Sunday's game against the Packers because of his hamstring injury and the team confirmed it by listing him as inactive on Sunday morning. Unless Ben Johnson opts for a repeat of the creativity he showed last week, Tyson Bagent is set to start against Green Bay. Bagent was 25-of-34 for 268 yards and an interception in last Sunday's win over the Jets. If Williams returns in Week 6, he'll face the Falcons in his first game back.
author: Josh Alper

title: After playing in London, Colts have an added disadvantage on Sunday at Steelers
summary: The NFL schedule is a 272-piece jigsaw puzzle with millions of potential configurations and no one arrangement of pieces that will be completely fair and equitable to all 32 teams.
full_text: The NFL schedule is a 272-piece jigsaw puzzle with millions of potential configurations and no one arrangement of pieces that will be completely fair and equitable to all 32 teams. The Week 4 and Week 5 games in 2026 include a glitch about which the Colts should not be thrilled. They got the shoulder tap to fly to London for a game against the Commanders last Sunday. This week, after returning from England, the Colts travel to Pittsburgh for a game against the Steelers. Meanwhile, the Steelers had a bus trip to and from Cleveland for a Week 4 Thursday night game, followed by a mini-bye while their next foe was playing overseas. It's a basic issue of competitive integrity that will take a back seat to the ongoing obsession with global expansion. And the league will gloss over such irregularities because there's nothing that can be done to eliminate the annoyances and inconveniences that come from expecting teams to make long trips for games on foreign soil and to return home for the next game on the slate. That's one of the reasons why the league hopes to get clearance from the NFL Players Association to stage 16 international games per year. If every team has to travel to and from another country once per season, the hassle is largely balanced out. Still, there's something to be said for also ensuring that any team that plays on a given Sunday in another country will be facing on the following Sunday a team that played on Sunday or Monday, and not on the preceding Thursday. That part was avoidable for the 2026 schedule — and it was not avoided.
author: Mike Florio

title: Darius Cooper 62-yard touchdown gives Eagles lead over Jaguars in London
summary: The Eagles took their first lead of the game on another big play from Cooper.
full_text: ''' All Darius Cooper does is catch touchdowns. Cooper scored another one today in London, a 62-yarder from Jalen Hurts that gave the Eagles a 14-7 lead over the Jaguars. Cooper now has six catches this season, and four of them are touchdowns. He scored two touchdowns last week against the Rams and one in Week 2 against the Titans. Cooper made the Eagles' roster last season as an undrafted rookie out of Tarleton State, and he's showing he belongs in the NFL. Now the Jaguars have to show something in London, where the Eagles have come to life.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Will Shipley touchdown run ties Eagles and Jaguars 7-7 in London
summary: Shipley's score was the first first-half touchdown the Jaguars' defense has allowed this season.
full_text: The Eagles have evened the score this morning in London. Eagles running back Will Shipley ran in a two-yard touchdown to tie the Jaguars 7-7. The Eagles had previously thrown an incompletion on third down that would have resulted in them settling for a field goal, but Jaguars cornerback Travis Hunter was flagged for pass interference, giving the Eagles first-and-goal. Jaguars long snapper Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury on his first snap of the game and was replaced by defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton. Hamilton's first snap, an extra point, was high, but punter Logan Cooke grabbed it and placed it well enough for Cam Little to make the kick. Hamilton's second snap, a punt, was perfect.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Vikings' touchdown drought isn't keeping them from winning
summary: The 4-0 Vikings have turned the page back to the days of the Purple People Eaters.
full_text: The 4-0 Vikings have turned the page back to the days of the Purple People Eaters. And the stout defense isn't getting a ton of help from the offense. The Vikings have had 18 straight drives without a touchdown. The last one happened in the second quarter of a Week 3 win over the Buccaneers. The Week 4 victory over the Dolphins happened with five field goals. Yes, tight end T.J. Hockenson could have scored just before the two-minute warning, but he wisely took a knee and allowed the Vikings to ensure the Dolphins wouldn't be able to score twice and steal the game. Either way, the Vikings did not register a touchdown against the Dolphins. As noted last Sunday, the win made the Vikings the first team in more than 100 years to start 4-0 despite not scoring a touchdown in multiple games . The 1922 and 1923 Chicago Cardinals were the only other teams to accomplish that feat. If the Vikings do it again at any point this year, they'll become only the fourth team in NFL history to win three or more games without scoring a touchdown. The others were the 1922 Chicago Cardinals, the 1923 Chicago Bears, and the 1993 Indianapolis Colts, per NBC Sports research. The all-time record, held by the 1922 Cardinals, is four. Still, there's reason to believe the Vikings could snap out of their early-season funk. After the Dolphins scored a touchdown late in the third quarter to cut Minnesota's lead to 12-10, the Vikings offense seemed to wake up. A 15-play, 60-yard drive consumed more than eight minutes of clock time and extended the lead to 15-10. Then, after a three-and-out effort from the Dolphins, the Vikings burned the remaining 5:41 by moving the ball 79 yards from their own 19 to the Miami two. The next test comes today, in New Orleans. The 1-3 Saints are desperate for a win after losing their first two home games of the season — capped by Monday night's embarrassing loss to the Falcons. New Orleans hasn't lost its first three games at home since 1995.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars take 7-0 lead on 51-yard touchdown catch-and-run by Parker Washington
summary: Washington's big play put the Jaguars on the board first in London.
full_text: Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington had the first big play in London today. At least, the first big play that wasn't called back by a penalty . Washington caught a short pass from Trevor Lawrence and raced through the Eagles' secondary for a 51-yard touchdown to give Jacksonville a 7-0 lead. On the play just before that one, Jaguars wide receiver Travis Hunter caught a nine-yard pass on second-and-7, a rare offensive contribution for the two-way player who has played mostly defense this season. The Jaguars' drive started when the Eagles were stopped on fourth-and-1, on a surprising play call when they had Jalen Hurts in the shotgun and handing off to running back Will Shipley, rather than taking it himself on the tush push. Now the Eagles' much-maligned offense needs to get something going.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Eagles' Jeremiah Trotter, Jaguars' Bryan Thomas ejected on opening kickoff
summary: A crazy start in London saw a kickoff return touchdown called back on a holding penalty.
full_text: ''' Today's game in London had the craziest beginning of any NFL game this season. The opening kickoff was returned for a touchdown by Jacksonville's Josh Cameron, but it was called back by a holding penalty. But that wasn't even the crazy part. During the chaos as the officials started to call everyone back to re-do the kickoff, Philadelphia's Jeremiah Trotter and Jacksonville's Bryan Thomas fought in the middle of the field, and both were ejected, before an official play had even been run. It's a loud and mostly pro-Eagles crowd in London, and fans who got to their seats late missed something wild.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: Some doctors believe Jayden Daniels risks another elbow dislocation
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returns on Sunday, three weeks after suffering a second dislocation of his left elbow in the past 11 months.
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels returns on Sunday, three weeks after suffering a second dislocation of his left elbow in the past 11 months. The move comes with a calculated risk. Via Adam Schefter of ESPN, "[t]here are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if " Daniels suffers a third dislocation of the elbow. Although none of the doctors who expressed that concern have actually examined Daniels (which, in most cases, means that they should politely shut the hell up), it's fairly obvious that the thing that has happened to Daniels twice could happen again. In both instances, he extended his left arm while falling. On impact with the ground, the elbow went out of joint. So, yes, there's something in the elbow that makes it susceptible to dislocation when he uses the arm to brace himself. Daniels will wear a brace on his non-throwing elbow. Whether it matters won't be known until the next time he falls and tries to brace himself with his left arm. The problem for Daniels, and the Commanders, is that surgery likely would be the only way to fix the problem. With Daniels eligible for a second contract after the 2026 season, he needs to play as many games as possible (and play well) to unlock a significant deal. The coaching staff also has plenty of reasons to let him risk it, especially with Marcus Mariota injured. Dan Quinn has been around long enough to know that, if 2026 goes the way 2025 did, he won't be around in 2027.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jonathan Greenard is inactive for the Eagles
summary: The Eagles ruled out a slew of players ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London, so there wasn't much mystery to their inactive list ahead of kickoff.

title: Eagles will keep Lane Johnson on the roster until June 2, for cap purposes
summary: What's the best way for the Eagles to avoid a salary-cap mess in 2027 due to the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson?
full_text: What's the best way for the Eagles to avoid a salary-cap mess in 2027 due to the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson? Behave as if he didn't retire, of course. We floated that idea both on PFT Live and in this item after Johnson unexpectedly retired from football this week. Placement of Johnson on the reserve/retired list would result in the Eagles taking the full acceleration of all past payments (signing bonus and option bonus). Keeping him on the roster avoids that outcome until 2028. And so, via Ian Rapoport of ESPNFL, the Eagles will keep Johnson on the roster until June 2. It's a little surprising that they're not coming up with a way to shift him to the non-football injury/illness list. That would invite inevitable gripes from other teams, who would accuse the Eagles of doing exactly what they're doing — avoiding the 2027 cap mess while also clearing out the roster spot. And so they'll willingly reduce their roster limit to 52 for the balance of the season in order to preserve the ability to delay the bulk of the cap hit until 2028. The most immediate impact of that decision happened in the quarterback room. They trimmed the depth chart from three to two by cutting veteran backup Andy Dalton, who was No. 2 until he threw an interception in the red zone while starter Jalen Hurts was getting a concussion evaluation in the Week 3 Monday night loss at Chicago. Keeping Johnson on the roster means that they won't be able to declare that Johnson has committed a forfeitable breach and recover some of his signing-bonus money. Rapoport notes that, as to the $21.7 million option bonus Johnson earned earlier this year, Johnson will "pay back several million dollars -- with the exact number to be determined." As we explained earlier this week, the option bonus was split into two payments: $10.85 million paid within 15 days of the exercise of the option bonus and $10.85 million paid on or before December 1, 2026. Johnson will likely give up some, or perhaps even all, of the unpaid amount. Given that the $21.7 million had been part of his 2026 salary with the option bonus used as a way to layer the cap consequences, it was advance pay for a full season of service. By choosing to retire with 14 weeks left in the season, it's more than reasonable for Johnson to give up half of the advance payment. Could the Eagles have played hardball with Johnson, putting him on the reserve/retired list and seeking repayment of millions in signing bonus and option bonus? Yes. Beyond the fact that bullying one of the franchise's all-time greats into giving back so much money (then again, that didn't stop the Lions when Barry Sanders retired — or when Calvin Johnson retired), it would have sparked a full acceleration of all remaining payments previously made (minus whatever they recover) in 2027. That's the biggest flaw in the much-ballyhooed " financial hack " of using a stream of option bonuses in big-money veteran contracts to manage the cap. An unexpected retirement can handcuff the front office, to the point at which (as it's doing with Johnson) the team behaves as if the retirement didn't happen until the right moment arrives to officially process the move.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jeremiah Smith is the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft
summary: The Ohio State wide receiver has moved ahead of Arch Manning and is now favored to go first overall.
full_text: No wide receiver has been the first overall pick in the NFL draft since Keyshawn Johnson in 1996. Jeremiah Smith may do it in 2027. Smith, the Ohio State wide receiver, is now the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft, with +300 odds. On Saturday, Smith put up another good performance, catching four passes for 93 yards and two touchdowns in a win over Maryland. Texas quarterback Arch Manning, who had been the betting favorite to go first overall, had a rough game in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma. Manning is now second in the betting odds to go first overall in 2027, at +350. Next in the odds is Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr at +380. Carr completed 14 of 20 passes for 181 yards, with three touchdowns and no interceptions, plus 41 rushing yards, in Saturday's 58-7 win over Stanford. Following Carr in the betting odds are Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss at +600, Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker at +650, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah at +750 and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore at +1200.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Kirk Cousins is having a rare debut run with the Raiders
summary: Now with his fourth NFL team, quarterback Kirk Cousins has made a significant initial impact in Las Vegas.
full_text: Now with his fourth NFL team, quarterback Kirk Cousins has made a significant initial impact in Las Vegas. His 11 touchdown passes in four games ties Cousins with 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy for the NFL lead. If Cousins gets three more on Sunday for the Raiders against the Patriots, he would join a club that currently consists of only two quarterbacks. Via NBC Sports research, Patrick Mahomes, with the Chiefs, and Kurt Warner, with the Rams, are the only quarterbacks to throw 14 or more touchdown passes in their first five games with a given franchise. Both won the MVP award in the year they accomplished that feat. If Cousins can keep it going, he'll eventually force his way into the MVP conversation. Which could result in a 38-year-old quarterback winning his first MVP award, one year after a 37-year-old quarterback (Matthew Stafford) won his first MVP award. There's still a long way to go. Winning in New England on Sunday, a week after the Raiders' first loss of the season, would definitely help Cousins's cause.
author: Mike Florio

title: Matt LaFleur takes 12-3 record vs. Bears into Sunday's showdown
summary: Bears coach Ben Johnson has made it clear that he doesn't like the Packers.
full_text: Bears coach Ben Johnson has made it clear that he doesn't like the Packers. Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur has given the Bears plenty of reasons not to like the Packers. Since arriving as head coach of the Packers in 2019, LaFleur has a 12-3 record against the Bears, including the postseason. His 80 percent win rate is the highest that any coach has ever generated against the Bears, with a minimum of 10 games played. Johnson, of course, has won the last two — late in the 2025 regular season and then in the wild-card round. The Bears haven't beaten the Packers three times in a row since 2005-06. They're favored to win at Lambeau Field for the first time in 20 years . Chicago's defense has become a real strength. The Bears have gone three straight games allowing 12 or fewer points. The last team to do that for four games in a row was the 2017 Eagles, who'd go on to win the Super Bowl that year.
author: Mike Florio

title: Trevor Lawrence continues to perform among the NFL's elite quarterbacks
summary: The hiring of Liam Coen as head coach of the Jaguars has been very good for quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
full_text: The hiring of Liam Coen as head coach of the Jaguars has been very good for quarterback Trevor Lawrence. After Coen arrived, Lawrence became one of the elite quarterbacks in the NFL. Case in point: Lawrence has produced more touchdowns since the start of the 2025 season than all NFL quarterbacks except two: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and Bills quarterback Josh Allen. Via NBC Sports research, Lawrence has 49 total touchdowns (40 passing, nine rushing). Stafford and Allen have 58 each. The Jaguars have also won 11 of their last 13 games. That gives them the best record in the AFC over that span. And, on Sunday morning, they'll play their 15th game in London — three times more than any other NFL team. Their record in London is 7-7. And they'll play their next two there, against the Eagles in Week 5 and the Texans in Week 6.
author: Mike Florio

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. wasn't present for Cardinals team meetings on Saturday night
summary: It's not clear where receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be playing as of next week.
full_text: ' It's not clear where receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will be playing as of next week. It's becoming more and more clear he won't be playing for the Cardinals. Via Josh Weinfuss of ESPN, Harrison was not present for team meetings on Saturday night. Harrison reportedly has been told he won't be active for Sunday's game against the Lions, as a trade is finalized. Some in league circles believe he'll be traded to the Texans. Some think the Raiders could be lurking. Sunday's games could shake things up, based on injuries that could happen in the various games. Regardless, it's hard to imagine Harrison staying with the Cardinals given these developments. At this point, it's just a matter of the Cardinals getting the best return they can for the fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams aren't likely to return Myles Garrett to practice this week
summary: The update that Rams coach Sean McVay promised on Monday to deliver on Thursday regarding defensive end Myles Garrett arrived on Saturday.
full_text: The update that Rams coach Sean McVay promised on Monday to deliver on Thursday regarding defensive end Myles Garrett arrived on Saturday. Garrett, who landed on injured reserve after Week 1 due to knee surgery, can return to practice after Week 5, the fourth game he'll miss. The Rams currently don't plan to open his practice window. “He’s making good progress, but what I will say is he's not ready to say whether we'll open that window or not," McVay told reporters on Saturday. "[T]he surgery went really well. He's making good progress as far as what that timeline looks like. It's week to week in terms of how he feels, but I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week. When I talk to Neal ElAttrache, and I think it's a great way to articulate it, there's a difference between return to play and return to performance. When you do something like this, let's put him in a good position to return to performance. Part of that will be once he gets to those benchmarks where he's hitting all the benchmarks that we want, then let's physically put him in a position to do things that are in alignment with playing football, see how the knee responds, which we expect it to respond well and then that's when you can really start talking about, ‘Okay, he's going to play for us,’ and things of that nature.” McVay also was asked whether the lack of practice time in training camp will be a factor in the decision. “I think a lot of that was because we were trying to manage a situation that we're hoping to be able to work through," McVay said. "A lot of that really stemmed from the irritation in the knee so hopefully that's gone and it’s really, how quickly can the alien get up to speed for us? But, no, I think because we got that fixed and because he's feeling so good, I think that'll be an accelerated process. Him actually doing football-related activities and drills will be very important for us to put him in a position to join the group and be the guy that we're accustomed to seeing and that he wants to be for this team as well.” Garrett apparently ignored the knee issue until he got into the game against the 49ers in Australia and realized it wasn't something he could play through. That resulted in the fairly quick decision to have the knee surgically repaired, with the goal of getting the 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year up to speed and ready to do what the Rams hope he'll be able to do. With Garrett unlikely to return to practice this week, that means he'll miss the Week 6 game against the Cardinals. After that, the Rams play the Raders, Chargers, Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals again before their Week 11 bye.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers will honor Mike Ditka with a moment of silence before Sunday's game vs. Bears
summary: The Packers will host the Bears on Sunday, two days after the passing of legendary coach Mike Ditka.
full_text: '' The Packers will host the Bears on Sunday, two days after the passing of legendary coach Mike Ditka. And the Packers will be paying their respects to their former nemesis. Via Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times , the Packers will honor Ditka with a moment of silence . “One of the fiercest competitors in NFL history, Mike helped define the intensity and tradition of the Packers-Bears rivalry, the oldest in professional football,” the Packers said in a statement. “He embodied the toughness and passion that have made the rivalry one of the most storied in all of sports. “While he was a formidable opponent, his contributions to the game and to a rivalry that has meant so much to both franchises will always be respected and remembered by the Green Bay Packers.” Ditka had a 15-5 record against the Packers during his eleven years as head coach of the Bears. The two games in his first season of 1982 were lost to a players' strike. The Bears under Ditka swept the Packers in 1985, 1986, 1987, 1988, 1990, and 1991.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL fines Quinn Meinerz for posting notice of drug test after flattening Aaron Donald
summary: During the Week 3 win over the Rams, Broncos offensive lineman Quinn Meinerz manhandled L.A. defensive tackle Aaron Donald.
full_text: ' During the Week 3 win over the Rams, Broncos offensive lineman Quinn Meinerz manhandled L.A. defensive tackle Aaron Donald . Meinerz promptly received a notice of a drug test — and he posted it on social media . To no surprise, the NFL has responded by disciplining Meinerz. Via Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post, Meinerz was fined $15,000 for posting the notice of the PED test. Gabriel adds that Meinerz is appealing the punishment. The current policy is as clear as it can be: "[A]ny recording or photography of any stage of the collection process via any media (audio or visual), including but not limited to screen shots of testing notifications, video of the collectors or the collection of a specimen, and sharing such information via any social media is not permitted. A player found in violation of the rule prohibiting unauthorized recording of the collection process and sharing such information on social media will be subject to a fine of $15,000." That's what Meinerz did. The negotiated terms of the PED policy prohibit it. The situation is as open and shut as it can be.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sunday's games could become a significant factor in the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade
summary: One injury could alter everything, as to Harrison's eventual destination.
full_text: ' The #insiders told us on Saturday morning that Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. will soon be traded. They didn't however, share the destination. With Harrison reportedly due to be inactive on Sunday versus the Lions as the trade details are finalized, Sunday's full slate of games could potentially reshuffle the deck. Many believe the Texans are the team that will be trading for Harrison, a move that would reunite him with former Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud. But what if the Texans lose to the Titans? Could Houston decide at that point to not devote future assets to a season that could be a lost cause? Likewise, if Stroud is injured on Sunday, the whole "Buckeye reunion" vibe would be significantly diminished. Then there's the possibility that a contender will lose a starting receiver due to injury during Sunday's games. Suddenly, a team that wasn't in the mix for Harrison could revisit its position, quickly. Nothing is ever done until it's done. Sunday's games could change the entire dynamic for a Harrison trade. For now, the league-wide speculation points to the Texans as the destination for Harrison. Some, however, think the Raiders could be lurking. Either way, Sunday's action could become a factor in the eventual transaction, with the only surprise at this point being Harrison not being traded.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Franklin-Myers was fined only $12,537 for kneeing Derrick Henry in the stomach
summary: The weekly list of NFL-imposed fines for Week 4 includes Titans defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers.
full_text: '' The weekly list of NFL-imposed fines for Week 4 includes Titans defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers. On the surface, the $12,537 fine for "striking/kicking/kneeing" seems as perfunctory as any such fine ever does. The video paints a different picture. It happened in the second quarter of Sunday's game between the Titans and the Ravens, on a play that resulted in a three-yard touchdown pass from Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson to tight end Mark Andrews. Although the game broadcast didn't capture it, the film reveals the full incident. Ravens running back Derrick Henry cut-blocked Franklin-Myers. After the ball was caught in the end zone, and while Henry was on all fours and not looking, Franklin-Myers took a step back and then jammed his knee into Henry's midsection. The officials presumably didn't see it, because no penalty flag was thrown. It was the kind of gratuitous move that could have resulted in an ejection. It's somewhat surprising it didn't lead to a suspension. The end result doesn't come close to matching the infraction. It's less than the league fined Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Browns running back Quinshon Judkins for a celebration that mimed smoking a joint. And it was nearly half the amount of a fine that was imposed earlier this season, we're told, on Ravens receiver LaJohntay Wester for — God forbid — displaying an unauthorized logo on his gloves. Those fines aren't part of the weekly announcement from the league. Wester was fined $23,882 after the Ravens' Week 1 game against the Colts for the foreign logo on his gloves. While the fine schedule is negotiated between the NFL and the NFL Players Association, something is off if a player can deliberately ram a knee into the midsection of an unsuspecting opponent and be fined only $12,537, but having an unauthorized logo on the official gloves costs $23,882.
author: Mike Florio

title: As Bears intend to build a dome, Mike Ditka would not approve
summary: The passing of larger-than-life NFL legend Mike Ditka has sparked a flood of great stories and clips from Ditka's time in football.
full_text: '' The passing of larger-than-life NFL legend Mike Ditka has sparked a flood of great stories and clips from Ditka's time in football. Many of them stand out. There's one that's particularly relevant to the Bears' ongoing quest to vacate Soldier Field for a venue with a roof. In December 1987, as the Bears prepared for their annual trip to the Metrodome in Minneapolis, Ditka went off on football not played in the elements. " I just don’t like indoor domes ," Ditka said. "They weren't meant for football. Football is meant to play it outside and on grass. . . . Indoor domes should be useful for roller rinks. That's all they should be for. Roller skating." That same week, Ditka skated through the Bears' offices in rollerblades. "They were a gift," Ditka said. "[Vikings G.M.] Mike Lynn sprung for them. That might refute everything I've heard about him from his players." The Bears won the " Rollerdome " game, 30-24, on a late touchdown pass from Mike Tomczak to Dennis Gentry. "I did what I did about the dome for certain reasons," Ditka said after the victory. "To get the pressure off the players and get it on me. And I think for that point, it worked." Ditka then made a point that hopefully will resonate with today's coaches. "If people don't like the things I do, that's just a point of life," Ditka said. "There's gotta be some levity in life, and there's gotta be a little bit of fun had. And we take this whole thing seriously, like it's life and death. It's not life and death. We're gonna go out and play as hard as we can. We're gonna be great representatives of the city of Chicago, the Chicago Bear organization. That's all we're trying to do is be something that people can be proud of. But, you know, if I'm not gonna have any fun on my way there, partner, I just — they got the wrong guy, because, you know, I said a long time ago, maybe the NFL is a little bit too staid and true in its ways. Maybe it takes somebody to loosen them up a little bit. And our players do that, so why shouldn't the coach be a little wacky?" Current Bears coach Ben Johnson seems to already be living that message. With the first game after Ditka's passing coming against the Packers at Lambeau Field, maybe Johnson will take it up a notch. Back to Ditka's point. Football really is meant to be played outside and on grass. Unfortunately, the indoor ship seems to have sailed. The Commanders, Browns, Titans, and Chiefs are currently moving toward swapping the elements for a roller rink. And the Bears inevitably will join them, whether that's in Chicago, Arlington Heights, or Hammond, Indiana. Whoever the coach of the Vikings is at the time should show up for the first game to be played there on roller skates, as the ultimate homage to Ditka.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Cardinals will be trading receiver Marvin Harrison Jr.
summary: The team hasn't been named; the thinking is it's the Texans.
full_text: ' Another 2024 top-10 draft pick is about to be on the move. According to ESPNFL, the Cardinals will be trading receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. Harrison, per the report, will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions, as the details are finalized. The current chatter in league circles is that Harrison will land in Houston, where he'd be reunited with former Ohio State quarterback C.J. Stroud. The Cardinals, we're told, had been looking for a package that includes a second-round pick. Whether they get that remains to be seen. And it's definitely unusual for the news of a trade to emerge without a destination. It could be an eleventh-hour attempt to get other teams to the table, in the hopes of driving up the price. When the trade happens, Harrison will join former Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who was taken tenth overall in 2024, as players traded fairly quickly by the teams that took them. Harrison has become largely forgotten in the Arizona offense under new coach Mike LaFleur. In four games this season, he has five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown.

title: Arch Manning's two fourth-quarter interceptions doom Texas in loss to Oklahoma
summary: Texas is No. 1 no more, after a two-interception fourth quarter from quarterback Arch Manning handed Oklahoma a come-from-behind victory in the Red River Rivalry.
full_text: ' Texas is No. 1 no more, after a two-interception fourth quarter from quarterback Arch Manning handed Oklahoma a come-from-behind victory in the Red River Rivalry. The Longhorns led 17-7 at halftime, but the second half was a disaster for Manning and Texas, and Oklahoma won 27-24 with a field goal as time expired. Texas entered the game 4-0 and the top-ranked team in the country; Oklahoma entered 2-2 and unranked. Texas punted on all three of its third-quarter possessions, and in the fourth quarter, Manning threw two interceptions. The first was a pick-six that gave Oklahoma its first lead of the game, and the second set up Oklahoma's game-winning field goal. Manning's numbers -- 19 of 31 for 260 yards, with three touchdowns and two interceptions, plus 20 rushing yards -- don't look terrible. But his fourth quarter performance is what will be remembered from this game. Manning is the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the NFL draft, just like his uncles Peyton and Eli were. He didn't look like a first overall pick today.

title: Bears to honor Mike Ditka by wearing special helmet decal in Week 5 against Packers
summary: Ditka, who played six years in Chicago before leading the Bears to a Super Bowl as a coach, passed away last week.
full_text:
Mike Ditka is one of the most legendary figures in Chicago Bears history, and the team is planning to honor him on Sunday.
For their Week 5 game in Green Bay, the Bears will be wearing a special helmet decal that will feature Ditka's 89, which was the number he wore during his six-year career as a player in Chicago.
The Bears unveiled the decal on Sunday morning.
For 89 💙 pic.twitter.com/0pynPgHoBb
Ditka died Friday at the age of 86 .
Ditka is an icon in Chicago, and his ties with the franchise go back 65 years. In 1961, the Bears made him the fifth overall pick in the NFL Draft . During his rookie season, he became the first tight end in NFL history to go over 1,000 yards receiving. He ended up spending a total of 12 seasons in the NFL, with six of those coming in Chicago. He also played for the Eagles (1967-68) and Cowboys (1969-72).
After his playing career ended, Ditka returned to Chicago when the Bears hired him as head coach in 1982. Three years later, he led the Bears to their first, and currently only, Super Bowl win in franchise history. Ditka ended up coaching the Bears for 11 seasons (1982-1992), and he was voted the NFL's coach of the year twice (1985, 1988) during that span.
Ditka is such an NFL legend that the Packers will also be honoring the Pro Football Hall of Famer on Sunday. According to the Chicago Sun-Times , the team is planning a moment of silence before the game.
"One of the fiercest competitors in NFL history, Mike helped define the intensity and tradition of the Packers-Bears rivalry, the oldest in professional football," the Packers said in a statement. "He embodied the toughness and passion that have made the rivalry one of the most storied in all of sports. While he was a formidable opponent, his contributions to the game and to a rivalry that has meant so much to both franchises will always be respected and remembered by the Green Bay Packers."
The Bears and Packers will be kicking off at 1 p.m. ET from Lambeau Field.

title: NFL Week 5 upset alert: Why these five favorites could easily lose, including the Patriots
summary: After accurately identifying three major upsets last week, we examine five more for Week 5
full_text:
No favorite appears to be safe these days in the NFL , as underdogs have come on strong over the first month of the regular season.
In the past two weeks, a total of 23 games have been decided by one score, which is tied for the most in a two-week span in NFL history. Naturally, those coin-flip games have produced quite a bit of upsets, and we've largely been on the scent with them. In last week's upset alert, we accurately identified the Texans , Lions , and Saints as favorites ripe to fall short, with the Cowboys , Panthers , and Falcons each pulling off upsets.
Now, we turn our focus to Week 5, where there are several home underdogs, which always put our antenna up. Three of which you can find below, as they could stun the road favorites this weekend, along with two AFC East favorites possibly on shaky ground at home.
All NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
New England is coming off its biggest win of the season after going up to Buffalo and upsetting the Bills to get to 2-2 on the year. After it felt like the sky was falling in Foxborough, that win -- at least for the moment -- stabilized things. That said, this does feel like a possible letdown spot for the Patriots after such a monumental victory. They host a Raiders team that saw its undefeated 3-0 start get snapped by the Kansas City Chiefs last week, but Las Vegas largely hung in there. The defeat didn't expose them as fool's gold. Rather, I expect them to go into Gillette Stadium and make the Patriots sweat.
Vegas ranks sixth in the NFL in pressure rate (42.5%) and fifth in sack rate (8.7%). Drake Maye was much improved against Buffalo's pressure last week, but he's still struggled overall when under duress and has had a propensity to turn the ball over. If that rears its head here, Kirk Cousins -- who is tied for the league lead in passing touchdowns (11) -- should be able to take advantage.
I don't think it's hyperbole to call this a make-or-break game for Green Bay. A loss at home to Chicago would drop them to 2-3 on the season and, more importantly for tiebreaker situations, 0-2 in the NFC North. That's the makings of a hole that'll soon be too big to claw out of, no matter if Micah Parsons and/or Josh Jacobs return. So, with that in mind, I think the Packers -- who are admittedly flawed -- could throw the kitchen sink at a Bears team that is still dinged up.
On top of Caleb Williams (hamstring) still being out and Tyson Bagent set to start at quarterback, Kyle Monangi (thumb) and D'Andre Swift (knee, hip) did not practice on Wednesday. They both could play in Week 5, but if they are limited in any way, that takes away/deminishes the identity of what this offense has been. Coming into Week 5, the Bears lead the NFL with 196.3 rushing yards per game.
It's also worth noting that the Ben Johnson-led Bears have struggled against the NFC North. Against the division, Chicago is 2-5, while they are 12-2 against everyone else.
What if the Browns are just good? Cleveland is coming off a marquee win over the Steelers in Week 4, and will have the rest advantage over the Jets after playing last Thursday. After a season opener where it looked like the Browns were going to sink to the bottom of the league, they've ripped off three straight, and Deshaun Watson has looked solid. In fact, he's been clutch. Over this winning streak, he's orchestrated three game-winning drives and has completed 15-of-20 passes, averaged 6.9 yards per attempt, and has two passing touchdowns with no interceptions in those drives.
Watson and the Browns now face a Jets team that has gone in the opposite direction from them. After winning its first game of the year, New York has lost three straight. As it relates to this matchup, it's the Jets defense that should be of central focus and possibly the reason for an upset. Sure, they got an interception last week, but the unit has struggled in the two games prior to Week 5. The Jets' defense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game allowed at 436.5. Watson also won't have to deal with a ton of pressure as New York ranks 28th in the NFL in pressure rate this season.
New York is 0-12 in its last 12 games against above-.500 teams.
The Saints were embarrassed on Monday night in a 45-24 loss to their division rival, the Atlanta Falcons, at home in primetime. Typically, a team playing on a short week might be at a disadvantage, but I'd guess New Orleans is foaming at the mouth to get back out there to get rid of the sour taste of that defeat.
Minnesota is 4-0 on the year, but that undefeated record has come despite some questionable play on offense. They've registered the third-fewest yards per game (262.8) during a 4-0 start to a season by any team since 1940. Meanwhile, Kyler Murray hasn't looked like the second coming of Sam Darnold by any stretch of the imagination to this point. Of the 28 quarterbacks who've thrown at least 70 pass attempts this year, Murray is 24th in passer rating, 25th in yards per attempt, and 27th in EPA per dropback.
Really, it's been the play of the Vikings defense that has spearheaded this undefeated start. Brian Flores' unit has allowed the fewest points per game (12.8) in the NFL this season and has by far the highest blitz rate (71%) in the league. Against the blitz this season, Saints quarterback Tyler Shough has a 105.8 passer rating (11th among QBs) and five passing touchdowns (tied for third-most in the NFL), so he has been solid in the face of added pressure.
If he can find some success against this Vikings blitz, that could be enough to pull out the win, especially if the Murray-led offense continues to struggle to get off the ground.
The Detroit Lions simply cannot be trusted as a road favorite with their current defense. They just let Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers torch them for 32 points and 329 passing yards, despite it largely just being a two-man show between Young and wideout Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches, 192 yards, and two touchdowns). Detroit's secondary is giving up a league-worst 423.8 total yards per game, and their 31.8 points per game allowed is the second-worst in the NFL.
While the Cardinals won't be mistaken for a Super Bowl contender, they have enough playmakers on offense to take advantage of the Lions' poor defense. Jacoby Brissett is coming off his worst statistical game of the season, tossing three interceptions against the Giants , but he is capable of bouncing back and throwing it around the yard, especially with the likes of Trey McBride and Michael Wilson at his disposal.

title: Eagles and Jaguars wild start in London: Two players ejected, 90-yard TD nullified after penalties
summary: A 90-yard touchdown return by Josh Cameron was wiped out at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as Bryan Thomas Jr. and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. were both disqualified after a wild sequence
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars couldn't get through the opening kickoff on Sunday without some controversy. On the first play of this international game, we saw a touchdown nullified by four penalties -- which included two ejections.
Jaguars rookie Josh Cameron fielded the opening kickoff at his own 10-yard line, and then ran it 90 yards back for the first touchdown of the game! So we thought.
There was some yellow laundry on the field that was going to take away Jacksonville's big play.
Josh Cameron Takes It To The House To Start The Kickoff, OMG. That’s A Statement. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PhXI3oACqv
There was so much for the officiating crew to sort through on this one play that it took several minutes before head umpire Ron Torbert felt comfortable enough to turn on his mic and address all of those assembled in Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to explain what happened.
Eventually, the Eagles were penalized for illegal formation on the kickoff, while the Jaguars were called for holding on the return. Then, Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr . and Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr . were both called for unsportsmanlike conduct after a brief scuffle, and both players were ejected from Sunday's contest.
Brian Thomas Jr. And Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Have Been Ejected After This Incident, On The First Kickoff Of The Game. That’s A Crazy Start. 😬 pic.twitter.com/SCUcHL0lXR
What's a bit humorous is that this was not even the fastest ejection in the Trotter family. Back in 2005, Trotter's father, Jeremiah Trotter, was ejected before the season opener could even get underway. He and Atlanta Falcons cornerback Kevin Mathis got in a fight during pregame warmups and were both ejected.
The confusing and penalty-filled start to the game was an accurate depiction for our London friends how this NFL season has gone over in the states. Just last week, there were  271 total penalties called. That's the second-most penalties ever in a single week dating back to 1950. There were 963 penalties in the first 4 weeks of this season.

title: Cardinals finalizing Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, former No. 4 pick inactive vs. Lions
summary: The former No. 4 overall pick is inactive against the Lions after Arizona reportedly informed him of its decision
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , informing the former first-round pick of their decision ahead of Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions , per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The Cardinals informed the former first-round pick on Saturday morning of their decision to trade him.
Arizona desires a second-round pick or better in exchange for the former Ohio State star, according to Tom Pelissero .
Details of the trade are reportedly still being finalized, but Harrison is inactive for Sunday's game. The subject of recent trade speculation, Harrison has drawn interest from the Indianapolis Colts , among others, who are looking for a weapon in the passing game. However, longtime Colts reporter Mike Chappell reported Saturday that the Colts are not in the Harrison sweepstakes after initially doing their due diligence.
The Houston Texans are among the teams who have been in contact with Arizona about Harrison Jr., per Zenitz.
General manager Monti Ossenfort publicly maintained that Harrison remains part of the franchise's plans, but that appears moot after Sunday's reported deal. Harrison hasn't given the Cardinals reasons to feature him this season, with drops and productivity concerns.
A fresh start might eventually benefit everyone involved.
The ex-Ohio State standout who entered the NFL in 2024 as the franchise's fourth-overall pick hasn't been as impactful as expected, given his meteoric rise ahead of that offseason's draft.
Harrison registered 608 yards in 12 games last season, and through four games in 2026, only five catches for 85 yards. Over 16 starts as a rookie, Harrison recorded 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns before his production dwindled during his second campaign, part of that due to a concussion suffered last season.
A change of scenery could benefit Harrison, a 24-year-old talent whose size and body control impact the game when consistently targeted. His appeal is obvious — an athlete with his catch radius is covered in short-yardage situations and goal-to-go opportunities.
While he hasn't been the field-stretcher most assumed he would be early at the next level, perhaps Harrison's new team unlocks a certain level of comfort in a different scheme.
Cardinals first-year offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett seemed uninterested in moving Harrison around and manufacturing touches for a player the franchise was paying $35.3 million to during his four-year rookie deal. The plan was for Harrison to be Arizona's new No. 1 when drafted, but that never panned out, and his new landing spot won't have to tag him with that high an expectation level.
The bet is straightforward for the team that signs Harrison — get the most of his proven ability by providing a stable scheme around him that gets him more involved with the offense.
A player who was a two-time All-American with the Buckeyes and earned Biletnikoff honors as a junior in 2023 as the Big Ten's Offensive Player of the Year hasn't forgotten how to play football. Instead, he was never the right fit for a franchise that refused to mold its offense around his abilities.
Amid slow start to the season, Harrison addressed some of the vitriol he's seen out there during his third campaign.
"It's a social media era, you see everything," Harrison told reporters last month before the Cardinals' loss to the 49ers. "I'm not going to sit here and say I don't see nothing. You get told to block out the noise and not pay attention to it. That's part of it, you can still see something and still block it out. I see everything, and everybody's entitled to their own opinions. You get platforms to speak your mind and that's okay for me. I'm just gonna continue to worry about my team and my process and helping the team win best I can."
Harrison, who only caught one pass for 12 yards in last week's loss to the Giants isn't focused on what's going wrong thus far.
"Stick to my process," Harrison said. "Don't change anything I've been doing. Continue to work hard day in and day out. That's the best you can do in this situation."

title: Where is Marvin Harrison Jr. headed? Inside the mystery surrounding Cardinals' unfinished trade
summary: Houston is a team to watch as questions remain about Marvin Harrison Jr.'s destination and what Arizona will get in return
full_text:
Early Saturday morning, somewhere pre-7 a.m. local time, the Arizona Cardinals decided they had enough of a trade offer on the table for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . that they felt comfortable offloading the 2024 No. 4 overall draft pick.
The news of an expected trade of Harrison Jr. was then shared with the wide receiver. It then circulated around the building before news of the impending trade broke open in the media.
Twenty-four hours later, the destination (or likely destination) for Harrison Jr. remains a mystery to everybody outside of such figures as general manager Monti Ossenfort and head coach Mike LaFleur. All that's been shared internally, including among players, is that the Cardinals are trading Harrison, that his time in Arizona is done and that he'll be inactive for the Cardinals' game against the Lions on Sunday.
Some internally, including teammates, think the Texans are a clear top possibility (and CBS Sports can confirm that Houston has been among the teams in contact about Harrison, who was college teammates at Ohio State with Texans QB C.J. Stroud ) but sources don't believe that any trade has been officially finalized yet as of Sunday morning.
Even with Houston, league sources outside of Arizona have wondered if anything could change if the Texans fall to 0-5 Sunday when they face the Titans, if other teams are quietly involved and also if another team could ultimately jump in depending on the outcome of the Week 5 games.
What's clear is that the Cardinals, despite Harrison having just five catches through four games, have been hoping for as much as a first-round draft pick if they were trading Harrison and it seemed like the inclusion of a first-round pick would ultimately trigger Arizona to move on from him. Even though it's fair to question whether another team would actually be willing to give up that level of compensation, multiple sources did indicate being under the impression -- without knowing the exact compensation -- that the Cardinals seem poised to receive a strong return for Harrison, who's 24 years old and only two years removed from posting 885 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie in 2024.
The thought for now among several NFL sources is that Arizona clearly has an offer from at least one team (maybe Houston, maybe someone else) that's good enough and locked in to the point that they were comfortable informing Harrison on Saturday morning that he'll be traded in the coming days.
Now, it's just a matter of who that new team for Harrison ends up being.

title: It wouldn't shock me IF ... NFL Week 5: Nick Sirianni's seat heats up, Sean Payton takes back playcalling
summary: Could the 49ers plant their flag as the Super Bowl favorites? Will Jacoby Brissett be the latest QB to light up the Lions?
full_text:
When you step outside in the morning, you'll notice that chill in the air. It's a reminder that the fall months have arrived, and that typically means the action across the NFL is ramping up. Now that the first month is in the rearview mirror, teams are rounding into form, and we should start to see some significant separation between the contenders and pretenders over these next few weeks.
This is also the time when we begin to see if some early-season struggles or even hot starts are legit or mere flashes in the pan. For the former, that could create some awkward situations, particularly as we continue to gauge the temperature of the head coach's hot seat or coordinator duties.
Both of those could be at the forefront of the headlines by the time we wrap up Week 5 in the NFL, which we discuss in depth below, along with other storylines that could sprout out of the upcoming slate.
The Philadelphia Eagles might be on the verge of blowing it up. The club is off to a teetering 2-2 start to the regular season, has been dealt with an onslaught of injuries, and saw Lane Johnson retire this week. That said, the biggest indicator that something may be afoot is that they just shipped away starting interior lineman Cam Jurgens to the Ravens . For a team still trying to be in the Super Bowl conversation, it's a bit striking to see them trade someone of Jurgens' caliber, even if there are solid reasons for Howie Roseman to make such a move .
And that brings us to this weekend, when Philadelphia will be in London taking on the Jacksonville Jaguars . In my eyes, this has the makings of a Jags blowout win . Jacksonville is essentially the polar opposite of the Eagles right now offensively. They have the third-best third-down conversion rate (51.1%) in the NFL entering Week 5, the second-best red zone touchdown rate (81.8%), and Trevor Lawrence has the second-highest passer rating in the NFL (min. 100 pass attempts). If they keep that up, the Eagles offense, which hasn't converted a third down in its last 17 attempts, could be lapped.
Philadelphia would fall under .500, and Nick Sirianni would be 5-8 since Week 12 of last season (including playoffs). The head coach's seat would be as hot as it's arguably ever been, and this Eagles ownership hasn't been shy about making bold decisions if they believe it's in the best interest of the team.
The Chargers are in dire straits right now, as they enter Week 5 at 0-4 and have been lifeless on the offensive side of the ball. Justin Herbert has thrown more interceptions (6) than touchdowns (4) and has been the second-most pressured quarterback (46.5%) in the NFL. Herbert's 12 sacks taken are also tied for the second-most in the league.
With injuries to the offensive line, this sets the stage for him to be under siege more than he's been all year. L.A. already knows it'll be without starting left tackle Rashawn Slater , who will miss time due to a high ankle sprain. On top of Slater, starting right tackle Joe Alt is also not expected to play on Sunday due to a neck injury. Alt was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's opening injury report. Even with those two, the Chargers' offensive line was surrendering loads of pressure onto Herbert, and that's only going to get worse with them out of the picture and the Chargers squaring off against the Broncos .
Denver's pass rush isn't as prolific as it was last season, but it is still 11th in the NFL in pressure rate (38.9%). Over the last two seasons combined, it has piled up the most sacks (76) in the NFL.
Through four weeks, the most Herbert had been sacked in a game was four, which came last week against Seattle. At SoFi Stadium on Sunday, the Chargers QB will endure a new season high in sacks with the Broncos tagging him at least five times, just as they did the last time they faced him in Week 3 of last season.
The Lions defense is unquestionably the worst in the NFL right now. Their secondary is coming off a Week 4 showing where they were demolished by Bryce Young , who threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns. Detroit is giving up the second-most points per game in the NFL (31.8) and the most total yards (423.8) per game this season. The Lions' 1,216 total passing yards allowed are also the most in the league, while their 110.4 passer rating allowed is the fourth-highest. No matter which way you slice it, it's putrid.
That should be music to Jacoby Brissett's ears as he's eager to rebound from a three-interception performance against the Giants last week. Judging by the opponent he's facing, he's primed to throw it all over the yard.
So far this season, Brissett's high in passing yards is 280, which came back in Week 3 against the San Francisco 49ers . However, if you go back to last season when he became the starter in Arizona, he's had several eye-popping yardage totals. Brissett went over 300 yards four times and even had a 452-yard passing game thrown in there as well. I believe we get an aerial avalanche from Brissett, which gets him to 350 passing yards on Sunday.
Arizona has the weapons for Brissett to pile up yardage, particularly Trey McBride and Michael Wilson . McBride could go berserk as the Lions are giving up the most receptions and receiving touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, and the second-most receiving yards. Meanwhile, Michael Wilson could follow in Tetairoa McMillan's shoes, who torched the Lions last Sunday to the tune of 14 catches, 192 yards and two touchdowns.
Because the Cardinals are the fourth-worst scoring defense (29.3 points per game allowed) in the NFL this season, Brissett could be forced even more into a pass-heavy game script.
Gambling nugget to note : Jacoby Brissett's O/U passing yard prop is set at 269.5 yards (-111 to the Over). Brissett is +115 to reach 280 passing yards, +145 to reach 290 passing yards, +183 to reach 300 passing yards, and +567 to reach 350 passing yards (via DraftKings Sportsbook).
The leash is getting shorter and shorter for Broncos offensive coordinator David Webb and his ability to call the plays in Denver. The Broncos are 2-2 on the season, which finds them in third place in the AFC West. Part of the reason for their .500 mark through the first month has been their sluggish starts on offense. Denver is scoring the fewest first-half points (13 total points) in the NFL this season and has only stayed afloat because their 61 total second-half points scored are the fifth-highest in the league.
So far this season, the Broncos (with Webb calling the plays) are averaging 18.5 points per game, which ranks 26th in the NFL. Last year, when Joe Lombardi was the OC and Sean Payton was calling the plays, Denver averaged 23.6 points per game, which ranked 14th.
Meanwhile, Bo Nix appears to be regressing under this new leadership. Over the first two years of his career, Nix's air yards per pass attempt were 7.3. This year, it's down to 5.4. The former first-round quarterback's yards per attempt this season (6.1), completion percentage (60%), and passer rating (80.4) are all on pace for career lows. His turnover-worthy throw rate of 3.7% is also on pace for a career-high.
Even if Denver wins on Sunday to improve to 3-2, it's on the table that Sean Payton takes back the play sheet from Webb if the offense continues to sputter, particularly entering a short week where they'll host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. Moreover, if the Broncos are upset by the Chargers and the offense is a key reason for the defeat, it'll be curtains for Webb's days as the play caller.
Despite a shaky 2-2 start to the season, the betting favorite to win Super Bowl LXI remains the Los Angeles Rams . While it's certainly a long season and there's plenty of time to go before we kick off that championship matchup at SoFi Stadium, I'm surprised L.A. has held onto being the favorite this long. With that in mind, I think we see the odds flip this weekend with a new NFC West team claiming the top spot. The San Francisco 49ers —…

title: Are Eagles tanking? Why Philadelphia's teardown looks like a full-scale rebuild
summary: The Eagles are stockpiling premium draft picks while dismantling a once-dominant offensive line
full_text:
The sky is falling in Philadelphia. That's at least how it looks after Lane Johnson's abrupt retirement and the trade of Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to Baltimore.
Two years removed from a second Super Bowl win, Eagles fans surely hoped for a sequel reminiscent of Rocky IV. Instead, it appears that Philadelphia fans will be forced to spend the rest of the Eagles' 2026 season watching the equivalent of Rocky V.
Yes, it could get that bad for Eagles fans during the season's final 13 games.
Given recent events, there can be no other conclusion than that Eagles GM Howie Roseman is beginning the process of starting over. Championship-aspiring teams don't trade Pro Bowl-level players in October in exchange for future draft picks. It's as simple as that.
If you need further evidence, look at how the Eagles have positioned themselves for the future. In 2028, the Eagles are now slated to have two first- and two second-round picks, with the second second-rounder being acquired in the Jurgens trade.
The Eagles are setting themselves up for future success, but what does that mean for the present? If you haven't figured it out yet, it's not good.
From the outside, it looks like the franchise needs a reboot inside and out. On the field, the Eagles are a shell of the team that dominated the defending two-time defending champion Chiefs in the Super Bowl two years ago, especially on offense. Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley both regressed, the offensive line is now in shambles, and the revamped receiving corps hasn't masked AJ Brown's departure.
Football aside, something else appears to be off with this team. They no longer have the edge that helped them become champions in 2024. Go back to Philadelphia's Week 3 game against Chicago, a game they were favored to win as the Bears were trotting out 38-year-old Case Keenum , who was making his first start in three years.
Midway through the second quarter, Hurts was laid out by linebacker D'Marco Jackson on a hit that was rightfully penalized for unnecessary roughness. Jackson was flagged, but the collateral damage was done.
The hit -- and the Eagles' response to it -- revealed what's inside this Philadelphia team. Typically, when a franchise quarterback gets hit like that, all hell breaks loose. Yet, in this situation, DeVonta Smith was the only teammate who appeared to be terribly bothered by what he saw.
D'Marco Jackson laid out Jalen Hurts on the sideline, and Nick Sirianni was furious about it. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman on the Bears-Eagles call for ABC/ESPN 😳 🐻 🏈 #NFL pic.twitter.com/3qjCiq3EHa
Even worse was the Eagles' on-field response. Instead of elevating their intensity, the Eagles continued to get pushed around on both sides of the ball. Philadelphia didn't punch back and instead were the recipients of body blow after body blow. Somewhere, Clubber Lang and Ivan Drago were probably smiling.
The Eagles' lack of response that night likely speaks to the team's current culture, or lack thereof. It's fair to question the team's internal leadership, starting with coach Nick Sirianni .
Like his predecessor, Doug Pederson, Sirianni has led the Eagles to the promised land. Pederson's message eventually fell on deaf ears in Philadelphia, and it's more than fair to wonder if the same is happening now with Sirianni. Leading an NFL franchise is hard enough, and it's even harder when fans are calling for your job .
The Eagles relieved Pederson of his duties three years after winning the Super Bowl. His firing came at the end of a dreadful 4-11-1 season that ended -- ironically enough -- with Pederson and the Eagles being accused of tanking . At that point, the prospect of another Eagles championship parade anytime soon seemed as likely as Rocky getting back into the ring at age 60.
As it turns out, Rocky did fight again at 60 , and the Eagles did win it all just four years after that disastrous 2020 season. Roseman's successful rebuild, then, should give Philly fans solace now as they brace themselves for what could be the start of yet another rebuild. Until then, Eagles fans may want to spend their Sundays watching either Rocky films or replays of championship seasons past.

title: Jaguars vs. Eagles prediction: Philadelphia comes into London banged up, can it upset Jacksonville?
summary: Here's how to follow Sunday's action from London
full_text:
The Jacksonville Jaguars are returning to London, their second home, to host the Philadelphia Eagles in the first game of Sunday's NFL slate.
Jacksonville (3-1) just registered statement wins over the Patriots and Bengals . The steady play of quarterback Trevor Lawrence leads the way, supplemented by a defense that has allowed the second-fewest points in the NFL so far.
Philadelphia (2-2) experienced a tumultuous week that included a second-straight loss, the sudden retirement of perennial Pro Bowl lineman Lane Johnson and the trade of fellow Pro Bowl lineman Cam Jurgens . The trade of Jurgens raised questions about the Eagles' motives during the season's final 13 games.
Philadelphia's offensive line will look vastly different. Rookie Markel Bell will replace Johnson at right tackle, and Drew Kendall -- if healthy -- will replace Jurgens at center.
A third-round pick in April's draft, Bell made his first career start during last week's loss to the Rams . Given the circumstances, Bell's overall performance was solid. He allowed six pressures and an 18.8% pressure rate per drop-back. He was better in run blocking while helping the Eagles run for 104 yards despite Saquon Barkley missing most of the game with an injury.
Kendall, a 2025 fifth-round pick, has logged four career starts, including three this season. Kendell's play was one of the reasons why the Eagles felt comfortable trading Jurgens.
Philadelphia has a whopping 12 players on this week's injury report. Among them were Kendall (knee), Barkley (hamstring), and wideouts DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Marquise Brown (ankle) and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring).
These injuries (among others) surely contributed to the Eagles being a sizable underdog in London.
The two teams are in entirely different situations entering Sunday's game. The Eagles have lost two straight and appear to be in jeopardy of waiving the white flag on the season. Philadelphia's struggles have been on both sides of the ball. They're 26th in the NFL in scoring, and their defense is a mediocre 17th in points allowed.
One of the biggest issues so far has been Jalen Hurts ' struggles, which can be attributed in part to instability on the offensive line, injuries to Barkley, a new offensive coordinator for a second straight year, and AJ Brown's absence after he was traded to New England. Makai Lemon , a rookie first-round pick, has caught just 10 passes for 65 yards.
Jacksonville shook off a Week 3 loss in Denver with a blowout win over the Patriots and a five-point win in Cincinnati. The Jaguars have been money so far on third down and in the red zone. Their offense is third in both third-down and red-zone efficiency. The defense is ranked fifth on third down and second in the red zone. Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun has been a force this season with 24 tackles, two interceptions and a forced fumble.
It's hard to fathom the Eagles falling to 2-3 given the talent on their roster. It's even harder, however, to envision them beating the Jaguars unless Jacksonville beats itself with turnovers and other poor play.
Rest assured that Eagles veteran defensive coordinator Vic Fangio will try to make life difficult for Lawrence by taking away the running game and bottling up his receivers. If Lawrence can handle the pressure, the Jaguars should fly back to the States with a 4-1 record.
Score: Jaguars 16, Eagles 13

Jacksonville is rolling behind coach Liam Coen and quarterback Trevor Lawrence , with the team going 16-5 since Coen took over before last season. Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas Jr . have combined for 270 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten has rushed for 277 yards and has seven catches for 54 yards. Jacksonville isn't piling up yards but is scoring 26 points per game (12th in NFL) while Philly averages 18.8 (26th).
The Jags are really built on defense, as they lead the NFL with six takeaways, have 10 sacks and give up just 13.3 points per game, second-fewest in the league. They are 25th in the league in yards allowed at 354.5 per game but get the job done in the red zone, with teams coming away with a TD just 28.6% of the time, also second in the league. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker have 1.5 sacks apiece, and seven others have at least half a sack. The Jaguars allowed 437 yards to Joe Burrow and the Bengals last week, but only 23 came on the ground and the Jags had two takeaways in the 22-17 victory. The Eagles don't have a passing game like that and are likely to be missing top receiver DeVonta Smith . Star running back Saquon Barkley is also questionable and unlikely to play because of a hamstring injury. Philadelphia is in dire straits with some top players out and the offense struggling. Quarterback Jalen Hurts has 246 total passing yards over the past two games as the Eagles lost 27-7 to the Bears and 24-20 to the Rams . Los Angeles outgained them 415-172 in total yards but needed 14 points in the fourth quarter to surge to the victory. Hurts threw two interceptions, the Eagles were 0-for-12 on third down and were called for 10 penalties. Now, Hurts will be without his star receiver and running back. Barkley is the top rusher with 182 yards, and Hurts is second at 105. With Barkley out and with Tank Bigsby definitely on IR after core muscle surgery, Will Shipley will be the next man up. The 2024 fourth-round pick has 51 rushing yards and averages 3.4 yards per carry. Dontayvion Wicks has 197 receiving yards and is likely to be Hurts' go-to guy along with tight end Dallas Goedert , who is returning this weekend. The Eagles have the fourth-worst offense in the league, averaging 269.8 yards per game, and average 18.8 points (26th). They are second-to-last in passing yards per game at 160.8.
Things are only slightly better on defense, as Philly is 21st in the league in allowing 344 yards and yields 23.3 points per game (16th). The Jaguars have outscored their opponents by 51 points, the second-best differential in the league, while the Eagles have given up 18 more than they've scored. Philly also has just four sacks, two by Nolan Smith Jr. and one each from tackles Jalen Carter and linebacker Jihaad Campbell , the team's top tackler with 37. Pass rusher Jonathan Greenard , who missed the first two games with a pectoral injury, also is questionable after tweaking an ankle in last week's loss. The injuries have been piling up, and many of the stricken players are key pieces. They won their first two games, though those came against the Titans and Commanders. Hurts threw for 467 yards over those two, while Smith and Goedert were the top pass-catchers. Both teams fell short of 300 yards, but the Bears had 375 and Los Angeles topped 400. title: Is the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade the nail in the coffin for Monti Ossenfort?
summary: What could have been. The Arizona Cardinals are trading Marvin Harrison Jr. to someone (the Houston Texans right now) and then you are also unaware of what they are getting (a second round pick it sounds like) and all of this will happen after the Cardinals matchup today against the Detroit Lions. For the Cardinals, […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Owner Michael J. Bidwill of the Arizona Cardinals talks with general manager Monti Ossenfort prior to the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images What could have been. The Arizona Cardinals are trading Marvin Harrison Jr. to someone (the Houston Texans right now) and then you are also unaware of what they are getting (a second round pick it sounds like) and all of this will happen after the Cardinals matchup today against the Detroit Lions. For the Cardinals, that means another of the 2024 draft class no longer on the roster. In what was supposed to be the crown jewel of Monti’s work as GM, it is now looking like one of the biggest draft class disasters in recent memory. The rundown: 1.04 – Marvin Harrison Jr. 1.27 – Darius Robinson – 25 career games 12 starts 3 career sacks 7 tackles for loss 2.43 – Max Melton 3.66 – Trey Benson 3.71 – Isaiah Adams – 19 career starts 3.82 – Tip Reimain – 21 total games played (548 total snaps) 3.90 – Elijah Jones 4.104 – Dadrion Taylor-Demerson – 30 career games played (712 total snaps) 5.138 – Xavier Thomas 5.162 – Christian Jones 6.191 – Tejhaun Palmer 7.226 – Jaden Davis We can look at 2023 and the miss on not taking Will Anderson Jr., we can look at 2025 and wonder if injuries will be an issue that cause this class to not meet expectations, but the 2024 class was supposed to be the one. Now, there are five players left, they’ve played a combined 95 games and none have been difference makers. To be fair, none of the guys no longer on the roster were difference makers either. But this Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, without knowing what they are getting, and waiting a day to make it final, is just basically unheard of. Hope this works out for the Cardinals, and quite frankly hopefully it helps Marv get a fresh start. But, this also begs the question, why are they letting Monti make deals for players if he is on the hot seat?
