title: 5 Questions with the Enemy: Drew Petzing’s return, the struggling Lions defense and more
summary: Happy Saturday one and all. The Arizona Cardinals take on the Detroit Lions and Ryan Mathews of Pride of Detroit was kind enough to answer some questions for us ahead of the matchup. Enjoy. Right or wrong Arizona Cardinals fans were excited for the Drew Petzing era to end… what do the Lions fans think […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 13: Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing of the Detroit Lions during the first half of an NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 13, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Happy Saturday one and all. The Arizona Cardinals take on the Detroit Lions and Ryan Mathews of Pride of Detroit was kind enough to answer some questions for us ahead of the matchup. Enjoy. Right or wrong Arizona Cardinals fans were excited for the Drew Petzing era to end… what do the Lions fans think after four games? Aside from the “Lions miss Ben Johnson” memes, Detroit’s offense has looked progressively more potent each week. Detroit is fifth in points per game (29.8), sixth in yards per game (389.3), and seventh in EPA/play (+0.10). Things were a bit uneven in Week 1 against the New Orleans Saints, but the Lions capitalized on a couple of turnovers, turning a short field into touchdowns. Detroit put up 31 points in three consecutive weeks, but last week against the Carolina Panthers, the Lions’ offense stalled out in the red zone a couple of times, settling for field goals instead of touchdowns—something that hadn’t been an issue prior to “Sunday Night Football;” Detroit had a 78.6% red zone conversion rate heading into Week 4, good for sixth in the NFL. It does still feel like there’s another dimension of this offense to be unlocked, namely the explosive plays. It’s not necessarily for a lack of trying, as there’s been some failure to execute on those plays be it drops, errant throws, or breakdowns in pass protection. Once Detroit is able to break off some big runs or connect on some more of these deep shots, the offense will feel like it’s back to being one of the most lethal units in the NFL. What on earth is going on with the Lions defense? It’s a fool’s errand to make sense of why this defense has been as bad as it’s been through four weeks. The defensive line is legitimately good. Alim McNeill is first among interior defenders in pressures (20), Aidan Hutchinson is tied for first in pressures (29) among edge defenders, and Tyleik Williams has played really well against the run in his second year out of Ohio State. But for as good as the defensive front has been, the back-seven has been a disaster. Detroit’s 109.3 net passing yards allowed per game when getting pressure is the worst in the NFL —the team ranked 31st, the Atlanta Falcons, allow just 65.3 net passing yards when getting pressure. Woof. Last week’s performance really boiled down to the poor preparation for Carolina. The Panthers RPO’d the Lions into oblivion, with Bryce Young identifying the blitz and throwing the ball to the vacated part of the field. The cornerbacks are playing off coverage often, something that wasn’t a staple during the Aaron Glenn era, and it just doesn’t make sense given how much pressure their defensive front is generating (39.3%, ninth in the NFL). Some of that has to do with the personnel deficiencies—Detroit was in on the Joey Porter Jr. sweepstakes—but some of it is asking a veteran safety like Chuck Clark to pull off feats of athleticism he just can’t make happen at this point in his career. Dan Campbell is adamant there’s more tinkering that can be done to fix things, but consider me skeptical. The Arizona Cardinals defense can’t stop a cold, so is this the week the Lions put up 40+ for the first time? That sure would be nice! It would take Detroit to start hitting on those explosive plays that have yet to materialize reliably. Arizona’s run defense is second best in EPA/rush (-0.24) and they sport a better than average stuff rate at 17.0% (t-13th). The Lions need their rushing offense to be more consistent from kickoff in order to throw up 40+ points in the desert. It helps keep them on schedule and ahead of the sticks, which, at risk of sounding cliche, is when this offense really thrives. Especially with this defense looking the way it does, it’s important this offense put together long, sustained drives to wear down their opponent and their own defense off the field. Do you feel like Dan Campbell is on the hot seat? Not whatsoever. It’s really interesting to get that question from you, and to think of the way things look from the outside looking in. Detroit finished 15-2 just two seasons ago, backslid to a 9-8 record a year ago, and things aren’t off to the hottest of starts, but Campbell’s status with the team, that’s not even really a conversation until this team’s season plays out. It’s dependent upon their record, the playoffs, and a lot more. It would take a pretty abysmal finish to this season for Campbell’s job to be considered at risk. The Cardinals are not covering the 4.5-point line, at least in my mind, but do the Lions do enough on defense to get under 53.5, or is this going to be a monster total? Drew Petzing revenge game incoming? There’s no reason to believe this Lions defense can prevent teams from putting up at least 21 points in a game, so yes, this game feels like it has a great chance at reaching the over. Add to the fact that Campbell has been incredibly vocal about the offense not accepting “mediocrity” this week, noting they have too much talent not to expect greatness from that unit, and you could see Detroit’s offense finally exploding for a huge offensive performance. That being said, with the way Detroit’s defense has looked in 14 of its past 16 quarters, this will likely be a one-score game when it’s all said and done.

title: Falcons vs. Ravens: What will Week 5’s win or loss mean for Atlanta
summary: The season has done a full 180 in the best possible way for the Falcons. Just two weeks ago the doomsday scenarios were being looked at in a magnifying way following two early losses with Cooper Rush under center. Since then, Michael Penix Jr. has returned, the Falcons’ offense has taken off with the arrow […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 24: Linebacker Patrick Queen #6 of the Baltimore Ravens breaks up a pass intended for tight end MyCole Pruitt #85 of the Atlanta Falcons in the second half at M&T Bank Stadium on December 24, 2022 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Rob Carr/Getty Images) | Getty Images The season has done a full 180 in the best possible way for the Falcons. Just two weeks ago the doomsday scenarios were being looked at in a magnifying way following two early losses with Cooper Rush under center. Since then, Michael Penix Jr. has returned, the Falcons’ offense has taken off with the arrow now firmly pointing up. Nothing has given this fanbase as much joy in a very long time as spoiling the New Orleans Saints’ 20th year anniversary of their dome re-opening, and doing it in such an emphatic way on national television. The next test is another one in prime time, this time broadcast into living rooms across the country via NBC on Sunday Night Football. The opponents are the Baltimore Ravens, one of the serial contenders in the AFC. The Falcons caught a break in that they will not have to face Baltimore’s two time MVP winning quarterback Lamar Jackson, but this remains a formidable team nonetheless. Here is the scenario the Falcons face if they beat the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5, as well as if they lose. If the Falcons win They will have completely won back over the majority of the fanbase, including the many folks who are still highly (and very fairly) skeptical waiting in anticipation for the rug to get pulled out from under them. Three straight prime time triumphs will also showcase to the country just how good this team can be and will generate some national respect for the first time in a while. With the Carolina Panthers on a bye week, Atlanta will move into sole possession of first place in the NFC South and this division will all of a sudden not only be a very real goal but also an expectation at this point. The Falcons would win just their third ever game against the Ravens, and their first one since a Thursday Night Football showdown between Matt Ryan and Joe Flacco in 2010. This is the franchise against whom Atlanta has the joint-fewest victories against along the Steelers, who kept that win total at two earlier this season. While it’s still a hilariously low sample size, it will technically be correct to say that Kevin Stefanski will become just the sixth ever Falcons head coach with a record above .500, alongside Mike Smith, Dan Quinn, Leeman Bennett, Jim Mora and Wade Phillips (who has an all time 3-2 record as the head man in Atlanta). If the Falcons lose The wind will promptly be taken out of the sails and the momentum completely halted following back to back dominant wins against NFC opponents. Losing to an AFC team isn’t the end of the world, but for a Falcons team that’s still trying to dig themselves out of the hole they created with Cooper Rush, it’ll still be a blow. For as embarrassed as the Saints were this past week, if they beat Minnesota then they will finish the week tied with the Falcons in second place while the idle Panthers move into sole possession of first place with a 2-2 record. The schedule is tightening up now and there really aren’t too many breaks in it. Games against the Bears, 49ers, Bengals and Chiefs await before the bye week and to go into that stretch below .500, having just lost to a Ravens team missing Lamar, it will feel like one of those missed opportunities that comes back to bite at the end of a season.

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons throws a pass against the New Orleans Saints during the fourth quarter of the game at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty more needs to be proven, but it’s impossible not to be excited about Michael Penix Jr.’s immediate growth under Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees. He is making quicker, sharper decisions to hit his intended target in stride. The comfort with playing under center and being efficient off play action has been a massive boost in an offense that prefers using heavier personnel sets. These developments have led to two dominant wins. For this to happen with a player who largely wasn’t expected to play until midseason is hugely encouraging. His rapport with Drake London remains as strong as ever, after they clicked immediately in the final two games of the 2024 season. His overall command in the pocket helps offset his limitations in creating outside the pocket. There are still growing pains to be endured as Penix Jr. hasn’t started 16 games yet. That isn’t preventing fans from believing he can be Atlanta’s franchise quarterback. It’s been a dramatic shift not only for him, but for the team overall after a horrific start to the season. The Falcons enter a crucial stretch playing three teams that seem destined to be contenders. Facing Baltimore, Chicago, and San Francisco will be major litmus tests, no matter how much the Ravens and Bears adjust without their franchise quarterbacks. Both teams have proven they can win without them. Atlanta must prove they can beat playoff-bound teams and justify the fanbase’s enormous confidence. title: Falcons vs. Ravens: A look at the series history going into 2026
summary: The Falcons come home after back to back prime time road games, and they will continue the prime time sequence with a third consecutive such game. This one is against an opponent whom they have rarely ever beaten in the handful of games they have played. The Baltimore Ravens come to town and they put […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - SEPTEMBER 03: Matt Ryan #2 of the Atlanta Falcons converses with Joe Flacco #5 of the Baltimore Ravens after their 20-19 win at Georgia Dome on September 3, 2015 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons come home after back to back prime time road games, and they will continue the prime time sequence with a third consecutive such game. This one is against an opponent whom they have rarely ever beaten in the handful of games they have played. The Baltimore Ravens come to town and they put their 5-2 all time record against their fellow bird themed opponent on the line. Due to their recent inception into the NFL in 1996 (the Ravens were technically the old Cleveland Browns but the NFL made the ruling that the history of the Browns would stay in Cleveland as they quickly got an expansion franchise three years later) and playing in the AFC, the Ravens and Falcons have not faced off much. The first ever meeting went into overtime and went Baltimore’s way in 1999 before the Falcons got some payback behind the DVD offense in 2002. The Ravens as a franchise, meanwhile, did not have to wait long to taste ultimate glory in the NFL, as they won the Super Bowl behind one of the most dominant defensive units of all time just five years into their existence in 2000. That defense remained formidable for the next decade plus, led by the best linebacker of his generation (Ray Lewis) and the best safety of his generation (Ed Reed), and it was that defense which shut the Falcons down in 2006, before Matt Ryan figured them out and led a game winning drive on Thursday Night Football in an elite battle in the 2010 season. That was about all of Atlanta’s success, as they have dropped the last three games in this matchup since then. When these teams met last The Falcons’ season was dead in the water by the time they went up to Baltimore for a Christmas Eve showdown, sitting at just 5-9 and now using the rest of the campaign to evaluate the play of rookie quarterback Desmond Ridder. He faced off against Tyler Huntley, who was starting in relief of the injured Lamar Jackson (sound familiar?). It was a rough outing for the offense, as they came away with no points on their first four drives, getting into Baltimore territory twice but turning it over both times — once on downs and once via a Drake London fumble. They finally put together a last second field goal drive in the first half but the Ravens had already scored a touchdown, two point conversion and two field goals by that point. The uphill battle was on in the second half as the Falcons’ defense tightened up and allowed just one field goal the rest of the way, but the offense stayed stuck in neutral. Younghoe Koo kicked a pair of field goals, but the back breaker was Tyler Allgeier getting stuffed from the Baltimore 1-yard-line on 4th and goal to cap off a long fourth quarter drive as the end zone was a foreign concept to the Atlanta offense on this day.

title: Ravens discussion: score predictions, X-factors vs. Falcons in Week 5
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are taking on the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday night in their first primetime game of the season. The absence of Lamar Jackson looms large over the matchup, as does the Falcons’ dominant performance in their last two games. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for Sunday Night Football: Nikhil Mehta The Falcons are […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Trenton Simpson #32 of the Baltimore Ravens reacts as he takes the field against the New Orleans Saints prior to an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are taking on the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday night in their first primetime game of the season. The absence of Lamar Jackson looms large over the matchup, as does the Falcons’ dominant performance in their last two games. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s predictions for Sunday Night Football: Nikhil Mehta The Falcons are the wrong opponent at the wrong time for the Ravens. With Lamar Jackson healthy, this game would have the potential to be the most explosive shootout of the year. But Tyler Huntley could be in for a long night behind Baltimore’s injured, reshuffled offensive line against Atlanta’s disruptive interior rushers. What’s more, neither his nor Derrick Henry’s legs will be able to bail him out against the Falcons’ phenomenal run defense. It’s a similar story on the other side of the ball. The Ravens have struggled to tackle to start the year, so naturally, their next opponent is Bijan Robinson. This could seriously be a rough loss for Baltimore. I believe in Huntley’s ‘gamer’ quality that allows him to take his game to another level when he steps on the field, but everything about this matchup leans in Atlanta’s direction. X-factor: Tyler Huntley. Obvious? Absolutely. But it’s never been more true. The Ravens leaned on their run game in Snoop’s starts last year, but he made the handful of throws they needed him to. Those moments could come at a much higher volume on Sunday night. Score prediction: Falcons 28, Ravens 16 Zach Canter Despite the Ravens coming in shorthanded without Lamar Jackson facing the competition of primetime Bijan Robinson and a red hot Falcons, I don’t think this is going to be a bloodbath. This is a great spot for Jesse Minter kickstart the defense and finally get them right. I think the Ravens focus on trying to limit the run game and Robinson doesn’t bully them all game. Snoop Huntley and the offense will do just enough to put them in a spot to win. Overall, if the Ravens want to win, it’ll take the offense holding onto the ball and playing a simple calm game while the defenses forces the Atlanta offense to settle for field goals. I think both units are capable of this and will do it for most of the time. But the Ravens fall just short of pulling out the win. X-factor: Tackling: If the Ravens can solve their tackling woes, they have a chance to become one of the elite teams in the NFL. There’s no better place to start fixing it than facing Bijan Robinson. If the Ravens can limit his explosive plays, they’ll give Snoop Huntley a chance to win this game for them. Score prediction: Falcons 22, Ravens 17 Stephen Bopst The shorthanded Ravens head to Atlanta to face a red-hot Falcons team that’s coming off back-to-back blowout victories. With Lamar Jackson out, it will be Jesse Minters’ first real test as head coach playing without his star quarterback. The Falcons have the best running back in the NFL in Bijan Robinson and an opportunistic defense that’s been effective at getting after opposing quarterbacks. It would’ve been a challenge even if Jackson was healthy and not having him further compounds the importance of the defense having a great game. Tyler Huntley has performed well in these spots over the years and I expect him to play a clean game. Unfortunately, I think the absence of Jackson and Trey Hendrickson will be too much to overcome. The Ravens will play hard but lose a close one. X-factor: Trenton Simpson. Simpson has been a revelation for the Ravens this year and has the athleticism to chase down perimeter runs. The Falcons love running outside zone concepts and Simpson could be a weapon used to combat it. Score prediction: Falcons 27, Ravens 23 Dustin Cox This games revolves around the run game, with the defense needing to somehow slow down Bijan Robinson, and the offense leaning on Derrick Henry without Lamar Jackson. Baltimore’s defense will have a long day if they do not devote resources to stopping the run this week. Playing more defensive backs instead of heavier packages could be a recipe for disaster against the Falcons. Meanwhile, the Ravens’ offense cannot afford to find themselves in obvious passing situations with Tyler Huntley at quarterback behind a suspect offensive line. Keeping the offense running on schedule and ahead of the sticks will be paramount to avoid falling behind in this one. Pre-snap penalties could be a death penalty as well without Jackson on the field to bail the offense out. Ultimately, I think Baltimore will put up an admirable fight but will not have the juice on offense to get the win. X-factor: Mike Green. Green flashed his pass-rush potential last week, but he will need to hold up in the run game this week against Atlanta’s zone run scheme. Score prediction: Falcons 27, Ravens 17

title: NFL predictions: scheming up the Ravens’ primetime visit to Atlanta
summary: The Baltimore Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans came at a steep cost. Lamar Jackson’s “unconventional” ankle injury – neither a high nor low sprain, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport – will sideline him in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons, and potentially beyond. Jackson’s injury has positioned the red-hot Falcons as 3.5-point […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons runs the ball during the third quarter of a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans came at a steep cost. Lamar Jackson’s “unconventional” ankle injury – neither a high nor low sprain, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport – will sideline him in Week 5 against the Atlanta Falcons, and potentially beyond. Jackson’s injury has positioned the red-hot Falcons as 3.5-point favorites for a home primetime matchup ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). The Ravens will also be without leading edge rusher Trey Hendrickson, and newly-acquired center Cam Jurgens will not be available until next week. This will be a tough matchup for Jesse Minter’s 3-1 squad on both sides of the ball against a 2-2 Falcons team that is firing on all cylinders coming into Week 5. Atlanta lost their first two games with ex-Raven Cooper Rush under center, but Michael Penix’s return to the starting lineup has sent their offense into the stratosphere. The Falcons have eclipsed 200 passing and rushing yards in both of his starts with a total of 80 points and 918 yards of offense. Their defense has stifled opposing rushing offenses to the tune of just 48.3 yards per game and 2.7 yards per carry. They have allowed the third-most passing yards in the league, but just the seventh-fewest yards per attempt, due in large part to a ferocious pass rush. The Falcons’ run defense will be a major obstacle for the Ravens, who are trotting out backup quarterback Tyler Huntley for his 17th career start (12th in Baltimore). He came away with victories in both of Jackson’s absence last year and has a reputation as a ‘gamer’ who can play above his perceived arm talent. But his success has been predicated on Baltimore’s ability to run the ball, both via traditional under-center concepts to Derrick Henry and utilizing Huntley’s legs in the read-option game. The Ravens’ run game with Jackson on the field has been underwhelming at times this year, so Declan Doyle and Dwayne Ledford will need to find a new way to break through the Falcons’ front. Beatdown’s Zach Canter proposed a heavy dose of outside zone runs to target Atlanta’s weakened group of edge defenders and force their fearsome interior to chase plays to the sideline, and I’m inclined to agree. Doyle needs to mix in plenty of QB runs for Huntley to keep the Falcons defense honest and take one defender out of the play whenever possible. Keeping the offense ahead of the sticks will avoid obvious passing downs that allow the opposing pass rush to pin their ears back and attack a Ravens offensive line that is still dealing with multiple injuries. In the pass game, Doyle should give Huntley quick reads and dial up plenty of high-percentage designed touches for his skill players. The Falcons will be keying on Zay Flowers, the league’s most efficient receiver through four weeks, so Doyle may need to explore some changeups. What about a TE screen to Matt Hibner, who has flashed a knack for YAC in his first four NFL games? Rashod Bateman is not as dynamic of an athlete as Flowers, but he is underrated after the catch and could take Atlanta by surprise if Doyle schemes him into open space. When scouting the Falcons during their win over the Saints on Monday night , I noted the potential for Jesse Minter to run more base defense against Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. But instead of moving back to Baltimore’s traditional 3-4, Minter could roll out some 4-3 looks with Roquan Smith, Trenton Simpson, and Teddye Buchanan as off-ball linebackers. If the Falcons go heavy, Kyle Hamilton can line up in the box into a modified 4-4 look, too. Might be a good game to break out a 3 LB look with Roquan, Simpson & Teddye on the field at the same time. Get Hamilton to move up more too. The issue with Bijan is he can also hit you on the perimeter so you need speed & creativity with the personnel packages. #Ravens https://t.co/mRFcSggFSC — Dev Panchwagh (@devpanchwagh) October 6, 2026 But scheme and personnel will not matter if the Ravens do not tackle. Minter and defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver have surely been stressing fundamentals all week, and I’ll throw one more note on there: stop selling out for the strip. Baltimore’s defenders love to fly in and attempt punch-outs, and they will be tempted to do so against Robinson, who has coughed the ball up 11 times since 2023. But that aggressiveness leads to more missed tackles that the defense will not be able to afford on Sunday night. Instead, the first defender needs to focus on wrapping up the ballcarrier and wait for his teammates to go for the ball. This does not mean give up on forcing fumbles, but rather controlling risk when doing so. The Falcons have installed a quick-passing game that gets the ball into the hands of their playmakers as fast as possible. Penix’s 2.29-second time-to-throw is the fastest in the league, so Minter needs to use that quickness against him. Blitzing will not work – the ball comes out too fast – but showing pressure could bait Penix into targeting his pre-snap hot reads. Minter has gleefully sent Kyle Hamilton at opposing quarterbacks this year, setting up a potential changeup on Sunday night with the 6-foot-4 safety dropping off the line of scrimmage into Penix’s quick passing lanes. title: 3 Keys to Victory for Ravens-Falcons Week 5
summary: The Ravens are taking on a real challenge in Week 5, traveling down to Atlanta to take on a red-hot Falcons team that has won back-to-back primetime games with Michael Penix back under center. Baltimore will not have Lamar Jackson on Sunday night, throwing a massive wrench into Declan Doyle’s offensive plans, while Jesse Minter […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 04: Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before the game against the Tennessee Titans at M&T Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Ravens are taking on a real challenge in Week 5, traveling down to Atlanta to take on a red-hot Falcons team that has won back-to-back primetime games with Michael Penix back under center. Baltimore will not have Lamar Jackson on Sunday night, throwing a massive wrench into Declan Doyle’s offensive plans, while Jesse Minter and Anthony Weaver will have to scheme against Bijan Robinson, who has demolished opposing defenses thus far this year. A heavily designed offensive plan Atlanta is going to score. They have too much offensive firepower between Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and other weapons not to. The Ravens offense is likely going to need to find a way to score more than 17 to have a chance. It’ll be Tyler Huntley leading the team in this one with Jackson down. The obvious first step is a heavy dose of the run game using both Huntley and Derrick Henry. Expect the Ravens to run a heavy outside zone game, similar to what Huntley and Henry did in their big win against Green Bay last year, especially against Atlanta’s depleted EDGE room. Huntley himself needs to get plenty of carries. He isn’t as good as running the option game as Jackson, but he’s certainly capable enough to take some of the attention off Henry. Keep the time of possession in favor of Baltimore and Atlanta’s weapons off the field. The pass game should be kept simple. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has done an excellent job of giving Lamar Jackson a ton of quick, easy first-read throw options. He needs to dial that up to the max this game. There should be a ton of designed touches planned for this one. Screens to Zay Flowers, Justice Hill, and Henry; tight end leaks to Matt Hibner like we’ve seen a ton this season; and easy quick reads to the top guys like Flowers, Rashod Bateman, and Mark Andrews. Make the completions easy and avoid putting your defense in a bad spot with turnovers. Sell out for the run Speaking of defense, we should clear something up. There’s been a lot of concern about the Ravens’ run defense going into this weekend, which is fair considering the opponent. Jonathan Taylor and Javonte Williams both averaged over five yards per carry in Weeks 1 and 2; what kind of damage can Robinson do? That being said, I think Baltimore’s run D is designed this way. From what I’ve seen, it feels like Jesse Minter is willing to take his chances with nickel and even dime personnel against the run, giving up more yardage on the ground but slowing opponents’ passing attacks. That can’t be the game plan against Atlanta. Without Jackson running the offense, capable of consistent drives with explosive plays, the Ravens can’t be content with letting Robinson, who’s been the best back in the league this year, eat up grass and drain the clock. While Minter likes to live in nickel and dime, it’s time to get all three of Roquan Smith, Trenton Simpson, and Teddye Buchanan on the field at the same time and bottle up Robinson as much as possible. Force Michael Penix to consistently make big throws over the top to Drake London, covered by Nate Wiggins, in order for Atlanta to win. This is the type of game where giving up quick scores is far preferable to long, punishing drives that take a toll as the game wars on. Short leash on Huntley I like Snoop. He’s been the most stable backup the Ravens have had behind Lamar Jackson since the Robert Griffin III days. He saved the season last year and kept the Ravens alive for a playoff chase when Jackson was down and Cooper Rush clearly couldn’t get it done. That being said, that was then, and this is now. It’s a new offense with a new coordinator and a new head coach. Plus, there’s the lingering fact that the Ravens very purposefully kept a third quarterback on their roster, UDFA Joe Fagnano, who came out of nowhere and dominated in the preseason enough to force a roster choice. In the second half of the Titans game, the Ravens offense was shut out, only generating 116 yards on 28 plays. That’s 4.1 yards per play and would rank last in the NFL. Game script was certainly a factor, as was the weather. But if Huntley puts together another first half like that against the Falcons, the Ravens should strongly consider putting in Joe Fagnano, who looked very comfortable operating what Doyle wants to do on offense, preseason competition aside.
author: Zach Canter

title: Buffalo Bills rule out two starters for Monday Night Football vs. Rams
summary: The Buffalo Bills won’t play football tomorrow. But when they do face the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football they will be without a couple of veteran starters.   After Saturday’s practice, head coach Joe Brady told us that Ed Oliver and Joshua Palmer have been ruled out for Week 5. Oliver is dealing with a knee injury he suffered last Sunday, and Palmer […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills won’t play football tomorrow. But when they do face the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football they will be without a couple of veteran starters. After Saturday’s practice, head coach Joe Brady told us that Ed Oliver and Joshua Palmer have been ruled out for Week 5. Oliver is dealing with a knee injury he suffered last Sunday, and Palmer popped up on Friday’s report with a shoulder injury. Despite those two designations, there’s still plenty of unknowns surrounding Monday night. DJ Moore is once again listed as questionable – same story as last week. The veteran wide receiver has not missed a game since 2020, but that doesn’t mean he shouldn’t. Last week Moore went through a similar practice routine, entered the weekend questionable, and then started the game. He didn’t last long as he headed to the locker room after aggravating the shoulder injury he’s been trying to play through. Not great for a Bills’ offense that thought it finally had a true WR1. Also questionable is Dee Alford, the Bills nickel corner. Buffalo doesn’t have anyone lined up behind Alford on their depth chart, and Sunday saw them throwing Damar Hamlin in the slot. Landon Jackson gets the questionable designation as well. He’s another one that some may have thought was worse than it ended up being. There were rumors that he could have suffered an ACL injury during last week’s game, but the second-year defensive lineman was able to return to the game, spent one day as a limited participant and then had two full practices this week. Despite the question marks, there are a couple of things we do know on the positive side of the scale. Brady said that Christian Benford will play. The Bills corner missed last week with a toe injury, but it was apparently not quite as bad as the walking boot he was in two weeks ago might have had us think. The Buffalo head coach also said that rookie Skyler Bell will be active this week. This will be the first NFL regular season action for the rookie wide receiver. The fourth round pick out of UConn has been saying he’s ready to go for weeks now. Monday, we find out.

summary: The drama surrounding Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. continues. After rampant speculation about the potential for him to be traded just as the 2026 NFL season began, ESPN senior NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport have both reported that the Cardinals’ front office is, indeed, finalizing a deal to trade Harrison to […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 12: Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts during the NFL 2025 game between Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The drama surrounding Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. continues. After rampant speculation about the potential for him to be traded just as the 2026 NFL season began, ESPN senior NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport have both reported that the Cardinals’ front office is, indeed, finalizing a deal to trade Harrison to a new team. Jordan Schultz also shared that Harrison will be inactive for Arizona’s Week 5 game, “and the teams involved would ‘prefer the trade destination is NOT announced’ until both team’s (sic) play this weekend, according to multiple sources. ” A tweet by @UnderdogNFL states that “Cardinals and Texans have engaged in ‘deep’ negotiations for Marvin Harrison Jr. in exchange for ‘significant draft capital,” while adding that “Cardinals informed Texans they are still listening to potential offers from other teams with hopes of receiving 1st-round draft choice.” That report goes on to state that “Several teams have reached out with interest in acquiring Harrison, although at least one team feels Harrison is worth a Day 2 pick.” That’s essentially it for the latest news on Harrison, which won’t end speculation about his next stop. There are no concrete reports linking the Buffalo Bills and Harrison at this juncture. But it’s reasonable to believe that the Bills could be among the mix of teams looking to negotiate a trade for Harrison. However, there is a bit of heat around him heading to the Houston Texans, with both Schefter and Rapoport saying that talks have happened . That’s likely to be true of many teams, including the Indianapolis Colts. Those sources would neither “confirm or deny at this time” about any trade talk, however, the Texans are in need of help at wide receiver. Additionally, if Arizona pulls off a trade with Houston, it would reunite Harrison with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud. Harrison has become an afterthought in the Cardinals’ moribund offense, but his mostly uninspired play and inability to make routine catches or create separation have an equal role in the failed relationship. Will a reset prove fruitful — and where is he headed? Could Buffalo hold the key to his next opportunity? The Bills have several injury concerns in the wide receivers room, namely to DJ Moore (AC-joint sprain), but Joshua Palmer (shoulder) also popped up on the injury report this week and will miss Week 5, per Sal Capaccio . Also of note is the fact that Keon Coleman has dealt with an ankle injury (though he’s managed to play through it). Considering that alone, One Bills Drive has almost certainly called about Harrison — that’s what president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane has told us he does with any intriguing player. If Harrison has struggled to succeed in Arizona, is the risk worth it weight in any potential trade? Many would say yes simply because he’s the son of Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver Marvin Harrison. Harrison entered the 2024 NFL Draft as a can’t-miss prospect with generational talent. The results have proven less than stunning, but many wonder if he just needs a generational talent at quarterback to get him better footballs. Quarterback Josh Allen fits the bill. What role would Harrison play in Buffalo is perhaps the better question. Adding Harrison probably means parting ways with someone currently on the roster, such as Palmer or Coleman. That carries risk as both Palmer and Coleman have built chemistry within the system, and both have been more productive in 2026. It’s unlikely the Cardinals receive a significant and early first-round pick for Harrison. His stock has never been lower, and NFL execs aren’t in the habit of digging deep into their resources for what amounts to a reclamation project at this point in time. Schefter Posted Harrison Jr traded but no details for where yet | Buffalo Rumblings

title: Buffalo Bills trending up, trending down: Who Bills need on Monday Night Football in Los Angeles
summary: It wasn’t pretty. The Patriots game told us what’s broken. Monday night at SoFi Stadium tells us whether Buffalo can fix (or at least mask) it in a week. The Rams are 2.5- to 3-point favorites, and they’re bringing the one thing the Bills’ secondary has struggled most to stop: receivers who win on the […]
full_text: It wasn’t pretty. The Patriots game told us what’s broken. Monday night at SoFi Stadium tells us whether Buffalo can fix (or at least mask) it in a week. The Rams are 2.5- to 3-point favorites, and they’re bringing the one thing the Bills’ secondary has struggled most to stop: receivers who win on the outside. I’m not here to relitigate the 29-26 loss. I’m here to use it. Every Hero and Head Scratcher below is judged by what he showed against New England and what he has to do against Matthew Stafford, Puka Nacua, and Davante Adams. Here’s the big picture. Buffalo’s offense leads the league in scoring (127 points through four games) and converts 53.3% of its third downs. The Rams’ defense allows just 145.5 passing yards per game and a 75.4 passer rating. On the other side, Buffalo allows 20.5 passing points per game, the second-most in the league, and a 6.8% touchdown rate (29th), per Sharp Football. A lot of players are banged up. Who needs to step up on the big stage to help the Bills move to 4-1? Heroes DE Greg Rousseau: the answer to Stafford’s pocket problem I’ve tried to avoid repeating names on this list, but it’s impossible at some point. Greg Rousseau has played lights out, week in and week out. Rousseau has six sacks, the most in the NFL. Against New England, his streak of two sacks per game ended, but he still had eight pressures and at least four hits on Drake Maye, while he defended the run as he usually does, very well. He also had a strip-sack called back after review, in a play where he was an inch away from making it count. Here’s why Groot matters on Monday. Stafford has the NFL’s third-worst passer rating under pressure (29.1) and the sixth-lowest completion rate when pressured (37.0%). His accuracy is 34 percentage points worse under pressure than in a clean pocket, the largest gap among qualifying quarterbacks. He has already thrown six interceptions in four games (eight all of last year), and he went 32-of-52 for 317 yards, no touchdowns and two picks at Philadelphia. Not exactly MVP numbers. So the Bills’ best coverage call is to put the heat on Stafford. The catch is real: 4for4 ranks the Rams’ offensive line first in the league, with a 29.5% pressure rate allowed (sixth) and the best interior group at preventing pressure. Rousseau on the edge is Buffalo’s cleanest path to that pocket. With the Bills’ secondary struggling, the pass rush is the plan to save the day. WR Keon Coleman: Can he be the guy if DJ Moore sits? DJ Moore left in the second quarter after re-injuring his shoulder and did not practice Thursday. Buffalo has its bye in Week 7, so resting him is a real possibility. Coleman is who stepped up against New England: six catches on seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown, six of those targets after Moore went out, and the team’s best PFF grade (79.2). In the fourth quarter, he caught a third-and-6 throw for 22, then caught a 24-yarder and a 34-yard touchdown on a deep post to put Buffalo up 26-21. He is 14-for-16 for 217 yards on the season, and with Moore off the field, he has run 3.33 yards per route, per Sharp Football. Skeptics will say New England was missing its top corner. Fair. The Rams are a different test. Trent McDuffie has allowed only 5 completions on 18 targets (27.8%), and Coleman plays 75% of his snaps outside, though Jaylen Watson is expected to miss the game, which leaves Josh Wallace opposite McDuffie. Los Angeles has allowed just five pass plays of 20-plus yards, tied for the fewest in the league. Buffalo has 17, tied for second most on offense. That’s the matchup: Coleman’s targets against the best secondary in football so far. With Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir also in the fold, Coleman might be able to keep up the good production. Head Scratchers CB Maxwell Hairston: from an asset to a liability, to… Uno was no bueno. Two touchdowns. Romeo Doubs finished with six catches on nine targets for 58 yards and two scores, both on Hairston, who was the most-targeted defender by New England. On the opening drive, he got lost in zone on a fourth-and-3 conversion, and Doubs beat him on the next play for 14 yards and a touchdown. In the second half, a holding flag wiped out a third-down sack, and two plays later Doubs made a one-handed grab on a 2-yard fade. He also played inexcusably far off the line on a red-zone fourth down. PFF graded him a 32.0, the lowest of any Bill in the game. This was a regression, not a verdict. Before Sunday, PFF had him at 56.7 on the season, and Next Gen Stats had him allowing a 36.4% completion rate (minimum 10 targets). He’s now at a 114.4 passer rating allowed when targeted, per Sharp Football. Draft status is not a guarantee of professional success, though, and Monday’s receivers don’t care where he was picked. Adams plays 88% of his snaps outside, and Buffalo allows 9.0 catches per game (26th) and a 9.3% touchdown rate (29th) to outside receivers. His target share has dipped with Nacua back (23.5% of routes and 1.54 yards per route with Nacua on the field, versus 33.5% and 3.23 without), and he saw just four catches for 32 yards in Philadelphia. But he is still touchdown-dependent in this offense, and touchdowns are where Hairston got hurt. Nacua returned from a two-game absence with 9 catches on 12 targets for 125 yards, running a route on 90.7% of dropbacks. Christian Benford, who missed Week 4 with a toe injury, was back at practice Thursday. But he is not an automatic fix: PFF had him at 40.6 entering Week 4 (97th of 99 corners), and he has allowed a 124.4 passer rating when targeted. Whoever draws Adams and Nacua, the Bills can’t afford a repeat of the fourth-and-short conversions that kept New England’s drives alive. QB Josh Allen: the last throw can’t be the first problem Monday I’ll say it plainly: that last throw was a head scratcher. Allen was 23-of-33 for 253 yards, a touchdown and an interception, plus a 2-yard sneak for a score. But down three with the clock on his side, he forced a throw that Craig Woodson picked off to end the game. An inexcusable decision, even if he had his WR open before he had to spin to avoid a sack. It’s a game of inches, and the second he spent to evade the free rusher changed the picture entirely. A 10-year vet, the best QB in the league, can’t do that, period. He also ran five times for four yards, avoiding contact and looking nothing like himself, mobility-wise. On Thursday, Alen quickly dismissed the possibility of playing injured, but honestly, it’s hard to believe his words with the way he moved last game. Josh has played through some meaningful injuries for a couple of seasons now, and I don’t believe he’s 100% healthy at the moment, as he suggests. Buffalo has seven giveaways in two games, five against the Chargers and two against New England. The Rams matter here for a specific reason. Their defense is stingy: second in completion rate allowed (53.5%) and first in yards per attempt allowed (4.8). But it isn’t a takeaway machine, and Myles Garrett is on injured reserve, so the pass rush runs through Byron Young (20.1% pressure rate). Allen’s 39.4% play-action rate is second in the NFL, while Stafford’s 22.5% ranks 31st, so Buffalo will lean on the tool this Rams defense has to respect. Establishing the run with James Cook will be important again, and if Buffalo loses Monday, it’s more likely to be because the Bills couldn’t run the ball and gave it away than because the Rams took it. Honorable Mentions Trending Up: RB James Cook: 6.4, 6.4, and 6.3 yards per carry over his last three games, and the league’s best rate of 10-plus-yard runs (21.4%). Yet he got just 12 carries on 35 snaps (59%) against New England. The Rams allow 3.8 yards per carry to backs (12th) and a 4.7% rate of 10-plus-yard runs (4th), so he needs volume. DT Greg Gaines: He recovered Maye’s fumble and posted PFF’s third-best grade on the team (73.8). With Ed Oliver sitting out Thursday’s practice with a knee issue, he matters against the NFL’s best…

title: Panthers fans optimistic, but not convinced on Young’s hot start
summary: Bryce Young has flashed promise, usually against the Atlanta Falcons, since his second year in the league. The one thing that Carolina Panthers fans have been asking from him is for Young to live up to that promise on a consistent basis. When he plays well, fan confidence surges. That confidence has plummeted immediately after […]
full_text: Bryce Young has flashed promise, usually against the Atlanta Falcons, since his second year in the league. The one thing that Carolina Panthers fans have been asking from him is for Young to live up to that promise on a consistent basis. When he plays well, fan confidence surges. That confidence has plummeted immediately after Young has played poorly in a loss. 70% of fans were confident in the team’s direction after the Panthers’ opening week loss to the Chicago Bears. That number jumped to 90% of fans after trouncing the Atlanta Falcons in Week 2. The Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns dropped it to 48% of fans. Now that last number has doubled. 96% of fans saw what Young accomplished with most of his team on the sidelines, against a surging Detroit Lions team and were happy with it. I’m not sure what the other 4% saw. If this is the Young we can expect going forwards then how could you not be confident in the Panthers current direction? That said, the ‘if’ in that last sentence is carrying a lot of weight. This is easily the best start to a season that Young has had as a pro. That can be measured in basic passing statistics, the team’s wins, or a casual eye test. Young flat out looks better than he ever has on the field. If he maintains that level of play then the Panthers are set up for something special. The question now before Panthers fans is what does Young have to do to convince you this is real. Does he have to keep playing at this level? Does he have to elevate further? Or are you already sold? Most fans, reasonably, just want to see sustained success across a whole season. Few fans are handing out free passes after watching his first three seasons. We’ll cross our fingers that the team can get healthier over this bye week to increase the possibility that the Young we have seen so far is the one we get to see again and again. title: Chicago Bears vs Green Bay Packers – Game Picks and Predictions
summary: Sunday at Lambeau Field (noon CT) — Hello Chicago Bears fans! The 3-1 Chicago Bears travel north for the latest chapter of the NFL’s oldest rivalry against the 2-2 Green Bay Packers. Chicago arrives without the back who just torched the Jets—Kyle Monangai is out with turf toe after his 30-carry, 146-yard, two-touchdown afternoon. The […]
full_text: Sunday at Lambeau Field (noon CT) — Hello Chicago Bears fans! The 3-1 Chicago Bears travel north for the latest chapter of the NFL’s oldest rivalry against the 2-2 Green Bay Packers. Chicago arrives without the back who just torched the Jets—Kyle Monangai is out with turf toe after his 30-carry, 146-yard, two-touchdown afternoon. The Bears will (probably?) once again go with Tyson Bagent under center while Caleb Williams (hamstring) remains questionable and is not expected to start. D’Andre Swift is set to shoulder the bulk of the ground game, with Roschon Johnson likely seeing a bigger role, against a Packers defense that has been generous on the ground. Green Bay has a starting quarterback, Jordan Love, so they’ve got that going for them along with the home-field advantage. Still, even with the missing key players for the Beloved, the Bears enter as slight favorites on the strength of their top-ranked rushing attack and a defense that has been stingy for three straight weeks. Below is our roundtable predicting the score, individual highlights like touchdowns, yardage, interceptions, and who we think goes off in this one. Special note : Rest in Peace, Iron Mike. We will be thinking of you this Sunday. Lester : My prediction for Sunday… to quote Clubber Lang, is “Pain.” The Bears will bully the Packers with their league-leading running game, and when the Packers least expect it, they’ll dial up a deep shot or two as they creep up to stop the run. These are two franchises headed in opposite directions, and after the Bears win, let’s call it, 28 to 17, the seat will get really warm for Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur. Sam : It’s still difficult for me to rewire my brain to expect the Bears to annually compete against the team up north after years of having my heart ripped out. But this is a new era and I think Ben Johnson doesn’t want to rely on Wild comebacks. He wants dominance. I think the Packers will keep it close though and will put up a fight. They aren’t ready to throw in the towel on the season or quit on their coach. Bears 28, Packers 23 Gary : t’s hard to get past how lopsided the rivalry has been up until these past two seasons, so on the surface level it’s hard for me to speak confidently. But F it, this is a new era, and Ben Johnson owns the Packers. Bears win by at least two scores in a fashion similar to the Jets game. Bears 27, Packers 13. TJ Starman : Emotions will be at the maximum for this one (mine at least) so you don’t know how what could go off the rails, but the Bears appear to clearly be the better team. I would expect Chicago to out-coach Green Bay, despite an exchange of a few haymakers both ways. Bears ultimately take a fairly close one, 24 – 20 GOOCH : I’m with TJ in that I am going to be all in my feelings for this game. Iron Mike and the 80s Bears were the team I grew up on. With that said, I think Ben Johnson will have the Bears focused and hungry this Sunday. I think the Bears are going to pound the rock – so two touchdowns for Swift and over 100 yards rushing. Roschan adds a short-yardage score and fifty yards himself. Tyson Bagent throws for just over two hundred yards in an efficient and effective outing and adds another touchdown, this time to Colston Loveland. As for the Bears defense they harry Love all day and, because they are down early, Love is throwing quite a bit. I see two sacks for Sweat, and one apiece for Booker and Motivated Dayo. Add in an interception for Muhammed, and it is the Bears in a rout: 42 – 10. Superfans: Question: Who would win, Coach Ditka vs. a hurricane, but the hurricane is named Hurricane Ditka, and the battle between Da Coach and Da Hurricane took place in Lambeau Field while Da Bears and Packers were playing a Week 5 game in 2026? Answer: It’s a trick question, because it would be a three-way tie, with Da Bears, the Midwestern weather anomaly, and Da Coach all declared winners, and the Packers the loser. Josh : It’s going to be closer than it should be because it’s a divisional game. Call it 31-24, with both run games going off, but the difference being made by Chicago limiting explosive plays. Swift gets redemption. Josh’s cats Arches & Denail : “meow, meow, meow meow, meow meow meow….meow meow.” Translation: Bears 5000 – Packers 0, powered by bapping Jordan Love, a strong run game, and Iron Mike looking down from Bears Heaven. You said it, Arches & Denail! But what do you guys think the score will be on Sunday as the Bears head to Lambeu to take on the Pack? What picks and predictions do you have for the game? Tell us in the comments below!

title: Chicago Bears @ Green Bay Packers: Week 5 Players to Watch
summary: It’s Packer week. Ditka joins Sweetness and the other departed legends in Heaven, and Chicago looks to get its third straight win over the Packers, and its fourth in its last five. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - JANUARY 5: Tight end Tucker Kraft #85 of the Green Bay Packers attempts to complete a catch under pressure during an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears, at Lambeau Field on January 5, 2025 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Packer week. Ditka joins Sweetness and the other departed legends in Heaven, and Chicago looks to get its third straight win over the Packers, and its fourth in its last five. In this weekly series, I’ll feature one player from the Chicago Bears opponent on each side of the ball who I think is integral to their team’s success. Like seasons past, you won’t see any quarterbacks, as the nature of the position always makes them critical for a team’s success. I’ll also try and mix in a few under the radar players from time to time. Let’s start with the Cheese defense. Defense: Lukas Van Ness, #90 – Edge Much like Dallas Turner of the Minnesota Vikings, Van Ness finally appears to be living up to his first round billing this season. Not only is the former Iowa Hawkeye among the league’s best when it comes to pass rush win rate (ESPN) and time to pressure (Stats IQ), but he is also top three in run grade for edge rushers according to PFN. To put it plainly, the 6’5”, 272 lb stud is making his presence felt on all three downs in a big way. Bears reserve LT Theo Benedet will have his work cut out for him in this one, but I am sure Ben Johnson will scheme some help his way as well. If Theo and co. can keep Van Ness at bay as a pass rusher and reach the edge in the run game, Chicago should have no problem moving the ball up and down the field and scoring points. But if he can continue with his high level of play against The Beloved, Green Bay could pull off the upset at home. Offense: Tucker Kraft, #85 – TE After starting last season on an absolute tear before his season ending injury, Kraft has not started with anywhere near as much production this season. To add insult to injury, he has also made some pretty foolish comments about the fan support, or lack thereof, on his home turf at Lambeau. All that said, Kraft is still one heck of a ball player and I expect Tight Ends from both teams to have big games in this one after the news of Iron Mike’s passing came out this week. When healthy, Kraft plays the game the right way and is a force to be reckoned with after the catch and an underrated blocker as well. Though he has recently struggled with drops of late, it has not been something he has made a habit of to this point in his career and feel it is just a mental slump than anything. Considering the GB offensive line is as bad as some of the dismal Bears offensive lines of recent memory, I am expecting Love to look Kraft’s way early and often as a quick outlet. If Chicago’s LBs and DBs can limit his production, particularly after the catch where he is so dangerous, it should keep the Lambeau crowd out of it and get the Packers offense off the field in a Bears rout. But if he saves his best game for the rivalry, it could be a long day for Chicago’s defense. What about you? Which Green Bay Packer will have your attention this week?

title: Who would shock you as a Chicago Bears Trade Target?
summary: We’ve been looking at rumors concerning the Chicago Bears and general manager Ryan Poles being looking to add to the roster before the trade deadline. After discussing who we do and do not want the team to target, now we’re considering whether or not the front office might have any surprises in store for fans. […]
full_text: We’ve been looking at rumors concerning the Chicago Bears and general manager Ryan Poles being looking to add to the roster before the trade deadline. After discussing who we do and do not want the team to target, now we’re considering whether or not the front office might have any surprises in store for fans. Who would shock you the most as a trade target? Lester Wiltfong: I wouldn’t expect a high-priced player like Vita Vea or Maxx Crosby, so that would be a surprise, but for shock value, trading for anything besides a defensive lineman would be a shocker. Bryan Orenchuk: It would shock me if we landed someone like Maxx Crosby. Not only are the Raiders playing well, but he’s a big reason why and is playing at an incredibly high level so he’ll cost way too much IMO. Erik Duerrwaechter : Maxx Crosby. At this point, the Raiders have made it clear they’re playing for this season as well as their future. However… they’ve also traded him away once already. As a result, no trade discussions can truly be shut down. I just do not think Ryan Poles, who has admitted to calling in on Mad Maxx’s availability, will be comfortable approaching anywhere close to the Raiders’ demands for two first round picks. Donald Gooch : Jeffrey Simmons. The Titans just re-signed him to a huge contract. And fitting him under the cap this year would require multiple restructures, not to mention at least a 2nd round pick in 2027 (if not more). That said, the Titans are 0-4 and the odds Simmons is still a plus player when the Titans are relevant again seems low. But man – what a move that would be for this Bears team. Mongo Peanut: I would be most shocked by any offensive addition. The offense looks deep and talented, and I don’t see Poles using future assets for offensive players when they need to be used for reinforcing the defense. Josh Sunderbruch : I would be shocked to see Chicago pursue another marginal player of the sorts they’ve traded for in the past. I feel like the peripheral tinkering on this roster should really be done at this point, and if Poles is going to make a move, it will be a meaningful one. So, those are the moves that would surprise us. Let us know in the comments if anything could shock you regarding pending moves from the Beloved.

title: Tyson Bagent to start for the Chicago Bears, unless he doesn’t
summary: The only thing we should expect from Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson is to expect the unexpected. Last week against the New York Jets, all signs pointed to Tyson Bagent getting the first start since he was a rookie in 2023. There were even a couple of prominent NFL insiders who broke the news […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears looks to pass during the second half of the game against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The only thing we should expect from Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson is to expect the unexpected. Last week against the New York Jets, all signs pointed to Tyson Bagent getting the first start since he was a rookie in 2023. There were even a couple of prominent NFL insiders who broke the news that Bagent took the majority of the first-team reps during the week of practice, so obviously, it would be Bagent. Only it wasn’t. Well, it sort of wasn’t, because Bagent did start, but Case Keenum also started, and since Keenum took the snap, the official record books show that the 38-year-old Keenum started a second consecutive game at quarterback for the Bears. Johnson said he opened the game that way because reports leaked about their intention to start Bagent. “Well, I got all these memos saying that Tyson was starting before I ever made an announcement, so I wanted to get Case out there,” Johnson said in his postgame press conference. “It was like his ceremonial first pitch out there. Handing off the torch.” That brings us to Sunday’s Bears clash with the Green Bay Packers. Johnson said earlier in the week that Bagent would start, and he still may, but Caleb Williams returned to practice today for the first time since injuring his hamstring on September 20, and his game status is officially questionable. Before Williams was limited at today’s practice, Johnson met the media and discussed what Williams has been doing earlier in the week. “We’ve got him progressively increasing the amount of running that’s going on, and of course the throwing aspect of it is a big part of his position as well,” Johnson said. “Our guys have a good plan in place, and we’re just going step-by-step with that right now. Every couple of days we’re getting this throwing protocol in and making sure there are no setbacks. So far, so good.” I assume Ben knew Caleb would get some actual practice time in, but I also assume he’s not quite ready. But this is a great step towards him getting in more side work this weekend, and then if he’s cleared to practice in full, he’ll be in line to start the Week 6 game in Atlanta. The line at FanDuel Sportsbook hasn’t moved (it’s still Packers +1.5), so the oddsmakers don’t think Chicago will get its QB1 back on Sunday in Green Bay, but this latest development may prompt the Packers to address that possibility.

title: Bengals trade candidates listed by PFF ahead of deadline
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are heading to Miami this weekend to look for a win over the Dolphins before the bye week. The Bengals are currently 2-2 but have the opportunity to get back in the win column against a Dolphins team that has yet to win a game this season. As improved as this roster […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are heading to Miami this weekend to look for a win over the Dolphins before the bye week. The Bengals are currently 2-2 but have the opportunity to get back in the win column against a Dolphins team that has yet to win a game this season. As improved as this roster is in 2026, there are still plenty of spots that can be improved before the trade deadline this season. PFF recently shared 15 trade candidates ahead of the deadline , and the Bengals were listed as possible fits for a few names. The first name is Tampa Bay Buccaneers corner Zyon McCollum, a name that has fallen down the CB rankings recently. “McCollum enjoyed a tremendous start to the 2024 season, but since then, his production has certainly waned. Over the first four games of 2026, McCollum sports just a 58.3 PFF coverage grade, although his passer rating against (80.4) and forced incompletion rate (13.3%) are both in at least the 60 th percentile. “In the first year of a three-year, $48 million extension, McCollum is another defender the Buccaneers could look to shed. The Steelers could reunite McCollum with Jamel Dean after trading away Porter, while the Lions urgently need more talent in their secondary. The Bears and Bengals could also make particular sense given McCollum’s superior man coverage work (69.4 PFF coverage grade) and their higher rates of utilizing the look, although McCollum was actually better in zone in 2024 and 2025. Raiders general manager John Spytek may make some calls to his former organization, too.” Another name the Bengals are listed as possible fits for is New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens. “Stephens has become an effective cornerback since joining the Jets last offseason. Since the start of 2025, his 70.2 overall PFF grade ranks 14 th out of 40 qualified corners. Stephens has also tightened up his coverage this year, with his 74.4 PFF coverage mark the ninth-highest at the position. “How much the 1-3 Jets will sell is unknown, but general manager Darren Mougey always seems open for business. Given that Stephens is a 2028 free agent and the team drafted D’Angelo Ponds in the second round, a trade may not be that implausible. Pittsburgh and Detroit could have interest given their needs, while Stephens’ 88.7 man coverage grade would be enticing to Chicago and Cincinnati.” Although it is unlikely for the Bengals to make a trade for a defensive player during the season based on their history, the defense could use a veteran linebacker, as well as some secondary help. What do you think about these names as potential trade options for the Bengals? Let us know in the comments section!

title: Ventrell Miller not fined or suspended for hit on Ja’Marr Chase; Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy fined
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are gearing up for a must-win game against the 0-4 Miami Dolphins this weekend. The Bengals are coming off a frustrating loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last weekend, which was full of penalties from start to finish. The NFL officially handed out fines from this game, and there are quite a few… […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are gearing up for a must-win game against the 0-4 Miami Dolphins this weekend. The Bengals are coming off a frustrating loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last weekend, which was full of penalties from start to finish. The NFL officially handed out fines from this game, and there are quite a few… The Bengals’ Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy were fined $11,941 each for facemask infractions, while the Jaguars’ Travon Walker was fined $11,941 for taunting. The Jaguars’ Jarrian Jones was fined $8,201 for his facemask against Ja’Marr Chase. However, the real story is that the hit by Ventrell Miller on Chase that caused the concussion was not fined by the league office, and he won’t be suspended either. As for Jones, he was fined less money for his facemask on Chase, which helped lead to him being knocked out of the game by Miller, than both Mafe and Murphy’s infractions. It is surprising to see that Miller was not fined for his dangerous hit on a defenseless player, but the NFL felt a fine was not needed. Luckily, Chase is currently trending to play against the Dolphins as long as he officially clears concussion protocol. Moving on.

full_text: Everyone knows that winning quarterbacks and head coaches get too much credit, and those on the losing side generally take too much blame. For the Cleveland Browns’ 3-1 start to the 2026 NFL season, credit has been spread around to HC Todd Monken , the stellar defense , and GM Andrew Berry’s last two great draft classes . While it might be a little early to have big playoff conversations , the Browns start has been exciting for fans. QB Deshaun Watson’s revival, from “ what does his contract mean if they cut him ” after the last preseason game to “led three fourth-quarter comebacks,” has been impressive, but his overall performance has been closer to “fine” than the main reason Cleveland has been winning games. According to Mary Kay Cabot, if Watson leads the Browns to the playoffs the team “will certaintly try to re-sign or extend him.” Cabot notes that Watson “has a great relationship with the front office, coaching staff, and his teammates…” as part of the reason an extension could be possible. A long season remains before any of those ifs will be answered, including what Watson’s contract extension could look like. Prior to Cleveland’s good start to the year, most expected Shedeur Sanders to get a chance to show what he has this season before the Browns looked to use their extensive draft capital to address the quarterback position. Now, if the team continues to have success, the 31-year-old Watson could be the plan for the immediate future. Do you think the Browns will extend Watson’s contract? How would you feel if they do? Win today, and the Browns will be guaranteed to be in first […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns have a huge opportunity today when they face the New York Jets. Both teams come into the game heading in opposite directions, as the Browns have won three in a row while the Jets are riding a three-game losing streak. Win today, and the Browns will be guaranteed to be in first place in the AFC North when they take the field next week at home against the Baltimore Ravens. They have to get past the Jets first, of course, and this has the makings of a trap game if the Browns get too full of themselves and overlook the Jets. Cleveland safety Grant Delpit was asked about that possibility on Friday and correctly responded that the Browns are in no position to overlook any opponent given the nature of their close victories and penalty issues . That is the right answer and the right mindset for a team that is slowly learning how to win games, rather than finding ways to lose them. Will it carry over to the field this afternoon? title: NFL predictions: Rain could throw a wrench in Browns-Jets expected matchup advantages
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (3-1) take on the New York Jets (1-3). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Can’t Ignore the Weather The Browns have already had one game make a weather impact this year, that being the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - OCTOBER 29: Fans of the New York Jets celebrate in the rain during the first half of the game against the Atlanta Falcons at MetLife Stadium on October 29, 2017 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (3-1) take on the New York Jets (1-3). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Can’t Ignore the Weather The Browns have already had one game make a weather impact this year, that being the closing moments of their first win of the season in Week 2 over the Buccaneers. It’s about to happen again, although this one is more anticipated. Current weather forecasts are calling for rain before, during, and after the game, so it looks like it’s going to be difficult to avoid. Obviously, that leads to a lot of wildcard factors. Instincts would tell me that an already-solid Browns defense have an even bigger edge over the Jets’ offense now. However, the Browns are also missing two of their defensive tackles in Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. Even though the Jets’ rush offense has not done much this year, what if the weather conditions allow them to churn those tough yards out? And then for the Browns’ offense, will Deshaun Watson be able to maintain his rhythm in the rain, or will he be turnover prone? Now Let’s Try Ignoring the Weather The Browns come into this game as 1.5 point underdogs, but based on the way each team has played, Cleveland has the edge in my book. That doesn’t mean it’s a definitive edge by any means, but I think it’s Cleveland’s game to lose. Want to know how good Denzel Ward is? A week after Ward held the Panthers’ Tetairoa McMillan to 2 catches for 17 yards, McMillan had 14 catches for 192 yards and 2 touchdowns against the Lions. Last week, he had a key interception in the first half that swung the momentum to Cleveland. Ward’s mission this week? Shutting down Garrett Wilson. Wilson leads the team with 24 catches for 270 yards and 2 touchdowns. Besides a game against the Lions — who give up passing yards to everybody — the Jets’ receivers haven’t blown anyone away. It is worth noting that Geno Smith has been playing responsibly at quarterback. He’s completed 72.6% of his passes, with 5 touchdowns and 0 interceptions. It’s still only led to one victory, though. The Browns’ defense sacked him 10 times when he was with the Raiders last year, so hopefully those guys feel like they have a sense of what Smith’s cadence is. Let’s see if Deshaun Watson can keep things up for the Browns. You get the feeling that KC Concepcion , Harold Fannin , and Denzel Boston are threats that teams can’t stop, and I loved seeing Jerry Jeudy get involved late last week. Despite the hate that Jeudy got last year, we know that when he’s at the top of his game, he can make defenses pay. If he is clicking and going against lower-tier cornerbacks, what a weapon that can be. The Browns are calling up DT Sam Kamara and DT Chris Williams from the practice squad this week for some depth at defensive tackle. The Browns’ offensive line has been very impressive overall this year. That doesn’t mean they have Pro Bowlers, as each player seems to do better in one area over the other (either run or pass blocking). Cumulatively, it’s at least an average unit — and for the run blocking, I get the feeling that it’s more of a chemistry-building issue than a talent issue. Even if the running backs aren’t having lots of room on the ground, they are catching the ball well and doing damage there. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 1.5 point underdogs against the Jets. The over/under is 39.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about how the running game can keep improving: “Yeah, I think that we’ve improved every week in that area and in all areas of the run game. It’s very rarely one thing. Right? I think that our guys have really taken to heart the strain and finish piece of it. I think we’re starting to displace the line of scrimmage, right, more and more every week. That’s shown up. I think our ‘backs are getting a little bit more comfortable with the things that we’re doing, and then us as a staff too, especially in year one, there’s going to be a learning curve through the first few weeks, and just continuing to learn about our guys and what they do well and how do we expand in those areas. Right? So, I think it’s all parts of it, but it’s improved every week and we’re going to continue to do that.” Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg talked about the heavier shift to man coverage: “Well, not going to go too deep into what went into it, but as we’re all learning and progressing through the season, it is week to week to week to week in the NFL, and you guys know that. You guys have been covering the NFL. I’ll steal Monk’s (Todd Monken’s) line that it’s constantly under construction. And the truth is each little week is a season, right? Because this thing is a marathon, it’s a grind. And every week you’re trying to find that winning edge. You’re trying to find that winning margin. You’re trying to eliminate the things that can hurt you, build on the things that can help you, and week to week finding your players’ superpowers, finding what can make your players go, what can make your coaches go, and then building on that week to week and then having the humility to say, ‘oh, that didn’t go as we thought, let’s work it back to this way.’ And it’s a credit to our players for constantly trying to find those inches in their game.” Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer talked about not kicking the kickoff in play after the 56-yard field goal last week: “Okay, yes, we would prefer not to kick a touchback in that situation, but the deal is this, it’s a learning experience for me and Andre as well. You have to put yourself in Andre’s shoes and understand he just made a 56-yard field goal, presumably to win the game with 10 seconds left to go in the game. So, his adrenaline, all of his teammates were around him, too. I mean, we’re saying, ‘hey, get to the kickoff huddle, get to the kickoff huddle.’ And he knew what he had to do. And I’ll back up for one second. The great thing that happened was, in the beginning of the game, they won the toss. They deferred and we got a chance to choose the direction in the fourth quarter. We wanted to go that direction. That was the preferred direction to go at the end of the game in the fourth quarter. And so, in that same breath, you have the wind with you in that situation, and going that whole game going that direction, if Andre kicked it pure, it went long, he had a touchback. Yeah, I think he had one touchback before that. And then he said if he hit it, he tried to just baby it and get it down there. That’s when he felt like… so, long story short, that 20-yard window for the landing zone, it shortens when you have a ton of adrenaline, you’ve got the wind at your back, and you’re also thinking to yourself, I don’t want to hit it too short because my guy’s got to cover this kick as well. You know what I’m saying? We don’t want to give up a return in that situation. So, it’s just me and Andre talked about it, and I said, ‘how can we better handle this situation in the future?’ And really, I think it’s taking a couple deep breaths, as simple as that sounds, to take a couple deep breaths, get yourself centered for this next play, and then go on and execute that one. So, me and Andre both, I’ve got to be a better communicator with him and try to calm him down in that moment so that he can perform at a higher level. And he learned from that.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “Even though it’s a different defensive coordinator, I’ve seen much of this Browns’ defense completely lock down offenses in rain storms, so I’m not so concerned about that. However, I also don’t know if I have…
