full_text: Sam Kamara #92 (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Cleveland Browns are heading into Sunday’s game against the New York Jets with some issues at defensive tackle. On Friday, the team ruled out Mason Graham (knee/ankle) and Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), as well as Kalia Davis, who just had his 21-day practice window opened this week after returning from the injured reserve list with a quad injury. That left the Browns with Maliek Collins and the versatile Adin Huntington as the only healthy options, not an ideal situation, but also one that had defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg not making any excuses for this week : “Since we’ve been together as a defensive line and as a team, we go as our engine goes. So that engine is revved up, no matter what. And that’s the great part about Jac (Jacques Cesaire) and the D-line coaches and the men in that room. Like, that’s the Bugatti, man. And that thing goes and goes and goes, and there will never be an excuse or a reason for it not to go. And we feed off that. Not only the way they play, but their personality.” Reinforcements arrived on Saturday as the Browns have elevated defensive tackles Sam Kamara and Chris Williams from the practice squad to the game-day roster. He has 38 tackles and six tackles for loss in his career. The 6-foot and 272-pound Kamara originally signed with the Chicago Bears as an undrafted free agent in 2021. He has played in 26 career games, 18 of which have been with the Browns. The 6-foot-2 and 298-pound Williams originally signed with the Indianapolis Colts as an undrafted free agent in 2020. He has played in 44 career games between the Colts (2021 and 2022) and the Chicago Bears (2024 and 2025). He has four sacks, 43 tackles, 10 quarterback hits, and four tackles for loss in his career. Is it an ideal situation? No. But Rutenberg and the defensive staff likely had a good idea that Graham and Hall would not be able to go this week, so hopefully they came up with a plan to negate the absence of two of their best defensive tackles.

title: What the stats really say about the Cowboys playoff chances
summary: We know that 26% of teams that started 2-3 from 2020 through 2025 eventually made the playoffs. But does 2-3 accurately describe the 2026 Cowboys? As it currently stands, there is no chance this team makes the playoffs. Instead, the lowly Giants currently look to be the NFC East favorite right now – not because […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 8: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys leaves the field following the team's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images We know that 26% of teams that started 2-3 from 2020 through 2025 eventually made the playoffs. But does 2-3 accurately describe the 2026 Cowboys? As it currently stands, there is no chance this team makes the playoffs. Instead, the lowly Giants currently look to be the NFC East favorite right now – not because they have a better roster, far from it, but simply because they are better coached. But how bad are the 2-3 Cowboys really? In statistics, the relationship between two variables is called a correlation, and the strength of that correlation is measured by the “correlation coefficient”. This coefficient (r²) is expressed as a number between 0 and 1. The closer the r² number is to 1, the stronger the relationship between the two variables. The closer it is to zero, the weaker the relationship. In 2025, the metrics most strongly correlated with wins in the NFL were Points differential (r² = 0.845) EPA/Play differential (r² = 0.76) Passer Rating differential (r² = 0.68) Conveniently for us, all three can be used to calculate projected wins. Points differential : Last week , the Pythagorean win projection (essentially a souped up version of points differential), adjusted for the games already played, showed the Cowboys as a 9.2-wins team. Five games into the season, the Cowboys have now scored 138 points and allowed 136. The Pythagorean projected wins for that stat line: 8.6 wins, and adjusted for the games already played: 8.1 wins. EPA/Play differential : One of the interesting things about both EPA/Play and Passer Rating Differential is that they can both be plugged into a very simple formula to predict win totals in the NFL. The EPA/Play formula (Projected Wins = EPA Differential * 25 + 8.5) based on a 0.158 offensive EPA/Play and a .182 defensive EPA/Play projects the Cowboys for 7.9 wins . Passer Rating Differential (PRD): The PRD formula (Projected Wins = PRD * 0.17 + 8.5) based on a 98.2 offensive passer rating and a 109.6 defensive passer rating projects the Cowboys for 6.6 win s. Prediction markets : A different sort of math, but similar results nonetheless. Kalshi has the Cowboys with 8.7 wins . Predictionmarketspicks.com has the Cowboys with 7.9 wins . The historical numbers give the Cowboys a 26% playoff rate from this position. That’s a useful baseline, but it tells us nothing specific about this team. The three statistical models put Dallas somewhere between 6.6 and 8.1 wins. The prediction markets are in roughly the same neighborhood. That’s not a playoff profile. And if anything, those numbers may be flattering the Cowboys. Seven or eight wins looks like a reasonable statistical baseline. But depending on your eye test, even that might be optimistic. Let us know if you think there is any chance they can turn this around, or are they going to miss the playoffs again?
author: One Cool Customer

title: The Cowboys coaching decision no one is talking about
summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost on Thursday night. It remains incredibly frustrating. If I asked you for the most contentious decision that the coaching staff made in the process, you would likely bring up the decision that Brian Schottenheimer made to go for two when down by eight in the fourth quarter. This particular author supported […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 8: Brandon Aubrey #17 of the Dallas Cowboys warms up against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers prior to an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys lost on Thursday night. It remains incredibly frustrating. If I asked you for the most contentious decision that the coaching staff made in the process, you would likely bring up the decision that Brian Schottenheimer made to go for two when down by eight in the fourth quarter. This particular author supported that for what it’s worth, just about the only thing I endorsed from Schottenheimer throughout the loss. While that decision has inspired a lot of responses there is another Cowboys coaching decision that merits discussion. This one came much earlier in the game. Almost halfway through the second quarter, Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb failed to connect on a 3rd and 10. It was 4th and 10, obviously, and the Cowboys chose to punt. The thing is the Cowboys were on the Tampa Bay 47-yard line. They turned down a 64-yard field goal attempt, something that Brandon Aubrey is regarded to be very good at. Aubrey hasn’t exactly been super reliable on these as of late, though. He had a 59-yard attempt blocked by the Baltimore Ravens, and a week later he had a 62-yard attempt blocked by the Houston Texans. Schottenheimer also chose to have Aubrey attempt a 65-yarder against Houston on the possession after the block and he missed it outright. In the week after the game, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans talked about how they were partly able to block the kick they did because of something they saw on film from Dallas’ game against Baltimore. DeMeco Ryans details how the Texans saw the Ravens blocked kick vs the Cowboys and moved Will Anderson Jr. inside like they did when he blocked a FG in 2023 vs JAX pic.twitter.com/Dbdyc3wm7E — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) October 7, 2026 You never want to see this kind of thing. It looks bad on the Cowboys, it looks bad on Schottenheimer, and it specifically looks bad on special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen. Did those two blocks occupy some rent in the Cowboys’ minds on the decision to not let Aubrey attempt the 64-yarder against Tampa? It is hard to say not. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram’s Nick Harris pulled the last time that Dallas punted from across the 50-yard line and it was midway through last year, but the last time they punted from inside of the 47-yard line specifically was late in the 2024 season. It is worth noting that by that time in that season Dak Prescott was out for the year already so the calculus was a bit different. Last time: Week 7 2025 vs. WAS (punted from the WAS 49) Last time it was punted from the 47-and-in: Week 13 2024 vs. NYG (punted from the NYG 47 and the NYG 45) — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) October 9, 2026 To be clear, it is impossible to say with full certainty that the Cowboys punted because of a lack of faith in any one person or side of the ball. But it is certainly a legitimate theory. That particular decision was hardly costly. The Buccaneers went on the punt themselves so there was no blood drawn. But what if Aubrey had attempted the 64-yard attempt? What if he had made it? Then the Cowboys could have gone for two when they did in an effort to make the game (at that time) a three-point contest. And if they had gotten it, they didn’t get it as we all know, then they would have only needed a field goal to tie at the end of regulation. That is a lot of ifs and hypotheticals, but they rest on the decision that Dallas made to not have Brandon Aubrey attempt the field goal. What do you think? Was it a lack of faith? Or something random?

title: NFL Week 5 gambling preview: Bet on Trevor Lawrence, plus other picks
summary: The fifth Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will be here soon. It’s time to sit back, relax, and enjoy some football. Before the third Sunday festivities of the year kick off, here are our gambling picks for the Week 5 slate. All odds via FanDuel Sportsbook. Three Picks of the Week 2026 Record: […]
full_text: (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images The fifth Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will be here soon. It’s time to sit back, relax, and enjoy some football. Before the third Sunday festivities of the year kick off, here are our gambling picks for the Week 5 slate. All odds via FanDuel Sportsbook . Three Picks of the Week 2026 Record: 3-5 1) Trevor Lawrence OVER 14.5 rushing yards (-110) Trevor Lawrence hasn’t been using his legs much to start this season, but we will see that change this week. Lawrence and the Jaguars face off against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. While they are currently dealing with a plethora of injuries, the Eagles still have plenty of healthy talent on the defensive side of the ball. Philly’s ability to get after the quarterback has forced opposing quarterbacks to run against them at a high rate. In four games this year, the Eagles have seen quarterbacks run the ball 16 times against their defense. I think we see that trend continue Sunday as Lawrence uses his legs to escape some sacks and pick up extra yardage. Take the over on his rushing yards. 2) Cincinnati Bengals/Seattle Seahawks ML (+106) Both the Bengals and Seahawks are in great spots in Week 5. Cincinnati is going up against arguably the worst team in football, the Miami Dolphins, with Seattle facing off against a San Francisco 49ers team due for some regression in a tough road matchup. While the 49ers are 4-0, two of their wins have come against the Cardinals and Dolphins. Those blowout victories have overinflated their value, and we will see the defending Super Bowl champs bring them down a peg on Sunday afternoon. Take both Cincinnati and Seattle to win on Sunday. 3) Jayden Daniels 30+ rushing yards (-125) After suffering an elbow injury in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will make his return to the lineup this week against the New York Giants. When healthy, one thing Daniels has done consistently well during his NFL career is use his legs to his advantage. Washington’s quarterback has recorded 30 or more rushing yards in 20 of the 26 regular season games he has played in throughout his career. This week Daniels should be able to continue that trend against this Giants’ defense. Player Prop Best Bet Jeremiyah Love OVER 2.5 receptions (-102) Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love’s NFL career hasn’t gotten off to the best start, but the number three pick faces a favorable matchup this week against a dreadful Detroit Lions defense. In his four games as a pro, one thing Love has consistently done is catch the ball out of the backfield. The 21-year-old has 11 receptions in four games, recording two or more in a single game three times. The Lions defense came into Week 5 last in the league in passes completed against and first downs allowed, making this a good spot to bet on the Notre Dame product. Love should be able to get involved through the air against a poor Lions’ defensive unit. Take his over on receptions in this one. title: 2026 Week 5 rooting guide for Cowboys fans
summary: If you’re taking the weekend off from the NFL after Thursday night’s debacle in Dallas, we don’t blame you. But for those who still want football in their lives this Sunday, and still care about the Cowboys’ prospects for 2026, this rooting guide’s for you. With the Cowboys now 2-3, we’re getting perilously close to […]
full_text: Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If you’re taking the weekend off from the NFL after Thursday night’s debacle in Dallas, we don’t blame you. But for those who still want football in their lives this Sunday, and still care about the Cowboys’ prospects for 2026, this rooting guide’s for you. With the Cowboys now 2-3, we’re getting perilously close to the point where we’ll need other games to go our way to make the playoffs. Maybe Dallas gets healthy and rested and goes on a run, but that’s hard to wrap your head around after they messed the bed against the winless Bucs. Controlling our own destiny is little more than a pipe dream at this point, so let’s start digging into the Sunday slate for Week 5 and what’s best for the Cowboys. NFC East teams Jaguars d. Eagles Commanders d. Giants You can start your football Sunday early this week with the Eagles-Jaguars game in London. Philly’s dropped two in a row and the 3-1 Jaguars, who are much more accustomed to transatlantic travel, could easily make it three. Trevor Lawrence is playing better QB so far this season than Jalen Hurts, which may be the deciding factor. We would gladly move into a tie with the Commanders if it means they put a loss on the 3-1 Giants. Jayden Daniels is expected back for this division rivalry game, which is a huge factor in Washington’s (and the Cowboys’) favor. Coming out of this week with Dallas, Philadelphia, and Washington all at 2-3, and New York at just 3-2, would make the Cowboys’ prospects in the NFC East look so much brighter. NFC vs. NFC Packers d. Bears Saints d. Vikings Cardinals d. Lions 49ers d. Seahawks It’s only Week 5, so we’re not going with a draft-focused mentality just yet. You still want to see NFC contenders taking hits, especially if they’re a potential Wild Card team. That’s why we’re taking the 2-2 Packers over the 3-1 Bears, even if we’re invested in Green Bay’s 2027 first-round pick. The Vikings are 4-0 but there’s still plenty of time for them to slip out of that NFC North lead. New Orleans doesn’t feel like much of a threat, so it’s better they put a loss on Minnesota. The same goes for Arizona-Detroit, where a Lions’ loss is likely to be far more helpful to Dallas down the road. With the Niners at 4-0 and the Seahawks at 3-1, you could make a case either way. But right now, San Francisco feels like the team that’s going to finish first in the NFC. If they do end up at least taking the NFC West, if not the whole conference, you’d rather have Seattle be easier to catch in the Wild Card race. NFC vs. AFC Ravens d. Falcons Bills d. Rams There are only two interconference matchups this week. Both Atlanta and Los Angeles are 2-2 right now, and we have no skin in the results for these AFC teams. So these are easy picks against our NFC rivals. Also, the 2-2 Carolina Panthers are on an early bye this week. AFC vs. AFC Colts d. Steelers Raiders d. Patriots Cowboys fans can take interest in these AFC games, as we own picks from the Steelers and Patriots in 2027. Pittsburgh’s fourth-rounder is coming to us from the Broderick Jones trade, and New England’s seventh comes to by way of Houston and the trade for OT Nate Thomas.

title: Cowboys vs Buccaneers: George Pickens finds his rhythm in tough loss
summary: It’s fair to say Thursday night’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was one of the Dallas Cowboys’ worst regular-season performances of the last two decades. Dallas came into the game as 8.5-point favorites and ended up losing 24-16 to a winless Buccaneers team. As has been a theme all season, Dallas’ defense was once […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s fair to say Thursday night’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was one of the Dallas Cowboys’ worst regular-season performances of the last two decades. Dallas came into the game as 8.5-point favorites and ended up losing 24-16 to a winless Buccaneers team. As has been a theme all season, Dallas’ defense was once again unable to stop a nosebleed in this matchup. Tampa moved the ball up and down the field with ease all night long, recording 419 yards of total offense and outscoring Dallas 17-6 in the second half. At this point in time, the only way the Cowboys seem to be able to win games is if their offense plays the hero and carries them to a victory. Unfortunately for Dallas, unlike last weekend in Houston, their offense was not able to get going on Thursday night. The Cowboys struggled against the Buccaneers’ defense that blitzed at a high rate and had Dallas’ offense looking out of sync for most of the night. While the offense did not play well as a whole, there was one player who had far and away his best performance of the season. That guy was wide receiver George Pickens. For the first time this season, the 25-year-old looked like the guy we saw throughout the entirety of the 2025 campaign, earning him this week’s game ball award. Pickens finished the game with nine catches for 130 yards and a touchdown, all season highs. Pickens’ 83.0 Pro Football Focus receiving grade was the highest of any wideout in the contest, as was his 43 YAC. SIX FOR PICKENS @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/h3gLE06eDP — NFL (@NFL) October 9, 2026 #GeorgePickens #George #Pickens #DallasCowboys #DakPrescott #Dallas #Cowboys #Dak #Prescott #Qb #WR pic.twitter.com/3cjPOOKic4 — Ball In Sports Net (@BallInSportsNet) October 9, 2026 This performance was the type of game we expected to see on a consistent basis from George Pickens this season. While it may have taken him a few weeks to get his feet wet, Thursday’s night’s performance may have been a sign of things to come for the 25-year-old wideout. If the Cowboys offense wants to be GOTI, as they’ve deemed themselves, they need Pickens to be playing at a consistently high level like he was last season. We’ll see if Dallas can use Thursday night’s performance from the wideout as a building block to get him playing at a high level once again.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Brian Schottenheimer is getting the least wins out of Dak Prescott
summary: Dak Prescott is a quarterback that you can win with. Operating as if this is the case, the current Dallas Cowboys head coach is proving to be the outlier in that respect. Brian Schottenheimer is the third head coach that Prescott has had in his now 11-year career, and he is far and away the […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dak Prescott is a quarterback that you can win with. Operating as if this is the case, the current Dallas Cowboys head coach is proving to be the outlier in that respect. Brian Schottenheimer is the third head coach that Prescott has had in his now 11-year career, and he is far and away the one getting the least wins out of him. This is striking when you really think about it. Whatever your thoughts are/were on Jason Garrett and/or Mike McCarthy, the 2026 version of Prescott is more advanced than any that either had to work with. Schottenheimer has at the very least one of the best versions of Dak and he is somehow, some way, converting that into fewer wins than either of his predecessors. Schotty is down to 39% now. Dak has been healthy for all 22 games of the Schottenheimer era. Dallas has won 9 of them. https://t.co/DpOvqrZnJY — Tim Timothy (@NoMoreMisteaks) October 9, 2026 It is striking how similar the win rates were between Garrett and McCarthy when Prescott was under center. Obviously the full iterations of their Cowboys teams were different, and McCarthy had some incredible defenses on the other side of the ball to balance things out. That is clearly where Schottenheimer is at the biggest disadvantage. How big of a disadvantage is that? Schottenheimer is an offensive guy and the offensive play-caller, but his responsibilities don’t end on the offensive side of the ball. Matt Eberflus was essentially chosen for him to be his first defensive coordinator, but he hand-picked Christian Parker and that hasn’t looked better so far. Football is a game of balance so the defenses matter here, but it remains true that Schottenheimer is so far proving to be the least able to convert Prescott-led teams into wins at the same rate as either of the other coaches who Prescott played for. This is a serious problem. What is particularly difficult to take is that Prescott has had full health in the Schottenheimer era. He had full health for his days with Jason Garrett too, Garrett struggled without Tony Romo when he was the starting quarterback, and Mike McCarthy famously made things work with Cooper Rush. We can point at the very least to that as something that separates McCarthy from Garrett and specifically Schottenheimer in this particular conversation. It is all frustrating. And it is admittedly a little bit of cherry-picking. But these conversations are ringing louder than ever on the heels of Thursday night’s loss. The demerits are the only things that people see and right now they are hovering around Brian Schottenheimer. That’s what comes with the territory.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys vs. Buccaneers Stock Report: Coaches, players almost universally downgraded
summary: The Dallas Cowboys inexplicably lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night. It remains impossible to believe. Unfortunately we have to wait a little bit before the Cowboys have a chance at redemption. Such is the issue with losing on a Thursday. We have a lot of time to sit and think about what […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys inexplicably lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night. It remains impossible to believe. Unfortunately we have to wait a little bit before the Cowboys have a chance at redemption. Such is the issue with losing on a Thursday. We have a lot of time to sit and think about what we were all subjected to during the only home game at AT&T Stadium throughout the month of October. As we do, let’s check out our stock report following the Buccaneers loss. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer It is often said that short weeks either highlight or expose a head coach for what he does to have his team ready to go. Brian Schottenheimer in no way had the Dallas Cowboys ready to go. You can make an argument that he has rarely had the team ready to go in any given week this season. We are approaching mid-October of his second season at the helm and the Cowboys have only been above .500 once under his leadership. The defense is and has been bad and all of that jazz, but the head coach has to find a way. He has not. Stock Down: Christian Parker Have we, at any point, felt like we got what we thought we did with Parker? There is an argument to be made that Christian Parker is the most disappointing person across the entire NFL so far this season, at least relative to expectations. Consider the level of impossibility that he would be so similar to Matt Eberflus in results. Stock Down: Dak Prescott The end of the game was interesting, but the burying on the way there was a big issue. To be clear, Dak doesn’t deserve stock down for his interceptions. Tipped balls are not the quarterback’s fault. But not being able to move the Greatest Offense There Is repeatedly and allowing the hole to be dug is. Prescott took way too long to get going and the team as a whole suffered as a result. Stock Down: DaRon Bland There isn’t much to say that hasn’t been said right now. It is bad. It is historically bad. It is unbelievably bad. Sigh. Stock Down: Nick Sorensen It is possible that they didn’t let Brandon Aubrey attempt a 64-yard field goal out of fear given blocks in the last two weeks. If that is the case then the failures of Nick Sorensen’s special teams group have officially handicapped the team at large. Stock Down: Jake Ferguson I’ve been slower to jump at the idea that Ferguson is really limiting the team, but this game was a really bad look for him. Clearly the tipped pass at the end was a breaking point. It may legitimately be time to let Brevyn Spann-Ford have more opportunities. Stock Down: Quinnen Williams The Cowboys paid to have a war daddy on their defensive line and Quinnen Williams has had barely a handful of legitimate moments this season. Against a rookie, undrafted free agent quarterback? Getting no real pressure in his face? This simply cannot happen. Stock Down: KaVontae Turpin It was remarkable that it was his first fumble on a return, but the fumble did happen and it came at a critical time. In a similar way to Quinnen Williams, Turpin hasn’t really provided a real advantage in some time. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy Good for him. This was a great game in a vacuum. But empty calories. Stock Up: Malachi Lawrence The rookie deserves kudos for playing hard. It came in a loss, but perhaps he is a promising point for the future.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: College football’s top Cowboys draft targets in Week 6
summary: It’s never too early to check out draft prospects from the best college football matchups, where a future prospect lurks that could be on the Cowboys radar.  Georgia vs Alabama Georgia and Alabama are both 5-0 and scoring more than 49 points per game. Georgia counters with one of the country’s best defenses, while Alabama […]
full_text: Photo by Perry McIntyre/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images | ISI Photos via Getty Images It’s never too early to check out draft prospects from the best college football matchups, where a future prospect lurks that could be on the Cowboys radar. Georgia vs Alabama Georgia and Alabama are both 5-0 and scoring more than 49 points per game. Georgia counters with one of the country’s best defenses, while Alabama has forced 13 turnovers and already returned four interceptions for touchdowns. This game should expose any weakness because neither team can hide a struggling player from the opponent’s depth and athleticism. Georgia: Ellis Robinson IV, Cornerback Robinson has developed into one of the leading cornerbacks in the 2027 class. The 6-foot, 180-pound junior recorded four interceptions and seven pass breakups during his breakout 2025 season. Through five games this year, he has added nine tackles, four passes defended and another interception. His best quality is his ability to remain connected to a receiver in man coverage. Robinson is patient at the line of scrimmage and his long arms allow him to reach through the receiver’s hands and disrupt the catch without arriving too early. Why The Cowboys Care The trade for Joey Porter Jr. changed the immediate picture at cornerback, but it did not remove every long-term question. Porter arrived after extension talks with Pittsburgh failed, Shavon Revel Jr. has continued to battle injuries, DaRon Bland is showing the limitations to his game, and Dallas has already needed several replacement combinations in the secondary this season. Robinson could give Christian Parker a corner capable of playing tight man coverage or working with his eyes on the quarterback. Pairing him with Porter or Bland would allow Dallas to be more aggressive with its pressure packages because the defence would not need to protect both outside cornerbacks on every passing down. Alabama: Ryan Coleman-Williams, Wide Receiver Coleman-Williams remains one of the most explosive receivers in college football. The 6-foot, 184-pound junior has caught 20 passes for a team-leading 376 yards and four touchdowns through five games. He is averaging 18.8 yards per reception and has scored in three consecutive games. His acceleration is the first trait defenders notice. Coleman-Williams can attack the space behind a cornerback, but his speed is just as dangerous on crossing routes and quick throws. Alabama can move him across the formation and allow him to create yards rather than asking him to run deep on every snap. Why The Cowboys Care CeeDee Lamb remains the center of the Dallas passing game, and with George Pickens playing on a one-year franchise tag, the team cannot negotiate a new contract until after the season. His future will become a major decision in 2027. Coleman-Williams would give Dak Prescott another receiver who changes how a defense positions its safeties. He could stretch the field from outside, or turn a short completion into an explosive gain. His presence would prevent opponents from concentrating all their coverage on Lamb and be an exceptional plan of the team decides to not retain Pickens. UCLA vs Oregon UCLA has built the Big Ten’s most productive rushing attack under its new coaching staff, while Oregon is averaging 47.5 points and more than 500 yards per game. The Ducks will start Dylan Raiola at quarterback because Dante Moore has been ruled out, placing even more responsibility on Oregon’s offensive line. UCLA: Wayne Knight, Running Back Knight followed his coaching staff from James Madison to UCLA after producing 2,039 all-purpose yards in 2025. The 5-foot-7, 193-pound senior has immediately handled the step into Power Four football, rushing 49 times for 445 yards and nine touchdowns through four games. His average of 9.1 yards per carry shows how frequently he has turned a normal running lane into an explosive play. His compact build works in his favour. Knight stays low behind his blockers and changes direction without taking extra steps. He runs with more force than his height suggests and does not regularly fall at first contact. Why The Cowboys Care We all know Javonte Williams is the clear starter, the uncertainty comes behind him. Emari Demercado was waived before the Tampa Bay game, leaving Tyler Goodson as the current backup and keeping the RB2 role unsettled this season and beyond. Knight would offer something different from Williams. Dallas could use his speed on outside runs, screens and option routes while allowing Williams to remain the physical center of the rushing attack. Knight’s return experience could also help him earn an active roster place. Oregon: Iapani Laloulu, IOL Laloulu is the experienced anchor of Oregon’s offensive line. The 6-foot-2, 325-pound senior entered the season with 27 consecutive starts, earned first-team All-America honours in 2025 and was a finalist for the Rimington Trophy as one of the country’s best inside offensive linemen. He allowed only one sack during Oregon’s 15-game season last year. His power and balance are most impressive in pass protection. Laloulu has the mass to absorb a bull rush without being pushed into the quarterback, but he also keeps his feet active enough to react when a defender moves across his face. His experience shows before the snap when he identifies pressure and helps the rest of the line understand its assignments. Why The Cowboys Care Dallas’ offensive line has struggled to provide consistent protection in consecutive games. Tyler Smith’s return helps, but the Cowboys still need better depth and more competition across the line. Cooper Beebe is the starting center, so this would be about strengthening the entire unit rather than replacing anyone. Laloulu could compete at guard, serve as the backup center and give Dallas experienced cover at three interior positions. His pass-protection strength would be particularly useful after the line allowed repeated quick pressure against Houston and Tampa Bay. His center/guard versatility could also protect the Cowboys when injuries force changes.

title: Broncos offense knows it needs to be better
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos know the offense has to get better. That’s one of the reasons head coach Sean Payton made the decision to take back the play-calling duties this week. But it’s all for naught unless the guys on the field execute better, and that includes Nix. There […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - DECEMBER 14: Bo Nix #10 and Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos talk during a time out during the second quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High on December 14, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos know the offense has to get better. That’s one of the reasons head coach Sean Payton made the decision to take back the play-callin g duties this week. But it’s all for naught unless the guys on the field execute better, and that includes Nix. There have been flashes in the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Los Angeles Rams, but it’s not consistent, and it’s not showing up in the first half. The first opportunity to change the offensive tide comes today against the Los Angeles Chargers. “I think running the ball efficiently, the play action passing game, and then the route specifics relative to protection,” Payton said to the media earlier this week. “There’s so much that goes into making his job easier, and then if you’re having trouble, for instance, with early-down efficiency, second-and-nine or third down-and-long, those would be a few that come to my mind right away.” As with any quarterback at this level of play, Nix always feels like he left plays on the field. That’s true for the loss to the San Francisco 49ers. As he said to the media earlier this week: “There’s never been a game that I’ve played that I didn’t want to have a couple back. There were a couple of plays where I wanted to make a throw, or maybe not pull the trigger or throw it to somebody else. That’s just unfortunately what I’ve learned, is that you could play out of your mind, and I’d still go home thinking about one or two plays that are just driving me crazy. “So it’s sort of a never-satisfied game, and that’s one thing you have to be careful with this job, is working so hard and not ever being satisfied. For us, obviously, it’s all about winning. It’s all about putting our team in the best situation possible. So, for me, there are definitely several things that I want to change, and I want to get better at. That’s going to happen. It’s going to come over time.” What helps Nix is his fearless approach to making plays. If we can see the Nix that we saw in the win over Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, which also happens to be the last time Payton called plays with Nix at quarterback, that would be a refreshing development. “It’s the hardest thing, in my opinion, about playing the position because as soon as you make one throw and it’s picked, then you made a bad decision,” Nix said about not being afraid to take risks. “As soon as you make one and you rip it, and you’re like, ‘Well, I fit it in there, but it probably wasn’t smart.’ Then you’re considered lucky, or you’re a gunslinger. To me, it’s not about the labels. It’s not even the overall outcome. It’s about, ‘What was this play asking for? Did I do my job? Did I not?’ If there’s an accumulation of plays that turns into me throwing the ball 100 times in a game down the field, then I’ll do it. But at the same time, when you consistently watch and if you look at the most successful guys, over and over, they just take completions. They keep the ball moving. They have less footballs on the ground. When it’s there, yes, you hit it, but at the same time, first-and-20, you’re not eager to just drop back and just force something out there. “At the same time, you want to get a positive play and get to second-and-manageable so that you can get to third-and-short. Now sometimes, you miss one, and you’re like, ‘Man, that first-and-20, I was a little too safe because I didn’t want to… We were close to field-goal range. I didn’t want to put the ball in harm’s way. We’re trying to start fast. I want to get for sure a field goal.’ So then it comes back to, ‘I should’ve been a little more aggressive. At the same time, if I’m dumb and I do something stupid, then you all are killing me because I didn’t take the field goal. So at the same time, ‘What does the play ask for? What situation in the game are we? Are we in the fourth quarter and we’re down by eight, and it doesn’t matter, I have to do this anyway?’ Yes, then let’s do it. At the same time, we weren’t in that situation the majority of the game to where it’s just all or nothing, let’s just be dumb. “So at the same time, it’s like I want to be aggressive. I want to be really, when it’s open, let’s hit it. But at the same time, I’ve been gotten too many times trying to do too much. In this day and age, in our offense, I don’t have to be a hero on every play. I don’t have to do too much. Get the ball to (RB) RJ (Harvey), and he’ll run for 20 [yards]. That’s just as good sometimes as throwing it 20 yards in the air. So I’m actively looking at it and seeing where I can grow. The labels and stuff, that’s where you can sort of get caught up in it. If you’re not careful, turnovers may go through the roof, and that’s just not what I need to be doing.” The good news for the Broncos is they’re 2-2 after a brutal schedule to start the season. The hope is that the switch back to Payton as play-caller lights a fire in the offense and the team. Against a division rival that’s winless, you know the Chargers will come out extremely motivated. “From a player perspective, we can always do more,” Broncos receiver Courtland Sutton said to the media. “There are things here and there that we may not be fully … I don’t want to say not dialed in on, but there is a little bit of attention to detail that we need to tighten up as players. As a collective, we need to find a way to maximize the opportunities when they do pop and minimize the lack of attention to detail that may transpire over the course of a full game.” Broncos links

title: Ultimate Fan: Broncos need to get back in sync
summary: Well, ultimate Broncos fans, the football gods were definitely Niners fans last week, but that’s OK, no one is truly a Chargers fan so all should be right with the world in a few days. And helping the Broncos get back to winning ways is a veteran to the UFG — SickBoy67 — who is […]
full_text: Well, ultimate Broncos fans, the football gods were definitely Niners fans last week, but that’s OK, no one is truly a Chargers fan so all should be right with the world in a few days. And helping the Broncos get back to winning ways is a veteran to the UFG — SickBoy67 — who is feeling like most of us…excited for the potential every week but frustrated by slow starts and squandered opportunities. Here’s to reversing that on a road game that always feels like home. And as always, come for the great insight and analysis on the UFG, stay for the superb “favorites” and “why I am a Broncos fan” … always the best stuff here! It's Chargers Week 💪 pic.twitter.com/WaL2GtMwIW — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) October 7, 2026 Week 5: Broncos at Chargers MHR – The Niners outcome wasn’t necessarily unexpected given the challenge, but it was certainly a disappointing result. What are your overall thoughts on the game? SickBoy67: I wasn’t expecting a win, but I was hoping for a closely fought game. The team managed that in the first half, but things slipped away after that. I think I feel the same frustration that most fans feel. I’m sick of the slow starts, and I’d like to see this team play a complete game at the level of competence and intensity that we know they’re capable of. MHR – Sean Payton announced Thursday that he would be taking over play calling. What do you think of this change…good idea? Not great? Doesn’t really matter? SickBoy67: I’m disappointed that Webb is only being given four games, but at the same time, windows close quickly in the NFL and the margins are thin. I can’t say whether things would have been different if Payton had called every game this year because this team has been notorious for slow starts during his time in Denver. We also have to consider the quality of the defenses the team has faced so far. I guess we’ll see how the team responds in the next couple of weeks. MHR – The slow starts keep coming up. Payton says it isn’t a script problem, it’s the little details, and Courtland Sutton said the offense has to tighten up its attention to detail. How frustrated are you with the slow starts, and what has to change on that opening drive Sunday? Do the Broncos get on the board first? SickBoy67: They have to be more effective running the ball, and they have to commit to doing it early. Tampa had an 11 minute opening drive last night. That wears a defense down. As to why it hasn’t been working, I think pretty much every coach and player on offense, with the possible exceptions of Harvey and Bryant, have mud on their hands. MHR – Bo Nix has been the comeback guy but has also had some costly turnovers. This week he faces a Chargers defense that forced five turnovers against Buffalo and still lost the game. Nix says he doesn’t have to be a hero on every play. How confident are you that he takes what the defense gives him and protects the ball? SickBoy67: I’m fairly confident about this aspect of Bo’s game. He’s usually pretty good at protecting the ball and being risk averse. A pretty good argument can be made that he’s been too cautious this year. He hasn’t found his rhythm yet and he often doesn’t look comfortable. MHR – Payton’s keys for the offense were an efficient run game, play action, and early-down success, meaning no more third-and-long. He also called J.K. Dobbins an important piece. Is the run game ready to show up this week? Which back needs to have the biggest day on Sunday? SickBoy67: Well, it would be Dobbins for sure. Harvey has improved as a runner, but he still doesn’t have the best vision for holes. He’s an amazing weapon in space, though. That really leaves Dobbins to do the heavy lifting. So far this season, he hasn’t looked right. I think he’s got some lingering injury issues which are slowing him down. I’m not sure this team will look dramatically better this week, but the Chargers run defense isn’t as scary as some we’ve faced, so there’s always hope. MHR – RJ Harvey had 10 catches last week while Sutton had one. This was partly due to the soft-zone defense, according to the head coach. Do you think it’s a problem that the ball isn’t necessarily getting to our biggest playmakers that often, such as Sutton and Jaylen Waddle? What kind of balance would you like to see between the run and pass game on Sunday and does it matter who is catching the ball? SickBoy67: It’s definitely a problem, but it goes back to taking what the defense gives us. If the running game is ineffective, defenses can put more players into coverage. Then they can play the Fangio zone philosophy of allowing short passes and waiting for the offense to get impatient or make a mistake. We need more balance in the passing game, but that starts having a more effective running game. . @danorlovsky7 details what he would like to see the Denver Broncos' offense improve on 👀 pic.twitter.com/gsxttJnSad — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 8, 2026 MHR – In a bit of a surprise, the Chargers are averaging just 16.8 points a game through four games, so this could be a lower-scoring game. Last year the Chargers rallied from a late double-digit deficit to beat the Broncos 23-20 at SoFi, and the Broncos have struggled to close out games in their last two road matchups with the Chargers. Now they face a winless, desperate team. Will this be a defensive battle, a come-from-behind surge by the Broncos to get a win or should the Broncos dominate this one? SickBoy67: I think this will be a defensive battle because I expect our defense to play well and our offense to continue to have a slow start. I think that they will come alive in the second half, as is usually the case, and pile on the points, though. MHR – Justin Herbert has been sacked 12 times in four games, and injuries forced the Chargers to play four rookies on the offensive line against Seattle. Is this the Sunday the Broncos’ pass rush really shows up (finally)? SickBoy67: Yes. If there’s one unit that will have a ‘get right’ game this week, it’s the pass rushers. My one concern is the corners covering well enough to buy them the time to get home. It’s not that I don’t have confidence in Barron or Abrams-Draine, it’s more that they’re a bit of an unknown commodity as starting boundary corners. MHR – Herbert has also thrown six interceptions to four touchdown passes this season, and Payton raved about young corners Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron for their instincts while Riley Moss and Pat Surtain II are out with injury. Who gets the Broncos’ first takeaway Sunday? How many picks will Herbert throw this week? SickBoy67: Again, we have to see how they do, but my bet would be McMillian or Huff, anyway. Both of these guys have a penchant for impact plays, and Hufanga has learned to catch the football, it seems. MHR – Payton compared McDaniel’s offense to Kyle Shanahan’s, and the Broncos just faced Shanahan’s 49ers. But the Chargers are 0-4, so how worried are you that McDaniel attacks this Vance Joseph’s defense the same way he did with the Dolphins in 2023? What is the best way for the Broncos’ defense to keep Justin Herbert in check? SickBoy67: I’d be fine with him attacking it the same way because I think it would blow up in his face. In 2023, Vance was trying to marry his system with a lot of the verbiage and concepts of the Fangio system in order to make the players more comfortable. He admitted afterwards that it was a huge mistake because it had the opposite effect. Although the defense has taken a step backward so far this season, they are a more talented and accomplished unit than the one McDaniel faced in 2023. MHR – Which Chargers offensive player scares you the most – Herbert, Ladd McConkey or Quentin Johnston through the air, or the running back committee? SickBoy67: McConkey. He just always seems to be open and to make a big play when they need one. It’s possible that he won’t play this week, so that should make life a bit easier. MHR – Which ONE player on offense and ONE player on defense has to…

title: Broncos vs. Chargers: 3 Players to Watch in Week 5
summary: Sunday’s battle against the Los Angeles Chargers will be a key divisional matchup for the Denver Broncos. It’s an opportunity for them to get back on track after their Week 4 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. In order to do so, these three players need to step up and play at a high level. […]
full_text: Sep 7, 2025; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos cornerback Jahdae Barron (23) after the game at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sunday’s battle against the Los Angeles Chargers will be a key divisional matchup for the Denver Broncos. It’s an opportunity for them to get back on track after their Week 4 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. In order to do so, these three players need to step up and play at a high level. Jahdae Barron — Cornerback The Broncos lost both Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss last week due to injury. That may pose some problems for their secondary, but thankfully, Denver has several young players with a lot of potential ready to be the next man up. With Surtain out for the next few games it’s time for 2025 first-round pick Jahdae Barron to shine. Many fans across Broncos Country have been critical about Barron’s lack of impact to date. Though it’s really no fault of his own. Can we really blame him for being behind Denver’s top trio of cornerbacks to date? I don’t think that’s necessarily fair. In fact, I remain optimistic about his future with the team. In the second half versus the 49ers, I thought Barron played well. The former Jim Thorpe Award winner may not have the desired length or athleticism at the position, but his football intelligence and ability to make plays on the ball are valuable traits. I assume he will have to go head-to-head against Quentin Johnson for most of the game. Johnson hasn’t made a strong connection with Justin Herbert thus far and is underperforming. Hopefully Barron is able to hold his own against him in coverage. Week 5 isn’t the time to let the former first-round pick to have his biggest impact game of the season. RJ Harvey — Running Back At some point in time, a skill position player will need to become a reliable fulcrum for Denver’s offensive endeavors. They need that on a week-to-week basis in order to win more football games. The Broncos have struggled to put points on the board through three games and have lacked explosive plays. One player I hope can make a big impact on Sunday versus the Chargers is second year running back RJ Harvey. Harvey hasn’t had a lot of opportunities to run the ball this season. However, he had ten catches last week against the 49ers. He is a dual threat player and capable of making game-changing plays. In just three games, Harvey already has 20 receptions on the season. He trails only Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London in yards after the catch. I’d like to see his yard per catch average go up and for him to get a hefty share of carries against a Chargers defense that is bottom ten in the NFL in run defense. We saw flashes of brilliance and Harvey’s top-notch playmaking ability during his rookie season. I’m hopeful he will have a quality outing against Los Angeles on Sunday. I expect him to be a big part of the team’s offensive game plan. Nik Bonitto — Edge Rusher Over the past two seasons, the Broncos have boasted the best pass rushing defense in the NFL. So far this year, they only have eight sacks and haven’t looked quite up to par. Earlier this week, I wrote about the importance of Denver’s pass rush kicking into high gear. Justin Herbert has been sacked twelve times this season and has thrown six interceptions. Herbert is definitely struggling. Due to that, the Chargers’ offense certainly isn’t firing on all cylinders. They also have a ton of injuries on that side of the ball. Pro Bowl left tackle Rashawn Slater will be out on Sunday and potentially their left guard. That may give edge rusher Nik Bonitto a favorable matchup and opportunity to shine. Bonitto was dominant in 2024 and 2025 posting back-to-back seasons of at least 13 sacks or more. Alas, he hasn’t started off this year on a high note and has just one sack. Without Jonathon Cooper opposite of him, the fifth-year pro has faced a lot of double teams and extra chips to keep him from chasing down opposing quarterbacks with ease. We all know Bonitto can be a dynamic defender that impacts games. I think he finds a way to get back on track against the Chargers on Sunday.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Jack Campbell hit with ‘major’ fine, could result in suspension if repeated
summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was fined $15,930 this week for a hip drop tackle in Sunday night’s game against the Carolina Panthers. On the surface, it’s not that big of a deal, as Campbell just got paid, and he can more than afford the penalty. However, the NFL has a new rule that could […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 04: Tetairoa McMillan #4 of the Carolina Panthers is tackled by Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions during the first half of a football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was fined $15,930 this week for a hip drop tackle in Sunday night’s game against the Carolina Panthers. On the surface, it’s not that big of a deal, as Campbell just got paid, and he can more than afford the penalty. However, the NFL has a new rule that could eventually result in Campbell being suspended . Starting this year, if a player commits a “major” foul three times, they will serve a one-game suspension. This rule is only in place for a very small set of infractions, aimed at targeting player safety. The five fouls that fit into this category are: Hip drop tackle Horse collar tackle Launching Hit on a defenseless player Blindside block Simply put, if at player commits a combination of three fouls in any of these categories, they will serve a one-game suspension. Per the NFL, these offenses will carry forward to subsequent seasons, as well. That said, all of these fines are subject to an appeal, if desired. Here is video of Campbell’s illegal tackle (no penalty was called on the play): Jack Campbell’s hip drop tackle that he was fined $15,930 for. pic.twitter.com/ZtmU3NJ4ww — Jeremy Reisman (@DetroitOnLion) October 10, 2026 Here is what the rulebook says about a hip drop tackle: ARTICLE 18. HIP-DROP TACKLE. It is a foul if a player uses the following technique to bring a runner to the ground: (a) grabs the runner with one or both hands or wraps the runner with both arms; and (b) unweights himself by swiveling and dropping his hips and/or lower body, landing on and/or trapping the runner’s leg(s) at or below the knee In addition to Campbell’s fine, Detroit tight end Brock Wright was also fined $17,911 for a leg whip. That is not one of the categories that would have Wright subject to a fine if he is a repeat offender.

title: Detroit Lions use final practice squad elevation on veteran safety
summary: The Detroit Lions made just one roster move ahead of their Sunday afternoon tilt with the Arizona Cardinals, and it’s a familiar one. They have elevated veteran safety Jalen Mills from the practice squad. This is the third straight week Mills has been elevated while the team navigates a shorthanded secondary that still has Avonte […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 04: Jalen Mills #27 of the Detroit Lions looks on before a football game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions made just one roster move ahead of their Sunday afternoon tilt with the Arizona Cardinals, and it’s a familiar one. They have elevated veteran safety Jalen Mills from the practice squad. This is the third straight week Mills has been elevated while the team navigates a shorthanded secondary that still has Avonte Maddox (IR), Thomas Harper (IR), and Brian Branch (PUP) unavailable due to injury. Mills didn’t play on his first elevation, but he got four defensive snaps and seven special teams snaps against the Carolina Panthers last week. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Mills is likely to get more playing time against the Arizona Cardinals now that he has been with the team for a few weeks. “I think (Keith) Abney will probably help us out a little bit more here this week. So will Mills. I can see both those guys taking on a bigger role,” Campbell said Wednesday. With three practice squad elevations for Mills, the Lions have now hit the maximum allowed for the veteran safety. That means if they want to play him again, he will have to be signed to the 53-man roster. However, the Lions have a bye next week, and in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers, Detroit is clearly expected Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch to be ready . So Detroit may continue to keep Mills on the practice squad. But if he takes full advantage his opportunity against the Cardinals, Mills could find his way onto the 53 given Detroit’s current struggles at the position.

title: Detroit Lions vs. Arizona Cardinals preview: 3 key stats
summary: The Detroit Lions had started at least 4-1 in each of the previous three seasons. Leading the NFC North pack from the jump was starting to become the norm. Not only have they suffered their earliest second loss since 2022, but both losses came in utterly demoralizing and shocking primetime fashion. Now they appear to […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 22: Trey McBride #85 of the Arizona Cardinals reacts during an NFL football game between the Arizona Cardinals and the Detroit Lions at State Farm Stadium on September 22, 2024 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions had started at least 4-1 in each of the previous three seasons. Leading the NFC North pack from the jump was starting to become the norm. Not only have they suffered their earliest second loss since 2022, but both losses came in utterly demoralizing and shocking primetime fashion. Now they appear to be a team that has lost respect nationally and around the league, a month into the season without having played anything close to a complete game. It was one of the most unenthusiastic weeks to be a Lions fan in recent years following the Bryce Young buzzsaw they ran into in Charlotte. Now they’ll head to the desert to take on the younger LaFleur brother, Mike, needing a get-right victory and a complete four-quarter performance to inspire some hope for the season heading into the much-needed early Week 6 bye. They’ll do so riding a 5-1 record against the Cardinals since 2017, after the Ford family’s franchise went 0-7 in seven matchups with Arizona between 2006 and 2015. The Cardinals have invested heavily in their skill players, with Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, Jeremiyah Love, and Marvin Harrison Jr., and all eyes will be on the Lions defense fighting back and moving past the narrative that they’re the worst defense in all of football. Every team in football has warts right now, so let’s get into my three key stats and matchups for Sunday afternoon’s West Coast business trip and how the Lions can rid themselves of those warts. Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, SumerSports, or Pro Football Focus. Three TEs is a Crowd While the Detroit Lions defense has been inexplicably dysfunctional this season, one thing they haven’t been on a bus straight to Rock Bottom on is defending against 13-personnel. Despite struggling overall in run defense against the Bills and Panthers, they’ve found some success against three tight end sets, allowing only 3.31 yards per rush on 16 attempts, with just one explosive rush allowed. Even against 13-personnel as a pass defense, where the Lions typically match with their base defense, they’ve been effective, allowing 10-of-17 passing (58.8% completion percentage) for 102 yards (6.0 yards per attempt, 12th), a 41.2% success rate (14th), 4.9 yards per catch (13th), and a 5.9% explosive pass rate (14th). All respectable numbers. If they could simply be middle of the pack in most pass-defense metrics, the outlook for their season would be a lot more optimistic than it’s felt in the aftermath of the last two dreary defeats. Most promisingly, the Lions’ pass rush against 13-personnel has generated a 66.7% pressure rate (3rd) and a 9.5% sack rate (8th). Their 13-personnel defensive prowess is important when facing the Cardinals in a post-Drew Petzing world. While Arizona’s 12-personnel usage has sharply declined from 36.2% (3rd) last season to 14.8% under LaFleur, its 13-personnel usage has remained a priority, jumping from 11.0% in 2025 (3rd) to 20.1% (3rd) when deploying Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins, and Hunter Long (with Tip Reiman injured). [Note: Long was placed on IR this week, with veteran Teagan Quitoriano expected to take his place.] The Cardinals’ rushing attack from three-tight-end sets has maintained success, averaging 4.14 yards per rush (t-6th), a 47.2% success rate (14th), and +0.02 EPA/rush (10th). They’re also top 10 in both yards before and after contact per carry, with both Jeremiyah Love (47.6% success rate) and Tyler Allgeier (+0.04 EPA/rush) averaging over 4 yards per carry from 13-personnel. Some of Jacoby Brissett’s best analytical metrics come from his 16 dropbacks (fourth most) when passing out of 13-personnel. He’s 11-for-16 for 90 passing yards (5.6 yards per attempt), two touchdowns, +0.367 EPA/pass (11th), and a 62.5% passing success rate (11th). While it’s a small sample size, the Lions defense needs to chip away and find avenues where it can have success. Being able to defend well on roughly every fifth play when the Cardinals go to 13-personnel would be a step in the right direction toward getting off the field and holding Arizona to field goals instead of touchdowns in the red zone. Death by a Thousand Checkdowns While it’s beneficial for the Lions that Cardinals left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. will miss the game due to injury, leaving either seventh-round rookie Jayden Williams or recently signed Jedrick Wills to man Jacoby Brissett’s blind side, with possibly backup Jon Gaines II filling in for the injury-battling right guard Isaiah Adams, the defense proved Sunday night against the Panthers that a favorable offensive line matchup isn’t always enough. While Detroit’s defensive front can generate pressure and take advantage of porous offensive lines, the back end hasn’t allowed it to fully capitalize. Receivers were running wide open for easy throws from Bryce Young, who also stood strong in the pocket just long enough to deliver backbreaking completions before the rush could get there. The Cardinals’ passing approach could further mitigate the effectiveness of the Lions’ defensive front against Arizona’s below-average offensive line. It’s not a dynamic passing attack, instead operating largely on dinking and dunking, which could provide a foundation for the Lions to keep everything in front of them, clean up their short-pass coverage, and maybe even force a hurried mistake. Among 29 qualifying quarterbacks, Jacoby Brissett ranks last in yards per pass attempt (5.4), 27th in average depth of target (6.10 yards) and average time to throw (2.6 seconds), and 26th in deep-ball rate (5.9% on throws of 20-plus air yards). He’s also tied with Joe Burrow for the second-most throws in under 2.5 seconds (94). All pedestrian and manageable numbers. The Cardinals’ passing offense is by far the least explosive in the league, averaging an explosive pass rate of only 2.6%. The next closest is the Giants at 6.2% (31st), while Arizona’s rushing offense isn’t much better, also ranking last with a 5.6% explosive run rate. The Lions defense ranks bottom five in both explosive pass and run rate allowed, but maybe this Cardinals offensive bunch is one against which they can finally look like a decently taught and executed defense, with all 11 players on the same page and where they need to be. Dan Campbell mentioned the need for his defensive players to be more disciplined this week and also said, “I want our guys to be where they’re supposed to be when they’re supposed to be there.” Perhaps this Cardinals offense is the starter kit Detroit needs to build back toward being bend-but-don’t-break as opposed to simply being broken. Finding Their Roar Drew Petzing should be all too familiar with his former co-worker, Cardinals fourth-year defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, someone who makes chicken salad out of chicken shit with disguised blitzes and simulated pressures. Petzing’s offensive unit has managed to put up points every game, but it hasn’t been as consistent or had as cohesive an approach throughout a game as one would like given its talent. Dan Campbell challenged the offense during multiple media availabilities this week . “We’re not going to be average. We’re going to raise the floor on these guys. Man, we’re going to push them,” Campbell said on local radio. “We’ve got too much offensively right now. Our quarterback’s too good. Our playmakers are too good. And we’ve got a young, hungry offensive line that’s got a ton of room to grow.” Petzing, in what some might call a revenge game against a talent-deficient Cardinals defense, will look to put together his most complete game plan of the season. The Cardinals’ defensive front has some solid…

title: Detroit Lions fan confidence hits record low for the Dan Campbell era
summary: Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook, and asked Detroit Lions fans two questions: After the Week 2 loss to the Bills, confidence that the Lions were headed in the right direction reached an all-time low, dropping below 50% for the first time in […]
full_text: Detroit Lions fans react to a play against New Orleans Saints during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 13, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Earlier this week, we published our latest SB Nation Reacts survey, sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , and asked Detroit Lions fans two questions : Will the Lions beat the Cardinals in Week 5? (weekly question) Are you confident the Lions are headed in the right direction? (recurring poll) After the Week 2 loss to the Bills, confidence that the Lions were headed in the right direction reached an all-time low, dropping below 50% for the first time in the Dan Campbell era. This week’s survey netted even more disastrous results: not only did the confidence poll results absolutely fall off a cliff, but the majority of fans don’t even think the Lions will beat the Cardinals this week, despite being 5.5-point favorites . Let’s take a look at the results of this week’s polls: Normally, I would use this section of the results piece to highlight the comment section of our original article and The Feed post to see fans’ explanations for why they voted the way they did. However, this week the comments were full of complaints—warranted or not—due to an overflow of understandable frustration. I completely empathize with fans’ need for an outlet, and venting online certainly can accomplish that. For those still in search of an outlet, the comment section in this piece is open for discussion. As a reminder, this survey was sponsored by the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook , which currently has the Lions listed at +2500 to win this year’s Super Bowl and as 5.5-point favorites in Week 5 . Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Detroit Lions fans and fans across the country. If you want to receive these surveys by email weekly, you can sign up here .

title: Packers place RB Chris Brooks on injured reserve
summary: The Green Bay Packers announced on Saturday that they have placed running back Chris Brooks, who was leading the backfield in snaps this season until his ankle injury, on the injured reserve. The Packers have already backfilled his position on the team with the addition of Pierre Strong Jr., who was brought up from the […]
full_text: (Photo by Adam Bettcher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers announced on Saturday that they have placed running back Chris Brooks, who was leading the backfield in snaps this season until his ankle injury, on the injured reserve. The Packers have already backfilled his position on the team with the addition of Pierre Strong Jr., who was brought up from the practice squad earlier this week. Moving forward, the team’s running back rotation will include Strong, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson, at least until Josh Jacobs is done fulfilling his time on the commisioner exempt list/suspension list. So far, the NFL has yet to move Jacobs off the exempt list, as they are still deciding whether or not to suspend Jacobs and for how long. With Brooks going on IR, he will miss at least the next four games on the Packers’ schedule. The first game that Brooks is eligible to be activated back to the 53-man roster for will be Week 9 against the New England Patriots. Green Bay did not make a corresponding roster move, and they currently have an open roster spot on the 53-man roster. Notably, the team started practicing receiver Savion Williams, who is designated to return from the injured reserve, this week. It’s possible that the next move the Packers make for their active roster is bringing Williams up in Week 6.

title: Packers Film Room: Week 4 Interceptions and a game-clinching pressure
summary: The Green Bay Packers intercepted Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Jalon Daniels two times in week four and we covered one of them briefly in another article. They nearly had a third interception to end the game but it was overturned to incomplete in replay. It’s still worth breaking down and mentioning. Today we’ll go a […]
full_text: Edgerrin Cooper intercepts Jalon Daniels in the second quarter of week 4. | Evan Siegle, packers.com The Green Bay Packers intercepted Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Jalon Daniels two times in week four and we covered one of them briefly in another article. They nearly had a third interception to end the game but it was overturned to incomplete in replay. It’s still worth breaking down and mentioning. Today we’ll go a bit more in-depth on those three plays and what led to them as the Packers defense dominated the Buccaneers offense. Jalon Daniels made his first start for the Buccaneers in place of the injured Baker Mayfield and went about as poorly as it could for the undrafted rookie quarterback. He made some plays with his legs but was generally off-target and flustered all game long by a defense and defensive coordinator with vastly more experience. First play, 1st quarter, 1st and 10, 7:15 remaining This interception came down to a missed pre-snap read by Daniels. Before the ball was snapped, the defense showed a single-high shell with clear man-coverage indicators, which almost certainly told Daniels he was looking at cover-1. That’s a coverage he should feel comfortable attacking, with only one deep safety and man coverage underneath, he’d have leverage to work with on the outside. The Packers weren’t really disguising their intentions either. Safety Evan Williams began creeping down toward the slot receiver, “capping” him from the top, while Brenton Cox was initially aligned over the slot as though he had him in coverage. That combination is a classic pressure tell. When a second-level defender starts walking down to “cap” a receiver who already appears to be covered, it usually means the man currently lined up on that receiver isn’t staying there. Daniels should have recognized that Cox was likely coming as a fifth rusher off the edge and that Williams was rotating down to take over the slot. That’s exactly how it played out. At the snap, Cox looped inside and got home, collapsing the pocket before Daniels could get through his progression. With pressure in his face, he couldn’t step into the throw and was forced to short-arm it. The ball came out late and without enough velocity, giving Williams the time to read it and undercut the route as the pass arrived. The coverage forced a bad throw that was set off by a chain reaction that started before the snap. Had Daniels identified the pressure look and the likely fifth rusher, he could have adjusted the protection, gotten to a hot answer, or simply known where his free access throw was before the pressure arrived. Second play, 2nd quarter, 2nd and 10, 00:41 remaining This was more of a bad read by Daniels than anything. He was picked off by Edgerrin Cooper just before halftime. Cooper was sitting in the hook zone and didn’t gain too much depth as he read the quarterback. The defense is in a straight cover-2 zone playing spot drop with vision on the quarterback. The Buccaneers are running a Y-cross pass concept. Daniels took a quick 1-step drop back from shotgun and quickly fired the ball to his slot receiver on a short curl route. Cooper, with vision on the quarterback, broke on the pass as soon as Daniels raised his arm to throw. Cooper shot downhill quickly and undercut the pass as it arrived and returned it for 18 yards. Third play, 4th quarter, 4th and 11, 1:34 remaining On the final play of the game for the Buccaneers offense, Keisean Nixon nearly picked off the pass from Daniels as he chucked it blindly over the middle as he was about to be sacked. It was ruled an interception on the field but overturned in replay. The defense is showing an all out pressure front again with single high coverage. It should be an indicator to Daniels that he’s getting some kind of pressure but not all out pressure because the safety isn’t aligned over any receiver. The Packers zone drop out to a 3-under/3-deep zone coverage shell that gets Evan Williams off the left edge of the defense as the free rusher. Williams grabs hold of the quarterback but can’t bring him before Daniels lets go of the pass. Nixon made a diving attempt but couldn’t hang on. It didn’t matter though because it was fourth down.

title: Weekend Musings: The Most Critical Game for the Houston Texans
summary: In one respect, this upcoming game is but one of 17 on the schedule for the Texans. They’ve already played 4, and after this, they still have 12 more. While far fewer matchups than any of their pro sports counterparts (Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, Dash), there are still quite a few opportunities for victory and glory. […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - OCTOBER 04: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans walks off the field after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at NRG Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Houston, Texas. The Cowboys defeated the Texans 34-30. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images In one respect, this upcoming game is but one of 17 on the schedule for the Texans. They’ve already played 4, and after this, they still have 12 more. While far fewer matchups than any of their pro sports counterparts (Astros, Rockets, Dynamo, Dash), there are still quite a few opportunities for victory and glory. Yet, this game, albeit 1/17th of the schedule, might just be the most important game of the season. The Texans, coming into the season as legitimate Super Bowl contenders, sit at 0-4. After yet another last-second lost lead, the Texans face the nightmare prospect of playing out the remaining three months in a lame-duck status. On the surface, if the Texans ever needed the ideal opponent for a “Get Right” game, they have it with the Tennessee Titans. Like the Texans, they sit at 0-4. While not seen as championship contenders, the franchise had hopes for showing marked improvement, especially with the pride of West Columbia, Cam Ward, leading the way. Thus far, that hope hasn’t materialized. Even with a new coaching staff, Ward hasn’t shown any signs of taking that step required for a QB to make it into the top tier of NFL quarterbacks. It is early in the Salah/Daboll regime and QB progression is not always on a steady linear progression, but Ward’s struggles, along with issues all across the roster, have the Titans buried with the Texans at the bottom of the NFL. Houston is not “all dead” for the playoffs, but when they couldn’t hold that lead against the Cowboys (a loss which looks even worse after Dallas’ Thursday Night debacle against Tampa Bay), they fell into the “mostly dead” realm. The 1992 Chargers haven’t been talked about this much since 1992, as they are the sole team to start 0-4 and get a postseason berth. Then again, Houston seemed destined for a lost season at this time last year, when they came into their first matchup 0-3 against…the Tennessee Titans. Last season, that 0-3 mark could have easily been 3-0. This season, they could arguably be 3-1 coming into this matchup, and even against the Bengals, an earlier start cashing in on the scoring opportunities might have the squad 4-0. However, as Bill Parcells would tell you “you are what your record says you are”. Houston stands 0-4, but technically worse than the Titans in the standings, as Houston has a 0-3 mark in conference play vs. the Titans’ 0-2 conference record. No wonder even the Weather Channel would pass on taking this game . Last season, Ryans, long a defensive coach, allowed defensive coordinator Matt Burke to call the defensive plays on the field in an attempt to shake things up for an 0-3 team. That seemed to be a great call (pun somewhat intended), as the defense pitched only the 3rd shutout in franchise history, blasting the Titans 26-0, sparking a 12-2 run that took Houston from also-ran to a playoff spot. This season, the defense has not lived up to the standard of last season, with significant communication issues at the hard of the problems. Ryans, in a move part desperation/part strategic, resumed calling the defensive plays. Will that help out again? We will have to see. As for the criticality of the game, a loss (or even a tie) likely closes the door on what little hope remained for a playoff run/championship. No team has ever started 0-5 to make the playoffs, and only 5 teams ever started 0-5 and finished the year at .500 or better. The only other time Houston started 0-5 was back in that disastrous 2005 season, which saw the Texans finish 2-14. Not that a win will magically trigger a major win streak. After the trek to Nashville, Houston must continue travelling eastward, facing the AFC South-leading Jaguars in London, only to then turn right back around westward to host a Giants team that Houston hasn’t beaten since its inaugural season. As some commentators have noted, the Texans could possibly enter their bye at 1-6. At that point, the main headlines shift to what sort of maneuvering would Houston undergo at the trade deadline to try to stockpile assets for the 2026-27 offseason. Perhaps every game from here on out will be super critical for what slim hopes Houston has for a playoff run. The AFC does not lack for playoff contenders and Houston 0-3 conference start does them no favors. Then again, it seemed that the 0-3 start last season saw Houston doomed for a lost season, which didn’t quite come to pass. Being “mostly dead” means there is still a chance for life, provided the right miracle hits in time. All of that has to start with Sunday’s game in Nashville. Win, and the season still has a pulse. Lose, and you can start searching the 2026 Texans for loose change.
