title: Dolphins rule out four for Sunday’s game against Bengals
summary: The Miami Dolphins have ruled out four players for their Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. The team will miss starters and key players on offense, defense, and special teams. Can they overcome the losses? Will two players return from the reserve lists by Sunday? The injury lists for both teams were released yesterday […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - JULY 30: Miami Dolphins linebacker Robert Beal Jr. (51) warms up during the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on July 30, 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins have ruled out four players for their Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. The team will miss starters and key players on offense, defense, and special teams. Can they overcome the losses? Will two players return from the reserve lists by Sunday? The injury lists for both teams were released yesterday afternoon. Players ruled out: Caleb Douglas continues to miss playing time Rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas caught 7 passes for 113 yards in Miami’s first two games, but has been sidelined with an ankle injury since. The third-round pick was the first of three wide receivers selected by the Dolphins in the 2026 Draft, joined by third-round selection Chris Bell and fifth-round addition Kevin Coleman Jr. Miami is hoping the three receivers can grow together and provide the nucleus for the team moving forward. Douglas, who is dealing with an ankle injury, unfortunately continues to miss playing time as he recovers. Joining Douglas on Miami’s injury report with an “out” designation are edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., tight end Justin Joly, and cornerback Reese Taylor. Beal, like Douglas, was injured during Week 2 and has not played since. The Dolphins’ pass rush seemed to breakout last week against the Minnesota Vikings, with the team recording four sacks, and returning Beal, who has a lingering hamstring injury, to the group would add to the attack. Taylor has a quadriceps injury. He has not seen any defensive snaps this year, but he has been on special teams and his absence leaves a hole there. Joly sustained a concussion this week, but he has already been inactive for much of the season, making one brief special teams appearance in Week 2. For the Bengals, safety Kyle Dugger has been ruled out with a quadriceps issue. Questionable status: Bengals wide receivers, Dolphins running back headline group The story of the week for the Bengals has been the health of their top two wide receivers, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Chase sustained a concussion during Cincinnati’s Week 4 game, while Tee Higgins has injuries to his groin and neck. Both players are questionable for the game, with no clear indication if they will be available. Chase returned to practice on Friday as a full participant after being limited earlier in the week, but he has not officially cleared the league’s concussion protocol that would allow him to play on Sunday. Higgins, according to Cincy Jungle , is expected to warm up with the team to see if his adductor and neck will allow him to play. Cincinnati also listed linebacker Swayze Bozeman (groin), safety Bryan Cook (ankle), and wide receiver Colbie Young (knee) as questionable for Sunday. The Miami side of the injury report includes running back Jaylen Wright, who continues to deal with a foot injury. The Dolphins are still adjusting following the loss of Pro Bowl running back De’Von Achane to a knee injury suffered in Week 3, with Wright and Ollie Gordon II expected to see increased opportunities without Achane on the field. Wright was able to play last week against the Minnesota Vikings, but he only had five carries for seven yards during the game. Miami also listed linebacker Jackson Woodard (ankle) as questionable. Will Miami activate players from their reserve lists? Miami could make some roster moves ahead of Sunday’s game. Defensive tackle Kenneth Grant is on the injured reserve list with a toe injury, but he returned to practice this week and fully participated in Friday’s workout. Cornerback Storm Duck, working his way back from a knee injury sustained last year, is in his second week of practices as he tries to return from the physically unable to perform list. Duck fully participated in the week’s practices. Both players are officially questionable on the injury report. If Miami plans to activate one or both players for Sunday’s game, it must make the roster moves by 4 p.m. Eastern today. The Dolphins’ bye week is Week 6, which could factor into the consideration of whether to activate Grant or Duck. Miami could leave them out of this week’s game to give them two more weeks of preparation before their first game of the year. Players with no game-day designation Both teams listed various players on the injury report during the week, but gave them no game-day designation, indicating they are fully available for tomorrow’s kickoff. For Miami, the list includes long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), wide receiver Chris Bell (knee), cornerback JuJu Brents (heel), tackle Austin Jackson (knee), and safety Dante Trader Jr. (shin). Cincinnati’s list includes defensive tackle Jonathan Allen (rest / knee), safety Jordan Battle (hamstring), linebacker Barrett Carter (ankle), defensive tackle B.J. Hill (rest/Achilles), defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence (rest/wrist), and guard Dalton Risner (knee).

full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - DECEMBER 14: Ben Yurosek #85 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on December 14, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ahead of their Week 5 matchup with the New Orleans Saints, the Minnesota Vikings made a handful of roster moves that we wanted to make sure everyone was aware of. The team took two players who had been placed on injured reserve during the preseason and moved them to the active roster. Those players are tight end Ben Yurosek and center Michael Jurgens. Both of those players saw their 21-day practice windows to return from IR open this week, and apparently the team liked what they saw from both of them enough to bring them back to the active roster. Jurgens, in particular, could provide some depth if the team decides they want to try Blake Brandel back at guard in the absence of Donovan Jackson, who will miss the rest of the regular season after tearing a meniscus last week against Tampa Bay. The Vikings also elevated wide receivers Odell Beckham Jr. and Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad. Both of them were signed this week, with Jones having spent this preseason with the team and coming back following receiving a three-game suspension for violating the league’s substance abuse policy. They could provide insurance after both Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, both of whom were limited in practice on Friday, were listed as “questionable” for Sunday’s game in New Orleans. With both Addison and Jefferson likely to be game time decisions, there’s a chance that both could be active on Sunday. . .or there’s a chance they could both wind up on the inactive list after being elevated. Those will be the last of the moves the Vikings make ahead of Sunday’s game, barring anything out of the ordinary.

full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: T.J. Hockenson #87 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball after a reception against the Miami Dolphins during the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time to bring everyone the results of our SB Nation Reacts polls for this week, so let’s get right to it! As always, the first question we wanted to ask everyone is whether or not they were confident in the direction of the Minnesota Vikings four weeks into the 2026 regular season. After opening the season with four consecutive wins, with a couple of them coming in relatively ugly fashion, the answer to that question is a resounding. . .“Ehhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh.” Despite being one of only three remaining undefeated teams in the NFL after the first four weeks of the season, only 53% of Vikings fans are confident that the team is heading in the right direction, according to the results of our survey. While the Vikings are winning games, they’re doing it in a manner that isn’t necessarily artistic. They’ve failed to find the end zone in two of their four wins and have only scored one offensive touchdown over the last three games, but the number that matters the most is the one in the “W” column, and right now the Vikings have as many as you can have. “Well,” you might say, “the Vikings could have had a touchdown on Sunday if T.J. Hockenson had just walked into the end zone on the last real play they ran on offense.“ Well, we asked everyone about that, too, and there are plenty of you who feel that the big tight end did exactly what he should have in that situation. Of those who responded to our survey, 76% feel that Hockenson did the right thing by sliding down at the 1-yard line rather than scoring a touchdown. Honestly? I’m surprised the number is that low. Sure, the odds of the Dolphins scoring 12 points after getting the ball back with two minutes left in the game are just about zero, particularly with the way Minnesota’s defense has been playing these first four weeks. However, the odds of the Dolphins scoring at all without seeing the football again are exactly zero. Since the Vikings forced Miami to burn all of their timeouts leading up to that play, the Dolphins weren’t going to get the ball back (barring an absolute “Miracle at the Meadowlands”-style catastrophe from the Vikings), so the only people who were really super, duper mad about Hockenson sliding down are the people who had Vikings -10.5. You did the right thing, T.J. So, for those about to Hock. . .we salute you. Those are your SB Nation Reacts results for this week, ladies and gentlemen. As always, we’d like to thank everybody who took the time to participate in our survey and discuss the questions in our comments section and in the Feed, and we’ll have another one for you here next week! full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Will Reichard #16 of the Minnesota Vikings kicks a field goal against the Miami Dolphins during the second quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday, the Minnesota Vikings visit the New Orleans Saints in the Caesars Superdome. The NFC South squad’s season has been up and down as they come into the game with a 1-3 record. Their offense has shown decent production so far this season, averaging 367 yards per game and 26.3 points per game, good for 9th and 10th in the NFL, respectively. The reason for this production, however, is due in large part to the abysmal play of the defense, which often results in negative game scripts and base coverage by opposing defenses. On the defensive side of the ball, the Saints rank dead last (or first, depending on how you interpret the metrics) in points allowed per game at 32, with the Lions at a close second with 31.8. The table is set for a big day Coming off a contest where they gave up 45 points to the Atlanta Falcons, I foresee this team coming into Sunday one of two ways: deflated after an embarrassing divisional loss on national television, or as a team that is fired up with their backs against the wall, playing to avoid a 1-4 start. No matter how you slice it, this should be a game in which the Vikings’ offense gets a rhythm and is able to build momentum going into the bye week. The Vikings are in an excellent position to execute a 5-0 start for the 10th time (in the modern NFL era). Out of the nine 5-0 starts in modern franchise history, the Minnesota Vikings have made the playoffs in seven of those nine seasons. Fun fact: history actually favors the 4-1 start for Minnesota, as they have reached the playoffs 100% of the time in seasons where they start with a 4-1 record. I will never forget History doesn’t matter to me as much as ABSOLUTELY CRUSHING THE NEW ORLEANS SAINTS. I know it’s been almost two decades, but I still haven’t forgiven this franchise for what it did to our most (or second-most) promising Super Bowl Season of my lifetime. It’s crazy to me to think that there are Vikings fans who have never felt an intense hatred or anger toward the New Orleans Saints. I know holding grudges is bad for you, but I don’t care. I don’t care that this is a completely different team with an all-new coaching staff and players. I will be singing the skol song with an emphasis on “run up the score” as I will always be craving more points against the Saints. I want to use more colorful language in describing our Week 5 opponent, but I will refrain to avoid getting fined. A rune for your thoughts Instead, I will ask a rune. I am only pulling one rune from my pouch while asking the question, “What are we going to see this weekend when the Vikings play the Saints?” The rune, which presented itself face-up and in an upright position, was Hagalaz. What does that mean, you might ask? Well, what we are going to see on Sunday, according to the mythical stone, is “hail, wrath of nature, uncontrolled forces, destruction.” That, my friends, is what is in store for the New Orleans Saints. It is time for the offense to take a significant step This will be the game where the offense gets rolling. With Justin Jefferson (as of Friday morning) potentially suiting up, I can see a hailstorm of bombs and dimes raining all over the New Orleans defense. This should be a game in which Kyler Murray can throw for 300 yards and multiple touchdowns. Now, this hasn’t been the style of our favorite football team so far this season. It could also be a game in which we see the running game be more efficient than it has been so far in 2026. Many of us witnessed the Falcons bully the Saints into giving up 5 rushing touchdowns last week, so look for a big game from Aaron Jones. However, I feel like many teams, when an aspect of their defense gets thrashed in a game, focus intensely on that unit going into the next week, so I think a pass-first approach is the way to go this week. A new kind of monster The Saints have been playing with negative game scripts and in high-scoring contests all season. They may have an advantage if the game turns into a shootout. However, they have not met this defense full of savvy veterans and the students of Young Nasty University. The wrath of nature will come from the mind of Brian Flores and his defense. The uncontrolled forces include the likes of Dallas Turner, Jalen Redmond, Blake Cashman, Eric Wilson, Andrew Van Ginkel, Levi-Drake Rodriguez, Caleb Banks, and Big Citrus. Look for this defensive front to wreak havoc and Shough a quarterback named Tyler into oblivion. There will be nothing left Destruction will come in the form of the hopes and dreams of New Orleans Saints fans. I respect them for what they have gone through, but they aren’t blameless here. They didn’t tell Greg Williams to put a bounty on Brett Favre, but they sure as hell cheered it on when he was getting crushed on every other play. Ever since that season, the Saints have had terrible luck in the postseason, including, but not limited to, miracles and no-calls. Good. They deserve it, and I wish them the worst of luck going forward. The frustration of watching this offense fail to score touchdowns in two of four contests so far this season is still in the back of my mind. With our history of kickers in big games, we need to save as many field goals for the postseason as possible. Will Reichard may go down in history as the best kicker in Vikings franchise history, but in order to reach G.O.A.T. status, we will have to see success in the playoffs. He has to emulate Adam Vinatieri’s postseason clutch gene. To do that, we have to get to the playoffs and put him in situations where he can make those legendary kicks. Field goals against the 0-3 Miami Dolphins are a waste of his talent and skill. Let’s save those for when we really need them against division opponents and in NFC Championship games (or Wild Card games). I am very much looking forward to Sunday and am hoping we can relax during the bye week as one of the few remaining undefeated teams in the NFL. Until Next Skol.

title: Sunday Patriots Notes: Efton Chism earning Drake Maye’s trust
summary: The New England Patriots will look to build their first winning streak of the 2026 season. To do so, they will have to take down the 3-1 Raiders back at Gillette Stadium. Naturally, most of our attention this week was on that particular game and looking back at the win in Buffalo. However, there is […]
full_text: The New England Patriots will look to build their first winning streak of the 2026 season. To do so, they will have to take down the 3-1 Raiders back at Gillette Stadium. Naturally, most of our attention this week was on that particular game and looking back at the win in Buffalo. However, there is a lot going on at One Patriot Place these days, so let’s clean out the notebook. Welcome to the latest edition of our Sunday Patriots Notes. Trust in Chism For Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, earning a quarterback’s trust is the most important thing a wide receiver can do. “The biggest thing for receivers is that there’s trust from the guy that throws the football,” Vrabel said. “When you earn the quarterback’s trust … it doesn’t take you long to figure out who the quarterback trusts. It’s the ones they target. That’s a good indicator.” Vrabel made that point during OTAs last June when asked about undrafted rookie wide receiver Efton Chism III. Chism earned a spot on the Patriots’ 53-man roster as a rookie after a strong offseason in which he consistently drew targets. Now, he’s making the most of his opportunities on Sundays. Chism caught both of his targets in Buffalo last week, including a one-handed touchdown catch on New England’s game-winning drive. Those targets in a critical situation offered a glimpse of the trust quarterback Drake Maye has developed in Chism. “That’s one of the things with Chiz, you’re not going to worry about him being in the right spot or knowing the right thing to do,” Maye said. “And I think that’s comforting for the quarterback and for me back there to have a guy out there in the huddle.” That trust didn’t develop by accident. Practice reps with Maye are relatively rare for Chism, who has shared a wide receiver room with veterans like Stefon Diggs, Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins since arriving in New England. Instead, Chism has largely worked with the second-team offense during training camp and spent his in-season reps on the scout team, where he gets opportunities to make plays against the Patriots’ top defense. “Like 50,” defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr said when asked if any plays stand out from Chism’s work on the scout team. In order to bank reps with Maye, Chism stays late after practice nearly every day or seeks out the quarterback at odd hours in the facility to watch film together. That extra work has caught Maye’s attention and helped build the trust between them. “He’s been doing a lot of the little things that I think were just showing up,” Maye said. “He comes in every day, enjoys trying to see my side of things, asks questions and tries to get on the same page, and that’s what ends up happening. You start seeing the results.” After making the biggest play of his young career in Buffalo, Chism returned to Foxboro and went right back to work. He again was at the facility around 6 a.m. each morning this week and staying late to catch passes from Maye. That preparation will be provide Chism another opportunity this Sunday as the Patriots take on the Raiders with A.J. Brown still on injured reserve and Mack Hollins (calf) also landing on IR. “Couldn’t say enough great things about him,” offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said. “Really excited that he had his opportunity and made the most of it and look forward to the future with him.” A.J.’s return New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown had a notable presence in the team’s locker room throughout the past week, being in good spirits and walking without a limp. Brown, who wore just a small tape job on his injured right ankle, is eligible to begin practicing next week as he works toward returning from injured reserve. Brown is making strong progress and is expected to return sooner rather than later. However, a Thursday night matchup against the Chicago Bears the following week could be another factor in the team’s decision on his return timeline. Shoulder injury Christian Gonzalez suffered a shoulder injury in Week 3 while delivering a physical tackle in the first quarter. Gonzalez stayed in the game and said he was “good” afterward, but he has not practiced since and was ruled out for his second straight game this Sunday. After being ruled out last week, Gonzalez underwent additional testing on his injured shoulder earlier this week. He was spotted in the locker room Friday and has avoided being placed on injured reserve, perhaps signaling that his recovery is trending in a positive direction. QB/Center exchange The exchange between quarterback Drake Maye and center Jared Wilson resulted in several footballs on the ground last week in Buffalo. Offensive line coach Doug Marrone said it’s a skill that requires reps, while Mike Vrabel shed more light on two of the mishaps: “The center’s moving laterally, he has a block that he has a guy off his body, and he’s moving one way. Is the quarterback excited on the goal line to try to get off the goal line? I mean, I think you see those plays down there, and I know that he’s thinking he has to get off the line.” Close friends The Patriots’ matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders this week offers an interesting parallel to the start of Drake Maye’s career. No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza has begun his rookie season on the bench, with veteran Kirk Cousins starting at quarterback for Las Vegas. Maye spent the first five games of his career on the sideline while Jacoby Brissett started for New England. Maye said watching Brissett operate on and off the field was one of the coolest experiences of his rookie season, and he still speaks with the veteran quarterback weekly. “He’s been one of my best friends since I got in the league. So, it’s been cool for me to keep that relationship,“ Maye said. Saturday nights Speaking of close friends, wide receivers Mack Hollins and Efton Chism III had developed a close bond over the past year plus. Part of the two’s week include a regular Saturday night review following team meetings, where they will go back through the entire call sheet and game plan together. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels called Hollins a “great mentor” for Chism, whose work ethic has provided him more opportunities moving forward. “It wouldn’t be right for me to sit up here and not talk about his work ethic and his character since the moment we got him has been at the highest level it could be,” McDaniels said. “Just, it’s hard to say that an undrafted college free agent would be a pro’s pro, but I would tell you that that’s what he was. So he came in with that kind of demeanor, that kind of attitude.” 2001 reunion The Patriots will honor their 2001 Super Bowl team before kickoff Sunday to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the franchise’s first championship. Kicker Adam Vinatieri will also receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame Ring of Excellence during halftime. A lot of stars are making their return to Foxborough this weekend 🌟 https://t.co/R8vyQ53HFr pic.twitter.com/oCZbGoRA6e — New England Patriots (@Patriots) October 9, 2026 Vinatieri is one of 35 members of that team returning to Foxboro this weekend, where Mike Vrabel joined the group for a celebratory dinner Saturday night. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels was also part of the team, beginning his coaching career as a personnel assistant that season. Twenty-five years later, McDaniels still carries one key lesson from that team with him: “There’s a way to win and everybody can’t do it the same way,” he said. Week ahead For the last time until the end of the season, the Patriots will maintain a typical week with their next game back at home at 1 p.m., where they’ll take on the New York Jets. This means Mike Vrabel media availability on Monday, off-day on Tuesday, and three straight practices plus injury reports from Wednesday through Friday. The team will then hold a final walkthrough on Saturday before hosting the Jets.
author: Brian Hines

title: 3 things the Patriots have to do to beat the Raiders
summary: The New England Patriots are back in the playoff picture following their upset win over the Buffalo Bills. In order to not just stay there but solidify its position, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will need to make it back-to-back wins on Sunday: a victory over the Las Vegas Raiders would allow the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are back in the playoff picture following their upset win over the Buffalo Bills. In order to not just stay there but solidify its position, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will need to make it back-to-back wins on Sunday: a victory over the Las Vegas Raiders would allow the Patriots to keep building some momentum after some early-season issues. How can the Patriots do so? Here are three things that will be important if they want to defend their home turf and improve to 3-2 on the year. Don’t play into the Raiders’ hands Through four games, no team in the NFL has had more takeaways than the Raiders, whose nine combined interceptions (4) and fumble recoveries (5) top the league and are a big reason behind their 3-1 record. Likewise, the Patriots giving the ball away 10 times — tied for worst in the league — is why they are only 2-2 so far this year. Needless to say that ball security is of the utmost importance every week and something the Patriots need continue to do more successfully than they have this season. However, against an opportunistic opponent that has proven itself capable of taking advantage of short fields or momentum swings, it will be under the microscope even more: New England simply cannot afford to give the Raiders any extra chances this week. Luckily for the Patriots, there have been some encouraging signs. Even though Drake Maye turned the ball over twice in last week’s win over the Bills, both of those giveaways were more excusable than the abysmal and frankly game-losing decisions the young QB had made over the first three games of the year. Ideally, neither of those plays — a strip sack and interception off an unlucky bounce — happens. But as far as error repetition from the quarterback is concerned, there is not much he could do differently. That won’t make much of a difference against the Raiders, but on the grand scale of things shows that Maye and company might be trending in a positive direction after all. Neutralize the pressure It is no surprise that the Baltimore Ravens were willing to pay two first-round draft picks for him this offseason, before a trade fell through due to a failed physical: Maxx Crosby remains one of the most disruptive players in the NFL and as good an edge rusher as the Patriots will go up against all season. He is not the only problem up front, though. Malcolm Koonce and Kwity Paye are also skilled enough to throw an offense off its tracks if given an opportunity to do so; the entire edge group is more than capable of helping decide the game in Las Vegas’ favor — especially as part of what is an aggressive pressure scheme — and the Patriots need to find a way to account for that. Helping offensive tackles Will Campbell and Morgan Moses through chips or double teams is one way, but offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels could also try to do something else. Go where Crosby and company are not by stressing the interior of the line. Tonka Hemingway, Folorunso Fatukasi and Adam Butler are not bad players, but there is a clear drop-off in quality from the edge to the interior. New England needs to find a way to use this to its advantage, and stress the group particularly on the ground. While the Raiders are ranked sixth in EPA given up per rush (-0.183), they are 31st in the league in rush yards per attempt (5.2). That disconnect stems mostly from the team’s ability to force turnovers, which naturally has a significant impact on expected points. If the Patriots can hold onto the football, though, they should be able to put pressure on a run defense that is not as good as its advanced statistical rankings might suggest. Force Kirk Cousins out of his comfort zone He only ranks third in catches (16) and second in both yards (202) and touchdowns (2) on the team, but tight end Brock Bowers very much is the motor that powers the Raiders offense. “What he does at his size, the speed, the route craft, and being able to catch at the catch point — he’s like a big slot receiver,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said about Bowers this week . “He has downfield speed, he runs outward breaking routes, he runs routes like a receiver, but then also he’s got the ability to double guys up inside.” From a Patriots’ defensive perspective, the goal very much is clear: find a way to make Bowers less effective, and by extension force quarterback Kirk Cousins out of his comfort zone. How do you do that, though? By focusing on what both of them do best. In Cousins’ case it is operating in rhythm and throwing timing routes; the 38-year-old is not necessarily capable of making extended plays or adjusting on the fly at this stage in his career. His biggest weapon is not his physical skill but rather his ability to solve problems with his mind, and take what a defense is giving him. Without Las Vegas having a wide receiver capable of stressing defenses deep, that is taking the underneath play rather than forcing throws that are not there to be made (as is reflected by Las Vegas’ 18th-ranked 7.1 yards per pass play). This means a heavy dosage of Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer, the latter being more of a traditional in-line option compared to the receiver-first TE that is Bowers. No team in. the NFL is playing more 12-personnel than the Raiders. From a New England perspective, it’s all about being sound in their zone coverage and not putting their personnel in exposed situations. They did a mighty fine job against Buffalo’s capable tight end duo of Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox last week, and a repeat performance on Sunday would go a long way toward securing a win.

title: Patriots fans believe playoffs remain possible
summary: Following the New England Patriots 29-26 upset victory over the Buffalo Bills last weekend, head coach Mike Vrabel labeled his team as “back in the race.” After dropping two of their first three games — including being on the wrong side of a 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars — the response in Buffalo […]
full_text: Following the New England Patriots 29-26 upset victory over the Buffalo Bills last weekend, head coach Mike Vrabel labeled his team as “back in the race.” After dropping two of their first three games — including being on the wrong side of a 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars — the response in Buffalo was a huge win for Vrabel and his team. Beyond getting back to .500 on the year, the Patriots avoided dropping two games behind the Bills in the AFC East. Back in the race, they are. In the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 42% of participants seem to be in agreement with the head coach as they are eyeing the playoffs. Some in the comment section argued in each direction: Felkey Need to see more consistency from Maye. Can’t be having mid game meltdowns like he did against Seattle or Jacksonville. Assuming Maye can revert to his normal firm and this was a sign of things to come, I still maintain 11-6 or better is a reasonable goal. Especially if we can start getting some guys back from injury. Bajer of course , they are only one game back with 1 games to play. It’d be silly to see it any other way. I definitely still need to see more, and Drake HAS to stop being a turnover machine– but the beat the best team in the afc east , that has to count for something. let;s see how they do in a few more games, ad then we can revisit the Q PDCeltics Poll needs a “they were never out of it” option. Gonzucla Unless some major changes happen on offense, I still believe they are a 6-win team. All in all, this week’s survey results look as follows: While the majority of voters believe playoffs are possible, a heavy percentage are a step above or below that feeling. 27% believe this Patriots team is fully legit, while 26% still need to see more after their 2-2 start to the season. Just 5%, however, are still skeptical even after the win in Buffalo. The Patriots win in Buffalo, coupled with a bounce back performance from Drake Maye, has fan confidence back trending in a positive direction. After fan confidence bottomed out to just 9% in last week’s poll, 82% of Patriots fans feel the team is headed in the right direction this week. title: What Patriots roster moves ahead of Raiders game mean for Week 5 and beyond
summary: The New England Patriots’ active roster underwent several modifications on the eve of the team’s Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Wide receiver Mack Hollins and fullback Reggie Gilliam were both placed on injured reserve, with safety and special teamer Brenden Schooler and cornerback Kindle Vildor taking their. spots on the 53-man team. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ active roster underwent several modifications on the eve of the team’s Week 5 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Wide receiver Mack Hollins and fullback Reggie Gilliam were both placed on injured reserve, with safety and special teamer Brenden Schooler and cornerback Kindle Vildor taking their. spots on the 53-man team. The Patriots also elevated linebacker K.J. Britt and safety Elliott Davison from the practice squad for the Raiders game, but our focus for now lies on the other four transactions. Let’s break down what they mean. FB Reggie Gilliam: Placed on IR While other moves received more attention, signing Gilliam to a three-year, $10.8 million contract in free agency was no insignificant investment by the Patriots either. Making him the highest-paid fullback in the NFL in terms of total contract value showed that the team had big plans for him on both offense and special teams. Those plans, however, need to be shelved for the foreseeable future. Now on injured reserve after previously dealing with knee and ankle issues, Gilliam will be out for at least four games. The Patriots already ruled out for the Raiders game on Friday, and in addition won’t have him available against the New York Jets, Chicago Bears and Miami Dolphins — at least on paper a comparatively easy stretch of games. Still, the Patriots won’t be without their only fullback over those four games. How big the on-field impact will actually be, however, can be questioned: New England’s run game had struggled even with him on the active roster, and Gilliam himself had played merely 22% of offense snaps thus far (plus 41% on special teams). He wasn’t necessarily bad, but it was clear that his role within the unit — just like New England’s run game as a whole — was a work in progress. That progress now takes a hit with the 29-year-old not eligible to return to practice until early November. In addition, going back to the investment mentioned earlier, Gilliam becomes the fourth serious offseason addition to be placed on injured reserve. Tight end Julian Hill was the first to go there and will miss the remainder of the season, while wide receiver A.J. Brown, offensive lineman Greg Van Roten and now Gilliam are eligible to come off of IR at a later point. How will the team replace him, though? There is a chance it won’t, and will use a tight end such as undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin as a fullback/H-back hybrid — a role he partially played over the summer. They also could decide to bring back second-year FB Brock Lampe, an undrafted rookie signing in 2025 who was cut ahead of training camp and currently is on the Bills’ practice squad. WR Mack Hollins: Placed on IR The Efton Chism Show is bound to continue — that is one of the takeaways of Mack Hollins moving to injured reserve after sustaining a calf injury versus his ex-team, the Bills, last Sunday. Chism did perform well and his teammates and coaches sang his praises since he made two big catches, including a one-handed touchdown from 23 yards out that capped the game-winning drive, in Buffalo. The second-year man being in a position to do so was a direct result of Hollins’ departure, and all signs point toward the arrangement continuing now that the veteran is on IR. This also means, however, that the Patriots are now down two of their top four wideouts entering the season: the aforementioned A.J. Brown remains on IR at least until next week, with Hollins now joining him. As a consequence, New England’s receiver corps now looks like this: 53-man roster (4): Romeo Doubs (87), DeMario Douglas (3), Kyle Williams (18 | KR), Efton Chism III (86) Practice squad (3): Kyle Dixon (83), Cameron Dorner (88), Chandler Brayboy (81) IR (3): A.J. Brown (1), Mack Hollins (13), Jeremiah Webb (29 | season-ending) Needless to say, what looked like an embarrassment of riches at one point in training camp has quickly started to deteriorate. Getting Brown, the nominal WR1, back will give the group a natural boost; the same is true for Drake Maye and Romeo Doubs continuing to develop their chemistry. Still, this is a position that can hardly afford to take any more hits. Could this mean the Patriots are the mystery team to trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. now that the Cardinals are reportedly finalizing a move of the former first-round draft pick? Nothing can ever be ruled out, but this would still come out of left field and might be a bit too reactionary for a club already having invested serious resources in both 2026 and beyond at the wide receiver position. CB Kindle Vildor: Promoted to 53-man roster After already promoting one defensive back from the practice squad to the active roster earlier in the week — safety Mike Brown — the Patriots have now also brought up Kindle Vildor. The veteran being part of the game day roster against the Raiders was expected after the team ruled out four cornerbacks, including starters Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. However, instead of using his second of three standard elevations, he now has officially become the seventh CB on the 53-man team: 53-man roster (7): Christian Gonzalez (0), Carlton Davis III (7), Marcus Jones (25 | PR), Charles Woods (22), Channing Canada (29), Karon Prunty (21), Kindle Vildor (28) Practice squad (1): Al’zillion Hamilton (26) The Patriots promoting Vildor does not only save those remaining two practice squad elevations should he return to the developmental roster at one point, it also comes with a pay increase and adds some more experience to New England’s CB room: Vildor has played in 86 combined regular season and playoff games since entering the league in 2020 as an undrafted free agent. This experience allowed him to step in last week versus Buffalo after Charles Woods, who was replacing Christian Gonzalez in the lineup, briefly departed with a shoulder injury. With Woods himself on the injury report as questionable, Vildor’s presence now also means that the Patriots have two fully-healthy CBs on their active team now. And if the Patriots are forced to use him, which seems likely given that they are down Gonzalez, Davis, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty, it is clear that they have some faith in him. “Kindle is the ultimate pro,” said defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr earlier this week. “Didn’t bat an eye, got in there, challenged. He’s a vet, so I think he’s got some different styles he’s used. He’s brought a great presence even since OTAs, and if he has to be the one to go in there, then we’ll be excited about it.” S Brenden Schooler: Activated off NFI The writing was already on the wall, and on Friday head coach Mike Vrabel effectively confirmed that Brenden Schooler would be activated before the game against the Raiders. After opening the season on the non-football injury list with a back ailment, the 2025 special teams captain is now back on the team. Whether he will return to his status as captain will be seen, but the actual on-field impact is what’s most important. And the Patriots should feel his presence right away, especially as a gunner on the punt team — a role that was, rather unusually, filled by rookie linebacker Erick Hunter last week in Buffalo. Hunter performed decently well, but Schooler is an All-Pro at that position and elsewhere in the kicking game. The trickle-down effect of his return could therefore be felt across the board, and in turn free up some players to play expanded roles elsewhere or simply get a few more snaps off between offensive or defensive series. With Schooler now joining Vildor on the active roster, and with neither Hollins nor Gilliam on it at the moment, the Patriots still have one spot open. They additionally also have a spot open on the practice squad now that Vildor has been promoted. How those spots will be used is unclear at the moment, but with A.J. Brown’s return looming in the distance the team might just keep the one on the 53-man team open for the time being.

title: College Players to Watch: Week 5
summary: The New Orleans Saints have struggled through the first four games, and there are some obvious deficiencies that have been on display week in and week out. So, if you’re looking for college football games to watch, let’s go over some players to be on the lookout for this weekend who may find themselves sitting […]
full_text: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 3: Princewill Umanmielen #1 of the LSU Tigers celebrates after a tackle against the McNeese State Cowboys at Tiger Stadium on October 3, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Ella Hall/LSU/University Images via Getty Images} The New Orleans Saints have struggled through the first four games, and there are some obvious deficiencies that have been on display week in and week out. So, if you’re looking for college football games to watch, let’s go over some players to be on the lookout for this weekend who may find themselves sitting near the top of the Saints’ draft board. First, the biggest game of the weekend will feature Alabama hosting Georgia at 6:30 PM on ABC. This game features two of the best defensive backs in the nation, both of whom play for Georgia. Safety KJ Bolden and cornerback Ellis Robinson IV lead a stingy Bulldogs pass defense. So far this season, Robinson has allowed a 48.5 passer rating when targeted and will most likely draw the assignment of covering talented receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams. Bolden is an all-around safety who can come down and make tackles while still being able to drop back into coverage. Both of these players are guys the Saints would love to have suiting up for them this weekend instead of the Bulldogs. If you’re watching UGA vs. Bama, be sure to keep an eye out for these two talented defenders. Interior pass rush and run defense have been problems for the Saints, partly because of a lack of depth at defensive tackle. Well, there are two players to check out this weekend who could help the Saints address those issues: Will Echoles and David Stone. Echoles is a dominant defensive lineman who plays for Ole Miss, and his performance against LSU led to the Tigers making changes along their own offensive line. He is strong, quick, and disruptive. The Rebels will be looking for Echoles to display all of his talents on Saturday as they travel to Nashville to take on Vandy at 2:30 PM. As for David Stone, he is the anchor of the Oklahoma defense. An interior defensive lineman who enjoys making double teams look silly, Stone is a fitting name for him. He stonewalls offensive linemen, and if Oklahoma has any chance of pulling off the upset against Texas at 2:30 PM on Saturday, it will have to start with Stone up front. Finally, the most obvious need for the Saints right now is a complementary piece at edge rusher to pair with Chase Young. Dylan Stewart could very well be that guy, along with Colin Simmons and possibly Princewill Umanmielen as a Day 2 option. Stewart has been dealing with some personal matters at South Carolina but is returning from suspension this week to face Florida at 11:45 AM. His size and athleticism are absolutely elite, and he’s rated only behind Colin Simmons. Simmons is the highest-rated pass rusher in this upcoming draft and will most likely be selected within the first five picks. But in case there’s a chance he ends up in New Orleans, you should give him a look. He will be lining up opposite David Stone in the Red River Rivalry on Saturday. Princewill Umanmielen is skyrocketing up draft boards right now. He’s currently viewed as a Day 2 selection, but if he continues at his current pace, he could firmly establish himself as a first-round talent. Umanmielen leads the nation with eight sacks in five games, and while he still needs to showcase his ability to hold his ground against bigger offensive linemen, his speed and frame make him an enticing prospect. Umanmielen will be in Lexington leading the Tigers’ defense against the Wildcats at 6:00 PM. Are there any other players you’re keeping your eyes on this weekend? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title: If the Saints win/lose vs. Vikings
summary: The New Orleans Saints are looking to pick themselves up off the floor after being routed by the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. They host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in yet another pivotal early-season game for the black and gold. Here’s what either outcome could mean for the Saints. If the Saints win: […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 05: Kool-Aid McKinstry #1 of the New Orleans Saints and Fadil Diggs #40 and Davon Godchaux #92 and Danny Stutsman #28 and Nathan Shepherd #93 huddle together for a play during the first half of a game against the Atlanta Falcons at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are looking to pick themselves up off the floor after being routed by the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football. They host the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday in yet another pivotal early-season game for the black and gold. Here’s what either outcome could mean for the Saints. If the Saints win: A win would garner a collective sigh of relief among Who Dat Nation and restore some of the belief that this team can still win the division this season. The Vikings have struggled to find the end zone in their last few games. If the defense can find enough to continue that trend, and the offense can squeeze out enough points against a very impressive Vikings defense, New Orleans will win this matchup. It’s one that the Saints simply have to have. If the Saints lose: One usually wants to avoid such hyperbolic descriptions in early October, but another defeat here could start to spell the beginning of the end of the Saints’ playoff hopes. With Carolina and Atlanta seemingly trending in the right direction, the division would already begin to feel out of reach. A third consecutive defeat, in three home games, would be beyond gut-punching for Kellen Moore and his team. Anyone who’s been around this league for a while knows the inherently unpredictable and surprising nature of an NFL season. Writing off this team, especially given the way the quarterback has played, can’t be done at this early stage. New Orleans has been on the wrong end of questionable decisions, faced injuries on both sides of the ball, and could’ve easily been 3-0 after the Raiders game. But nevertheless, the vibes would be particularly sour, and hopes nearly fully deflated, if the Saints fall to 1-4 this week. Another feature of this league is that it is unforgiving. Do you think the Saints can get it done on Sunday? How has the opening month of the season affected your outlook for the rest of 2026? Let us know in the comments!

title: Roster moves: NY Giants put Chauncey Golston on IR, elevate two from the practice squad
summary: The New York Giants have placed defensive lineman Chauncey Golston on the injured reserve with a neck injury. Golston suffered the injury in the Giants’ win over the Arizona Cardinals. While Golston and the Giants sought a second opinion during the week, the fear had been that Golston’s neck injury would be a “long term” […]
full_text: New York Giants defensive lineman Chauncey Golston | Getty Images The New York Giants have placed defensive lineman Chauncey Golston on the injured reserve with a neck injury. Golston suffered the injury in the Giants’ win over the Arizona Cardinals. While Golston and the Giants sought a second opinion during the week, the fear had been that Golston’s neck injury would be a “long term” injury. He’s emerged as a key contributor along the Giants’ defensive line, playing on both base downs and as a part of the Giants’ pass rush packages. The Giants signed defensive lineman Jihad Ward off the Minnesota Vikings practice squad last week, and placing Golston on the injured reserve will likely lead to his debut for the Giants. This is Ward’s second stint with the Giants, and he is familiar with Dennard Wilson after spending the 2025 season on the Tennessee Titans’ defense. Ward had a career year under Wilson with 31 total tackles, 4 for a loss, 5.0 sacks, 22 quarterback hits, and 4 passes defensed. The Giants are also elevating receiver/returner Dalen Cambre as well as OLB Trace Ford . Cambre is a fan favorite for his work over the last two preseasons, as well as a needed piece given the Giants’ shallow receiver depth chart and emphasis on special teams. Ford will help reinforce a Giants’ front seven that is thin following the injury to Brian Burns.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Should the NY Giants trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are preparing to trade wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., per multiple reports. ESPN’s Adam Schefter had the report first, and it’s been corroborated from multiple sources since his initial report. As so often happens when a big name is on the trading block or suddenly becomes a free agent, we need to […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 04: Greg Newsome II #20 of the New York Giants intercepts a pass intended for Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 of the Arizona Cardinals during the second quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are preparing to trade wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., per multiple reports. ESPN’s Adam Schefter had the report first , and it’s been corroborated from multiple sources since his initial report. As so often happens when a big name is on the trading block or suddenly becomes a free agent, we need to ask ourselves: Should the New York Giants be involved? In this case, should the Giants trade for Marvin Harrison Jr.? The current reporting is that the Houston Texans are the leading candidate for Harrison Jr., as they attempt to salvage their season following a surprising 0-4 start. However, Jordan Schultz is reporting that multiple other teams are engaged in talks with the Cardinals and at least one believes that he’s worth Day 2 compensation. Schefter hinted on the Pat McAfee show earlier in the week that the Giants have had some level of interest in Harrison Jr. Do the New York Giants need help at wide receiver? There’s a strong argument that they do need additional help at wide receiver, considering they only have three pure wide receivers on their roster right now. The Giants current receiving depth chart looks like this: Wide receivers Malik Nabers Darnell Mooney Malachi Fields Returner/receiver Charlie Jones Practice squad Jalin Hyatt Dalen Cambre Dontae Fleming Considerations about how the Giants want to operate their offense aside, the team’s depth chart is razor thin, and they’re one injury away from a crisis situation. Likewise there’s also a good question as to whether a receiver-light roster is even the best way to support quarterback Jameis Winston. Winston wants to attack downfield, and wide receivers are just better at that than tight ends. We’ve also seen a decline in the Giants’ rushing attack with the current roster composition since the injury to Jaxson Dart. But is trading potentially significant draft capital for Marvin Harrison Jr. the answer?

title: Survey results: Fans split on the Giants’ playoff potential
summary: The New York Giants are going into Week 5 with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East. If the season ended today, the Giants would have the third seed and host the Seattle Seahawks at MetLift Stadium. However, the season doesn’t end today. Instead, the Giants will be facing […]
full_text: New York Giants quarterback Jameis Winston before a play. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants are going into Week 5 with a 3-1 record and sole possession of first place in the NFC East. If the season ended today, the Giants would have the third seed and host the Seattle Seahawks at MetLift Stadium. However, the season doesn’t end today. Instead, the Giants will be facing the 1-3 Washington Commanders on the road; a game in which they’re 3.5-point underdogs (per FanDuel ). And despite holding first place in the NFC East, with the chance to gain a two-game lead in the division, few have confidence that the Giants will even make the playoffs — let alone win the division. This is an interesting spread of responses. “No” obviously won out, with nearly 40 percent of respondents believing that the Giants will be on the couch after Week 18. And it’s significantly higher than the number of fans who believe the Giants can execute the “worst to first” leap and win the NFC outright. However, almost as many fans believe their team will get a wildcard berth as will miss the playoffs. The Giants are (as of this writing) one of three teams in the NFC with a 3-1 record, and the only one in first place in their division. The other two are the Chicago Bears and Seattle Seahawks, who each sit behind the 4-0 Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers, respectively. So while many more fans think the Giants will miss the playoffs than win the division, that flips FanDuel has the Giants as relative longshots to make the playoffs, giving them just the 13th-best odds at +290. However, the Giants have a real chance to impact those odds this week. FanDuel considers both the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys to be much more likely to win the division than the Giants. They give the Cowboys the seventh-best odds to make the playoffs, while the Eagles have the 9th best odds, though both are extremely flawed teams. Dallas’ poor defense and inconsistent offense makes for an extremely volatile combination that can beat anyone, or lose to anyone. The Eagles are reshuffling their offensive line on the fly after the retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson and the trade of Cam Jurgens. At the same time, they’re dealing with injuries to offensive stars. The Giants, of course, have some questions of their own to answer, largely revolving around the quarterback position. And considering that quarterback is (arguably) the most important position in sports, those are automatically big questions. Overall, however, the Giants play in Week 4 has fans believing again. Confidence cratered after the Giants’ disastrous loss to the Los Angeles Rams which also saw the loss of Jaxson Dart. Since then, gritty wins over the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals have restored faith in the direction of the team. Giants fans’ confidence has typically proven to be resilient since we’ve been doing these surveys. Giants fans want to believe in their team, and typically respond well to teams as long as it’s clear that there’s a path forward. In this case, fans came into the 2026 season very confident that their team was headed in the right direction, which became almost universal confidence after their win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1. And now, we’re right back to those levels of confidence in the direction of the team. I suspect that the manner in which the Giants have been winning has had as much of an impact on fan confidence as the wins themselves. The Giants’ defense has been showing up on game day, holding the Titans to zero first downs in the first half of Week 3, and swarming the Cardinals offense after a slow start in Week 4. It also helps that resurgent players like safety Jevon Holland and cornerback Tae Banks have proven instrumental to their success. Likewise, the weekly improvement of Malik Nabers has to inspire some confidence as well. Giants running back Cam Skattebo promised that the game against the Commanders will be a “slugfest” thanks to the remnants of hurricane Isaias, as well both teams’ physicality. That’s exactly the type of game the Giants have been winning this year, so we’ll see if they can do it again.

title: College football Week 6: 2027 NFL Draft prospects for the NY Giants
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 6 of the 2026 college football season! We have some awesome games on the schedule today, including one that could be the game of the year and a National Championship preview. I said last week that we’re getting into the meat of the […]
full_text: Texas Longhorns defensive tackle Hero Kanu (93) | Getty Images Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 6 of the 2026 college football season! We have some awesome games on the schedule today, including one that could be the game of the year and a National Championship preview. I said last week that we’re getting into the meat of the schedule and this week could give us some must-watch scouting tape for the draft process. You always love to see “good against good” matchups, and we’ll get plenty of matchups between future NFL players today. As usual we’re going to concentrate on positions of perceived need for the Giants. In this case, we’ll be spotlighting an offensive and defensive lineman. So without further ado, let’s get to it! (14) Missouri vs. Texas A&M ABC – noon Player spotlight: Cayden Green (OT, Missouri) The Giants are pretty well set along the offensive line, at least for the moment. However, Green is an intriguing player in the mold of Sisi Mauigoa who could change the Giants’ plans if he slips to the second day. Green started his career at left guard and played the position for two years before moving out to left tackle. He reportedly measures in at 6-foot-5, 325 pounds and has the movement skills to play tackle as well as the power to play on the interior. Missouri has a formidable run game, and we know a big, powerful, and athletic lineman who’s a solid pass protector and powerful run blocker will appeal to the Giants. They can’t (easily) move on from Jon Runyan Jr. until after 2027, but the Giants might not want to wait if the value is right. Oklahoma vs. (1) Texas ABC – 3:30 p.m. Player spotlight: Hero Kanu (DT, Texas) Let’s get this out of the way right now: First Team All Name. Kanu has an interesting biography as a German-American and a relative latecomer to football. Kanu grew up in the small town of Geltendorf, which is just west of Munich, and was grew up a soccer player. Unfortunately, there aren’t too many 6-foot-5, 309 pound soccer players (even as a goalie), but Kanu eventually discovered American rules football and decided to swap fußball for football. He moved to America for the chance to play for a major college and eventually enrolled at Ohio State. He spent the first three years of his collegiate career at OSU before transferring to Texas in 2025. Kanu is only credited with 8 tackles for a loss and 3.5 sacks in his college career, but his production has improved since transferring to Texas and becoming a starter. He was a real problem for Tennessee last week and a consistent presence in the Vol’s backfield as a disruptive force. The Giants will need to continue to build their defensive tackle rotation, and Kanu could be see his profile rise if he continues to stack games like he had against Tennessee. (6) Alabama vs. (2) Georgia ABC – 7:30 p.m. ( Note: the game is still scheduled to be played as of this writing. Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the Gulf Coast and is expected to make landfall as a Category 2 hurricane. ) I’m deviating from this year’s format for this game, because there’s simply far far too much talent on the field in this game to spotlight a single player. This feels like the matchups between these two teams from a couple years ago, when there were NFL players everywhere you looked and often going against each other. It’s entirely possible that this winds up being one of the best games of the year and a preview of the National Championship. This is one of those games where my best advice is to watch, enjoy, and take note of the players who jump off the screen. Players to watch Alabama Ryan Coleman-Williams (WR) Devan Thompkins (iDL) Yhonzae Pierre (EDGE) Zabien Brown (CB) Keion Sabb (S) Bray Hubbard (S) Georgia Drew Bobo (iOL) Earnest Greene (OT) Nate Frazier (RB) Lawson Luckie (TE) Chris Cole (LB) Ellis Robinson IV (CB) KJ Bolden (S)

title: NFL Week 5 betting advice: Giants-Commanders picks and props
summary: Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 5 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that are less than -120. No gimmes! Here’s something you don’t see every day: The Giants are 3-1, their opponent this […]
full_text: Stay hot, Big Blue! | Getty Images Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 5 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that are less than -120. No gimmes! Here’s something you don’t see every day: The Giants are 3-1, their opponent this week (Washington) is 1-3, and they’re underdogs. New York comes in on a two-game winning streak, albeit with a pair of extremely narrow escapes, at home, over very weak competition. It gets a little harder this week. The Commanders lost to the Colts in London last week, but for much of the game they were led by a third-string, seventh-round rookie QB seeing his first NFL action. They’ll have Jayden Daniels back this week, and that’s obviously a massive boost. However, they could be without their top two wide receivers. Like the Giants, they’ve had a slew of key injuries on the young season. The Giants are 0-3 against the Commanders with Daniels under center. With Dallas losing to the previously winless Bucs on Thursday night at home, and the badly wounded Eagles traveling to London on Sunday to face the red-hot Jaguars, the Giants are staring down a great chance to go up two full games on the NFC East if they can upset the Commanders. So it’s a big division game for John Harbaugh’s team, which is trying to find solid footing after the losses of Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns. I’m on a heater – My picks are 3-0 each of the last two weeks, and I’m 8-4 on the season. I’ll try to keep the streak going in Week 5. Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel and are as of Saturday, Oct. 10. The forecast for Sunday is rainy, with some wind too, from tropical storm Isaias. The line for the game is Commanders -3.5, with a game total of 42.5 Game total UNDER 42.5 (-115) . This total feels high to me. Stefon Diggs isn’t going to play and Terry McLaurin is a game-time decision. The Commanders have struggled to run the ball. The Giants are going to want to establish the run, but the Commanders are pretty stout in that regard (sixth ranked defense against the run). They’re susceptible to the pass (24 th ranked pass defense), but I don’t think the Giants’ coaching staff wants Jameis Winston to drop back 30-plus times again, if they can avoid it. Throw in the bad weather that’s expected and I think scoring will be suppressed. Jameis Winston most passing yards in game (-120). Daniels is going to be without some key receiving weapons (although the Commanders will have RB Rachaad White back). Winston has all of his weapons, and I think the Giants are going to have to throw a lot to win this game. That’s how you beat the Commanders. Throw in the re-injury risk with Daniels and his bum elbow and I’ll take Winston to have more passing yards than his counterpart. Jayden Daniels OVER 30.5 rushing yards (-114). Daniels is supposedly playing without any limitations, but I suspect this line is as low as it is because there’s concern that he’ll run less to protect his elbow. I’m not buying it – he knows his legs are a fantastic weapon in his arsenal, and he’s always been aggressive about taking off when the opportunity is there. He averages almost 50 rushing yards per game for his career, and that average includes several games he didn’t finish. Even if the very athletic Arvell Reese is spying him, I expect plenty of running and especially given the Commanders’ depleted receiver corps. This over feels like free money – provided Daniels finishes the game. Those are the picks for Week 5. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 5 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, right here .

title: Giants notebook: Abdul Carter, Ben Mann’s accuracy, more
summary: Here are some notes, quotes, and numbers to know before the New York Giants face the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Confounding Carter Abdul Carter is a confounding pass rusher. He wins fast: He wins a lot: He just does not compile a lot of sacks. He has just one in four games this season, and […]
full_text: Here are some notes, quotes, and numbers to know before the New York Giants face the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Confounding Carter Abdul Carter is a confounding pass rusher. He wins fast: Fastest avg time to pressure (min. 50 pass rush snaps and 10 pressures): Abdul Carter: 2.20s Chop Robinson: 2.38s Ed Oliver: 2.39s Boye Mafe: 2.40s Nik Bonitto: 2.41s Andrew Van Ginkel: 2.41s Byron Murphy: 2.42s Leonard Williams: 2.44s Jared Verse: 2.44s Jonathan Allen: 2.45s pic.twitter.com/Zx91pfGFBj — SūmerSports (@SumerSports) October 7, 2026 He wins a lot: He just does not compile a lot of sacks. He has just one in four games this season, and five in 21 career games. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said this week that Carter was “throwing his fastball all game” against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4, and lauded his impact on Arizona quarterback Jacoby Brissett. It’s hard not to believe the sack numbers will eventually come for Carter. But, can he play quarterback? How good has rookie long-snapper Ben Mann been for the Giants this season? This good: Highest % of perfect-spiral long snaps this season (min 4 starts) Ben Mann 100% Reid Ferguson 95.7% Hogan Hatten 95.0% Ross Matiscik 92.3% Andrew DePaola 92.3% pic.twitter.com/dqtTm40aAJ — PFF NY Giants (@PFF_Giants) October 7, 2026 If only Jameis Winston were that accurate. Unblemished Commanders coach Dan Quinn is 6-0 as a head coach against the Giants, 4-0 with the Commanders and 2-0 with the Atlanta Falcons, per Giants PR. The only other coach with an undefeated record against the Giants (five-game minimum) is Sean McVay of the Los Angeles Rams. McVay is 5-0. “He’s Jameis. When I first got to meet him, I didn’t think he was as serious as he was. I didn’t know that. But he’s a very serious person at times. He knows how to be, when I say serious, very professional. But at the same point in time, I think we know who Jameis is too, and he likes to be lighthearted as well.” — Matt Nagy on Jameis Winston Skat’s magic number In two seasons, the Giants are 5-0 when Cam Skattebo has at least 18 rushing attempts. They are 0-7 when he has 17 carries or fewer. Speaking of the running game, I wrote this week that coach John Harbaugh admitted the Giants are “ just not good enough ” in the run game. The longest run from a running back so far this season is 13 yards. “I think we haven’t fully came into our own yet,” Skattebo said. “I think up front we’re in a new scheme, new system, and these guys are learning. Sisi (offensive lineman Francis Mauigoa) coming in, this is going into game five of his career. The guys up front are learning the system. B-Hud’s (offensive lineman Bryan Hudson) the center now. “At times, going on, we’ve just got to continue to work and get better at what we’re doing. I think as time goes on, it’s going to get better and better. These guys are going to really find the flow in the system and things are going to be just fine.” The most interesting takeaway there is Skattebo revealing that Hudson has indeed taken the starting center job from John Michael Schmitz. On the flip side, this is the first time since 2006 that the Giants have not allowed at least one run of 25 yards through their first four games. ( H/T, Giants PR ) Dealing with Jayden The Giants have to approach Jayden Daniels, a quarterback who can be devastating when he begins to run, differently than the stationary Jacoby Brissett of the Arizona Cardinals. Rush discipline is critical. “That’s a really big thing. That’s a big factor,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “That’s a big challenge because pinning your ears back, what does that exactly mean? There’s lanes, so to speak. There’s leverages. There’s angles involved. I think it’s really important to understand that you’re rushing to the quarterback, not past the blockers or past the offensive line. If you try to rush past the offensive line, you’re usually going to be past the quarterback. That’s not good. So, we want to be to the quarterback in a direct fashion, direct manner. Our guys are really focusing on doing that. But that doesn’t mean you can just run offensive linemen over. They don’t let you do that too often. “So, you’ve got to have ways to go about getting past them to the quarterback. That’s the challenge. I think if you think about it that way, you can see it’s not the easiest thing in the world to do. But that’s what we work on all the time. We have really good pass rushers, I think it’s starting to heat up a little bit. I feel like you can feel it. So, it’s good.”

title: Jets fan confidence collapses after blowout loss to Bears
summary: I think it’s fair to say that Jets fans were feeling pretty good heading into the Week 4 game against the Chicago Bears. The team’s 1-2 record obscured what looked like legitimate progress through the first three weeks of the season. Each week we take a poll of Jets fans about their confidence in the […]
full_text: New York Jets Head Coach, Aaron Glenn, is shown during the second quarter, Sunday, October 5, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I think it’s fair to say that Jets fans were feeling pretty good heading into the Week 4 game against the Chicago Bears. The team’s 1-2 record obscured what looked like legitimate progress through the first three weeks of the season. Each week we take a poll of Jets fans about their confidence in the team’s direction. Prior to the Chicago game 71 percent of fans who voted expressed confidence. It was easy to tell that the number would drop after an ugly loss to the Bears, but the effect is striking. One of the running gags of these confidence surveys is how one performance good or bad can have a monumental effect on fan confidence. Even by the standards of these polls, however, a 53 point swing in a single week is staggering. It’s clear Jets fans hold coaching responsible to a large extent. This week we asked fans what the team should do with Aaron Glenn. A vast majority said the second year head coach should be fired either now or after the season. There is one positive for Glenn and this team. If a bad week can lead to a large swing in a negative direction, a good week against Cleveland might have a similar impact in the other direction. title: New York Jets: A more disciplined defense is missing less tackles
summary: Missed tackles. They are a frustrating fact of life in the NFL. Every team misses multiple tackles per game, but some are worse offenders than others. The New York Jets have been egregious in this fundamental facet of the game for years. Different sites will give slightly different figures. Working with Pro Football Reference numbers, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Dane Belton #6 of the New York Jets tackles Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Missed tackles. They are a frustrating fact of life in the NFL. Every team misses multiple tackles per game, but some are worse offenders than others. The New York Jets have been egregious in this fundamental facet of the game for years. Different sites will give slightly different figures. Working with Pro Football Reference numbers, the Jets have been among the NFL’s least efficient tackling teams. In the six years from 2020 through 2025 the Jets ranked in the top half of the NFL just once, and they ranked in the bottom six four times. Yikes! That’s not good. Here are the Jets rankings in the NFL in missed tackles since 2020: 2025 – 27th 2024 – 28th 2023 – 24th 2022 – 14th 2021 – 27th 2020 – 30th 2026 has been a different story thus far. The Jets have missed just 17 tackles in their first four games this season. That number makes them the NFL’s 10th best team in tackling. Bringing in sound tacklers appears to have been a Jets priority in the 2026 offseason, and it is paying dividends early this season. We have seen more wrapping up and less rolling into guys with the shoulder this season. It’s been great to see, but surprisingly it is a bit difficult to find much correlation in missed tackles to a team’s record. Three of the top six teams this season in missed tackles are the Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins. They have combined for a 1-11 record this season. In fact, of the top ten teams in 2026 for missed tackles, just two teams have a winning record. Going back to 2025, seven of the top 16 teams in missed tackles had losing records. It is a somewhat puzzling thing, but missed tackles don’t appear to be much of a factor in wins and losses. Nonetheless, if given a choice, a team would certainly prefer not to miss tackles. For the first time in a long while, the Jets have actually been good at this. If nothing else, it makes the defense more fun to watch. Perhaps it also is a leading indicator that the Jets are finally instilling a more disciplined approach on a team that has been badly in need of it for years. It may not amount to a big deal, but perhaps it’s a small silver lining in what has been a disappointing start to the Aaron Glenn era.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Jets make roster moves ahead of Browns game
summary: The New York Jets have waived receiver Jamaal Pritchett, activated receiver Tim Patrick and elevated linebacker Jaden Keller from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. If the 6’ 5”, 210 pound Patrick plays on Sunday he will add a large, physical presence to the depleted Jets receiver group. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 14: Tim Patrick #17 of the New York Jets looks on prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at MetLife Stadium on August 14, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets have waived receiver Jamaal Pritchett, activated receiver Tim Patrick and elevated linebacker Jaden Keller from the practice squad ahead of their game against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. If the 6’ 5”, 210 pound Patrick plays on Sunday he will add a large, physical presence to the depleted Jets receiver group. Last season Patrick racked up 15 receptions for 187 yards and three touchdowns playing for the Jacksonville Jaguars. For his career Patrick has 191 receptions for 2590 yards and 18 touchdowns. Patrick has not had a 400 yard season since 2021. He will turn 33 years old in a little over a month, and his best years are long behind him, but perhaps Patrick can turn back the clock a bit and contribute to a Jets receiver group that is in need of some assistance. Patrick will take the place of Jamaal Pritchett among Jets receivers. The 23 year old, 5’ 8”, 190 pound second year receiver out of South Alabama made his NFL debut last week after the Jets signed him off their practice squad. Pritchett played just three special teams snaps and returned one kickoff in his first taste of NFL action. As often happens with fringe back of the roster players, that taste of the NFL was short-lived. Pritchett was waived to make room for Patrick. Perhaps he will be re-signed to the practice squad in the coming days. Jaden Keller is a 23 year old, 6’ 3”, 235 pound linebacker out of Virginia Tech. He went undrafted in 2026 and the Jets signed him as an undrafted free agent before releasing him prior to the start of the regular season and adding him to the practice squad. Like Pritchett, Keller made his NFL debut last week when the Jets elevated him from the practice squad. Last week Keller played 14 special teams snaps against the Chicago Bears. During the preseason, Keller had 10 total tackles and a pass defended.
