title: Jets vs Browns Pre-Game Ball
summary: Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Braelon Allen #0 of the New York Jets scores a touchdown against the Green Bay Packers during the second quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Plenty of people hand out game balls after the game. That’s easy. Watch the game, see who does well, give them the game ball. We’re doing something a little different. We’re handing out a pre-game ball. Before we watch the game, let’s settle on a player or players we think might be a decisive advantage for the Jets in the upcoming game. Occasionally we might hand out a pre-blame ball. If we think the Jets are going to get slaughtered, we’ll try to identify a prime culprit. One caveat: the quarterback is off limits. Nothing personal against quarterbacks, but they are obviously the most important players on the field. We could give out a pre-game or pre-blame ball to the quarterback virtually every week, but that would be boring, so we’re not going to do it. We’ll try to identify somebody besides the quarterback for the glory or the ignominy. This approach comes with the obvious drawback that predictions are difficult, especially about the future. We’re destined to get many of these wrong. No matter. We’ll have some laughs along the way. Let’s get to it. The Jets pre-game ball for the Jets game against the Cleveland Browns goes to (drum roll please) – Braelon Allen! The Jets are a bit of a mess on offense going into this game. They are missing starting running back Breece Hall, starting guard Dylan Parham and three receivers – Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr and Arian Smith on offense. In addition, the weather is likely to be a mess, with the game expected to be played in a driving rain storm. All of this makes the Jets’ passing offense carrying the day a bit unlikely. Consequently the team may need the the running game to step up and carry the offense. Fortunately for the Jets the Browns have struggled defending against the run. They rank 24th in the NFL in yards allowed per rushing attempt at 4.6. In addition, the Browns have struggled to run the ball on offense, ranking 25th in the NFL with 3.7 yards per carry. Braelon Allen has never had more than 81 yards from scrimmage in any game in his NFL career. He has rarely been given the opportunity to carry the load for the Jets. Sunday seems like a great day to change that. Bad weather games were made for big bruising backs. In bad weather against a Browns team that struggles to defend against the run the Jets may see Allen as the best path to victory. If they can find some success in running the ball early the Jets will probably ride Allen as far as he can take them. Braelon Allen, come on down! Your breakout game awaits. You get your opportunity on Sunday. Let’s see you run with it. What about you? Who would you give the pre-game ball to? Let us know in the comments.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Jets vs Browns Game Day Forecast
summary: The New York Jets are home in East Rutherford, New Jersey today. They will be taking on the Cleveland Browns. The game is scheduled to start shortly after 1:00 pm EDT. The game will be played in a driving rain storm. Cloudy skies will prevail for the entirety of the game. Winds will be moderate […]
full_text: METLIFE STADIUM, EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY, UNITED STATES - 2025/06/19: A general view shows MetLife Stadium at the end of the FIFA Club World Cup football match between SE Palmeiras and Al Ahly FC. SE Palmeiras won 2-0 over Al Ahly FC. (Photo by Nicolò Campo/LightRocket via Getty Images) | LightRocket via Getty Images The New York Jets are home in East Rutherford, New Jersey today. They will be taking on the Cleveland Browns. The game is scheduled to start shortly after 1:00 pm EDT. The game will be played in a driving rain storm. Cloudy skies will prevail for the entirety of the game. Winds will be moderate and variable at around 10 to 15 mph with a few higher gusts out of the east southeast to start the game, shifting to the east in the second half. Temperatures will be in the low 60s to start the game, holding steady throughout the game. Relative humidity will be high, starting in the mid 80% range and rising slightly to the upper 80s as the game progresses. There will be a near 100% chance of precipitation throughout the game. The rain will get heavier as the game progresses. In short, these will be sloppy, nasty conditions for players and fans alike. Fans will want to bring their rain gear. For the players ball security will be an issue, as the ball will be wet and slick. Fumbles and dropped passes could be a problem, and the passing game will be difficult. Enjoy the game everyone.

title: Jets vs Browns: Five Questions with Dawgs By Nature
summary: The New York Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Sunday for the 5th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Cleveland Browns. The Browns have won three straight games coming into this game and are 3-1 on the year. They are coming off a tight dominant 27-24 victory […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 1: Denzel Boston #12 of the Cleveland Browns completes a catch against the Pittsburgh Steelers during an NFL football game at Huntington Bank Field on October 1, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets are at home in East Rutherford, New Jersey on Sunday for the 5th game of their 2026 campaign. They will be facing the Cleveland Browns. The Browns have won three straight games coming into this game and are 3-1 on the year. They are coming off a tight dominant 27-24 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers last week. Previewing this matchup, Chris Pokorny, Site Manager at Dawgs By Nature , was kind enough to answer a few questions regarding the 2026 Cleveland Browns. 1. What are the Browns’ biggest advantages over the Jets in this game? Where might the Browns be at a disadvantage? For the Browns’ biggest advantage, I think we have to look at the player who is doing his job at an elite level right now in CB Denzel Ward. I’ve never seen him start a season this good, and that’s for a guy who has always been solid. He is completely shutting down opposing receivers. I’m not particularly high on the Jets’ group of receivers to begin with, so I like Cleveland’s ability to stop the Jets’ passing game pretty well. The part I’m concerned about is the Browns’ run blocking, and it’s not because of the Jets’ rushing attack. It has to do with the fact that defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr are both out with injuries. Veteran Maliek Collins plays well, but he’s not going to be an everydown player. After that, the team has Adin Huntington and will try to throw together some other rotation to help out. Cleveland hasn’t allowed a rushing touchdown this year, but if the Jets get down in the red zone, they might be able to attack the middle. 2. The Browns, like the Jets, have struggled to find a long term answer at quarterback. They currently have four quarterbacks: Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Taylen Green and Dillon Gabriel. Can any of these guys be a long term answer for the Browns at quarterback? Will the Browns be shopping for a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL draft? I’ll start with the most obvious one: I’d say No for Dillon Gabriel. I just don’t think he has the ability to get the ball downfield at an NFL level to be a long term starter. A backup, sure, but not someone you bank your future on. Taylen Green is an unknown, but our perception of him is that he’s probably a guy who can be a backup for his threat to run, but again, not someone expected to throw the ball at a high level long term. I think Shedeur Sanders has displayed a lot of intriguing elements, to where I see the potential for him to be a long-term answer. However, with the stockpile of draft picks the Browns have in 2027, I don’t think Sanders is viewed highly enough to pass on a quarterback in the first round of the draft. Deshaun Watson is a bit of a wildcard right now. Prior to this season, everyone would have said 0% chance. But, he’s legitimately looked the best he has in a Browns uniform. It’s still not fantastic per se, but if he keeps building off of this and leads the Browns to the playoffs, then I think all of a sudden we could be having a discussion we never expected to have regarding his future with the team. 3. Can you give us a synopsis of what the 2026 Browns draft class has looked like so far, and what you expect from them as the year goes on? It has been great. There are everyday contributions from five players. Last year on offense, the entire offensive line was in shambles, and the wide receiver group was among the worst in football. The Browns took left tackle Spencer Fano in the first round, and he’s played every snap at the position and done a fair job there. They also drafted Austin Barber in the third round — he was projected to be a backup offensive tackle, but due to injuries in camp, they gave him a shot at right guard. He won the job, has played every snap there, and has actually performed like the team’s best offensive linemen. Then, at receiver, I’m sure you guys have heard about KC Concepcion in the first round and Denzel Boston early in the second round. Concepcion does a nice job in space and providing that bit of electricity, while Boston is a big target who Deshaun Watson trusts on catches where you need a guy who can go get the ball with his hands, as well as intermediate and downfield throws. Lastly, second-round safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has been getting more reps as he plays the center field role beautifully, being given the freedom to use his instincts to jump passes. These past two years of draft classes have been absolute home runs for the Browns, and it’s the reason they are 3-1 and turning heads right now. 4. Every team has a player or two who may be somewhat unfamiliar to other teams’ fans but is known to be an unsung hero by fans of his own team. Who are the Browns’ unsung heroes? If possible give us one guy on each side of the ball. On offense, I talked about several offensive players in the previous question, so I’ll go with tight end Harold Fannin. He was one of the team’s key draft picks last year, but he leads the team in touchdowns and always has a knack for gaining several extra yards after contact, even when it doesn’t look like he will. On defense, I again spoiled this a bit with my talk of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren in the previous question, so just know that the answer would have been him. To throw a little twist to this answer, I’ll pick a guy who Jets fans know very well: linebacker Quincy Williams. My first exposure to him was in Week 1, and I wasn’t too happy. But someone lit a fire under him since then, to where he seems like a tackling machine who plays with a great intensity in finishing plays. I’ve been impressed, and his PFF scores have reflected it as well. 5. If you were an opposing head coach, how would you attack this Browns team on offense and on defense? As I mentioned earlier, solely because of the Browns’ defensive tackle issue, I’d try to attack the middle with the Jets’ run game. Cleveland’s defensive coordinator has done a nice job coming up with a different game plan each week based on his opponent, so it makes it a little more unpredictable for opposing offenses to know what to expect heading into the game. For the Browns’ offense, I’d utilize as many zone coverage drops as I can against Deshaun Watson — ones that start near the middle of the field and leak out toward the seams and sidelines. Watson couldn’t recognize that all of training camp, and was victimized by the same type of interception in Week 1. Although it hasn’t been an issue the past three games, part of that has been smarter play by Watson of taking the smart open plays short, while maintaining those occasional downfield throws. But, I imagine there is still an opportunity to bait him.
author: MacGregor Wells

title: Three Things I’m Looking at in the Jets vs Browns Game
summary: I will be at MetLife Stadium this Sunday to see our beloved New York Jets take on the Cleveland Browns! If you will be too, say hello to fellow GGN Contributor BoyGreen25 and me at parking lot J2 for our tailgate. When we looked at the schedule in June, I specifically picked this game for […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - NOVEMBER 09: Isaiah Williams #18 of the New York Jet returns a punt 74 yards for a touchdown during the first quarter of the game against the Cleveland Browns on November 9, 2025 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I will be at MetLife Stadium this Sunday to see our beloved New York Jets take on the Cleveland Browns! If you will be too, say hello to fellow GGN Contributor BoyGreen25 and me at parking lot J2 for our tailgate. When we looked at the schedule in June, I specifically picked this game for our tailgate because I wanted to make sure we’d be witnessing a win for our annual (and only) in-person experience. I even figured it could be the Jets’ first win of the season. Now that the game is here, the Jets are 1-3, and the same fanbase that merely eight days ago was ecstatic about the progress shown in a ‘competitive loss’ is now up in arms and ready to fire the same coach they were so confident in during those moral victories. Perspective is really an interesting concept because I think most fans expected 1-3 or 2-2 heading into this game. I heard zero fans, not even the most optimistic ones, predicting 4-0 or 3-1 heading into Week 5. Is it the contrast of beating the Titans by two scores in Week 1 to then losing to the Tyson Bagent Bears in Week 4? Was that Week 1 performance so shocking that people got their hopes up and couldn’t fathom finishing the NFC North gauntlet 0-3, even though that was the consensus-discussed scenario all summer? Or is it more that the pain of losing to backup quarterbacks is so painful that losing by two scores to Tyson Bagent just drummed up the decades of PTSD associated with our “Same Old Jets”? For what it’s worth, teams in today’s NFL lose to backup QBs fairly routinely. The same New England Patriots that just beat invincible Josh Allen and the Bills started their season losing to a backup QB. The reigning Super Bowl Champion Seattle Seahawks lost to a backup QB. Losing to a backup QB is far from a death sentence in today’s NFL. Losing four games straight, however, has a much higher mortality rate. Still, I respectfully disagree that this game is a “must-win.” Of course, should the Jets win? Yes. Would it go a long way toward quieting the fanbase’s uproar? Yes. But they could lose this game and then win the next three (Patriots, Dolphins, Raiders), and the entire fanbase would be completely revitalized and incredibly hopeful for the Week 9 showdown at Arrowhead Stadium against the Chiefs. The season will have a pulse on Monday, October 12, no matter what happens on Sunday. Let’s assess some of the things worth looking at during the game on Sunday and let’s see their impact on the final outcome of the game: Capture the Flag One of my earliest memories of the Glenn Era is all the bragging he did during press conferences. Glenn blasted the previous regime for all the penalties committed and blamed it on the coaching . He said he would coach the team to be better players, more disciplined, and take specific measures (such as hiring referees for training camp) to right these wrongs. The New York Jets are currently 4th in the NFL in penalties committed per play. They’ve been penalized frequently in all three phases of the game but have apparently earned the most delay-of-game penalties of any team through the first four weeks of any season this century. If you’re curious who leads the league in penalties per play this season, it’s the Cleveland Browns. Another fun stat: in Week 5, no NFL defense was more penalized than the New York Jets. They were tied with the Cleveland Browns’ defense, which fell victim to Aaron Rodgers’ infamous hard counts on Thursday Night Football. Between the Jets’ delay-of-game penalties and the Browns’ neutral-zone infractions, we’ll see if any chicanery happens on the lines when these teams match up on Sunday. The goal is simple – don’t commit penalties. Last week specifically, the Jets lost several interceptions to penalties that could’ve been avoided. It would’ve been incredible to end an interception drought with a downpour of them, but the team’s (lack of) discipline wouldn’t let that happen. Needless to say, had those interceptions stuck, the game’s outcome might’ve been very different. Pressure Cooker You may look at this article and say, “yeah yeah yeah, any football game can have the same three things to look at,” and list generic goals of every football game. Every football game, you want to take care of the football, move the ball down the field, and pressure the opposing quarterback. This article matters because it’s not that simple: every team is different and has different things going on. Each team’s different qualities get highlighted when they face off against each other. Deshaun Watson seems much closer to his Houston Texan form than any other version of Watson we’ve seen in orange. Not only is his accuracy back on all three levels, but he’s also elusive and confident on his feet again. He is third in the NFL for rushing yards among QBs and is only behind Josh Allen in rushing attempts. They have designed run plays for him, but he’s most lethal when there’s blanket coverage downfield, and he finds his lane in the pocket. This is where I’m calling for the Jets, currently 5th worst in the NFL at generating pressures per dropback (18.2%), to finally generate pressure on dropbacks. To be 4th in blitzes per dropback (33.6%) and 28th in pressures per dropback is a level of embarrassment I’m not ready to fully discuss right now. There’s been a lot of unwarranted criticism hurled at number two overall pick David Bailey, and some debate about whether it’s a talent issue or a usage issue. If I’m weighing in, I’d lean toward usage, since he’s already dropped back into coverage more times this season than he did in his entire senior year at Texas Tech. Regardless of the true answer to that debate, it’s up to Aaron Glenn to find some way to get into Deshaun’s face this Sunday. If not, he’ll be free to sit back, diagnose, and scramble as he pleases on his way to carving up the Jets defense. Will we see Will McDonald IV be relevant in any way? My call is for Bailey and Ossai to set the edge and force Deshaun into the middle of the field where the Jets have so many strong tacklers. With all the different things you can say about the Jets this year, you can’t say they’re bad at tackling. It’s been one of their strengths all year. 2-Minute Drill You may have seen my earlier article about Aaron Glenn’s biggest weakness, and I hope it stays front and center for them every day until they get this monkey off their back. With the first interception in 21 games finally caught, I’d imagine they’ll keep coming here and there for a team that has finally addressed the elephant in the room. The next largest elephant in that room is their horrid play at the end of halves. After the failure at the end of the first half of the Bears game, the Jets’ streak is now up to 15 consecutive scoreless 2-minute drill attempts. I didn’t do a deep dive into every NFL team’s 2-minute drill history, but in that article I explained that I looked at every team’s 2-minute drills this season, and since everyone has scored points at least once this season, we can say with certainty that this streak of 15 is the largest active scoreless streak in the NFL. Nick Folk’s game-winning field goal against the Falcons in Week 13 was the last time they scored any points within the last two minutes of a half. Overall, Aaron Glenn’s Jets have scored six times in 34(!) attempts. That is a putrid 17.6% rate. What’s even crazier is how often the Jets end up with the ball in their hands in this situation. Some teams had only two or three opportunities through the first four weeks, while the Jets have had six! So it makes it even worse to have so many opportunities and still come up short so often. If the Jets…

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: Cleveland Browns
summary: The New York Jets return home on Sunday, looking to avoid their third four-game losing streak in Aaron Glenn’s first 22 games as head coach against the surprising 3-1 Cleveland Browns. New York has won three of their last four games against Cleveland, including a 27-20 win last season. Let’s break down the Browns’ roster […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 09: Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns carries the ball against Tony Adams #22 of the New York Jets during the first half in the game at MetLife Stadium on November 09, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets return home on Sunday, looking to avoid their third four-game losing streak in Aaron Glenn’s first 22 games as head coach against the surprising 3-1 Cleveland Browns. New York has won three of their last four games against Cleveland, including a 27-20 win last season. Let’s break down the Browns’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks The controversial Deshaun Watson has rebounded from a shaky start to the season to lead the Browns to three straight wins by a total of 10 points. He has a quarterback rating of over 100 and has rushed for 10 first downs. However, he’s averaging just 214 passing yards per game and has been sacked 11 times with two interceptions and three fumbles. After going 3-4 as a starter last season, with 10 interceptions, Shedeur Sanders is now back to being the number two. Sixth round rookie Taylen Green has been the number three, although Dillon Gabriel was activated for practice from injured reserve this week. He will presumably replace Green on the roster soon, but not this weekend. Offensive Line The Browns have completely overhauled their starting offensive line since last season. Left tackle Spencer Fano was drafted in the first round and right guard Austin Barber was drafted in the third round, joining three veteran additions as the new starting group. At right tackle is Tytus Howard, who was acquired via trade. He has five penalties in four games so far this season. The left guard is Zion Johnson, who was a free agency signing who was previously with the Chargers. Center Elgton Jenkins, who will be making his return after missing last Thursday night’s win over the Steelers, was signed in March after his release from the Packers. The bench at least has a familiar look, as Luke Wypler, Dawand Jones and Teven Jenkins all started games for the Browns last year with Wypler also having started the last game at center. In addition, Zak Zinter has been with the team for three years, although he didn’t start in any of his four appearances last season. All three of his NFL starts were in his rookie year. (Teven) Jenkins has been ruled out of Sunday’s game but the other offensive lineman on the roster, fifth round rookie Parker Brailsford, will probably still be inactive. Running Backs The Browns’ lead back is Quinshon Judkins, who racked up 827 yards and seven touchdowns last season despite only playing in 14 games. He’s off to a bit of a slow start this year, though, as he averages just 3.0 yards per carry. Raheim Sanders only has six carries as the number two, but he’s used a lot in the passing game and has combined with Judkins for 25 catches in the first four games. The number three back is Jaleel McLaughlin, who only has two carries this season – although one went for a 28-yard touchdown. Veteran Michael Burton is also on the roster as a fullback. Pass catchers The Browns were surprisingly led in receiving by a rookie last year, as tight end Harold Fannin led the team in catches, yards and touchdown receptions, while 2024 pro bowler Jerry Jeudy had a down year. Youngsters are leading the way this year too. Second round rookie receiver Denzel Boston leads them in receiving yards and has flashed big play potential with 46 and 55-yard touchdowns as he is dangerous after the catch. First rounder KC Concepcion has also made an impact and he’s tied with Fannin on 17 receptions to lead the team. Jeudy has once again made a slow start, but he is still a starter. Backups Isaiah Bond, ex-Jet Malachi Corley and Tylan Wallace have just two catches between them. Wallace is ruled out for Sunday anyway. Fannin once again leads the Browns with three touchdown catches, but he no longer has David Njoku as a fellow starter at tight end. With seventh round rookie Carsen Ryan ruled out on Sunday, Blake Whiteheart will be the primary backup with Burton perhaps contributing here too. Whiteheart only has two catches this year, but one went for a touchdown. Defensive Line The Browns will be shorthanded on the defensive line this weekend, as last year’s first round pick Mason Graham and key reserve Mike Hall were both ruled out. In addition, Kalia Davis – who is on injured reserve but had his practice window opened this week – missed practice on Thursday and Friday so isn’t ready to be activated to provide reinforcements. Graham had been making a big impact with four sacks in the first four games, so that’s a significant loss. The starters will now be Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington with two of Cleveland’s three practice squad defensive tackles (Sam Kamara, Chris Williams and Zion Logue) presumably set to be elevated. Collins is a solid player who had 6.5 sacks last year, but the Browns should be downgraded from a unit which was already the ninth-worst in the NFL for yards per attempt allowed. Cleveland will be at full strength on the defensive line, although Jared Verse hasn’t been very productive so far as he deals with the pressure of being Myles Garrett’s replacement. Verse, who was included in the trade that sent Garrett to the Rams, was a pro bowler last season with 7.5 sacks, but has just two quarterback hits and no sacks so far this season. The other starting defensive end is Isaiah McGuire with Derek Barnett healthy enough to come off the bench despite missing practice earlier in the week. Sam Williams will also be in the rotation. The Browns lost a potential starter, Alex Wright, to an Achilles injury in August so he’s out for the year, which is why they added Barnett. Wright had 5.5 sacks last season. Linebackers The Browns’ linebacker unit is led by last year’s defensive rookie of the year, Carson Schwesinger, who racked up 156 tackles in 2025 and leads the team with 35 this year. With Devin Bush now in Chicago and Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah still on the PUP list, the other starter is a familiar face, Quincy Williams, who signed for the Browns during the offseason. The main thing that is different about Williams’ role with the Browns is that he’s blitzing at a much higher rate. The Jets have had some issue with blitz pick-ups in key moments, so hopefully that’s something they’ll have been working on all week. Easton Mascarenas-Arnold is also listed as a starter, but the Browns rarely have more than two linebackers on the field so he’s only played 20 snaps in the first four games. The backups are Winston Reid and fifth round rookie Justin Jefferson. Defensive Backs The Browns’ secondary is led by Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward, and the other starting cornerback is Tyson Campbell, who was acquired via trade last season and ended up with 18 pass breakups. The primary slot cornerback is Myles Harden, who currently leads the team with three pass breakups. Mekhi Blackmon also made one start this year in a game Campbell missed. The Browns have two reliable veterans at safety in Ronnie Hickman and Grant Delpit, but they also have second round rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, who has been seeing some playing time in three-safety sets. Additional secondary depth comes in the shape of cornerbacks Noah Igbinoghene and Toriano Pride Jr. and safeties Daniel Thomas and Donovan McMillan. Special Teams The Browns’ placekicker is Andre Szmyt, who only missed three field goals last season and is perfect on all kicks this year, including a 56-yard game winner in the last game. Their punter is the veteran Corey Bojorquez, who is putting up big numbers so far this season. In the return game, Corley is listed as the main kickoff returner, although Sanders had the most success so far with a 74-yard runback. Concepcion is the punt returner, with Boston listed as his backup. You will no doubt recall how first quarter touchdown returns…

summary: The Eagles offensive line has already seen significant changes through just four games, and they turned to yet another new grouping in the second half against in London. Right guard Tyler Steen left the game with a shoulder injury and after heading to the locker room, he was listed as questionable to return. Fred Johnson […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles offensive line has already seen significant changes through just four games, and they turned to yet another new grouping in the second half against in London. Right guard Tyler Steen left the game with a shoulder injury and after heading to the locker room, he was listed as questionable to return. Injury Updates: DB Michael Carter II (abdomen) is out. OLB Jalyx Hunt (ankle/knee) and G Tyler Steen (shoulder) are questionable to return. — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 11, 2026 Fred Johnson stepped in to that role, and joins Markel Bell, Willie Lampkin, Jake Majors, and Jordan Mailata up front. Quarterback Jalen Hurts has been affected by the pass rush, but was able to get the ball out much faster this week and connect with his receivers. The run game is decimated by injuries, with the team already without Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby, and then losing Will Shipley in the first half on Sunday. The team has been able to get things going despite all of the adversity they’re facing, but long-term, the roster depth is more than a little concerning.
author: Alexis Chassen

full_text: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images | Getty Images With just under a minute before halftime, Eagles safety Michael Carter took a big hit while he was trying to tackle Bhayshul Tuten, and came off the field. He was ultimately ruled out with an abdomen injury halfway through the third quarter. Injury Updates: DB Michael Carter II (abdomen) is out. OLB Jalyx Hunt (ankle/knee) and G Tyler Steen (shoulder) are questionable to return. — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 11, 2026 Carter had six total tackles before leaving the game, and new Eagles DB Kenny Moore was put in at safety. DC Vic Fangio has hesitated when it comes to putting Moore in at safety, often pointing to the veteran having so few career snaps at the position. Still, the Eagles aren’t really in a position to make better decisions thanks to other injuries. Marcus Epps is still out with a injury, and the depth at the position pretty much stops there. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. being ejected early in the game doesn’t help things either. They’ll have to rely on Moore’s experience to offset his lack of playing time at safety, and hopefully Carter is able to return sooner rather than later. Regardless, Howie Roseman has his work cut out for him in the coming days.

title: Eagles vs. Jaguars: Live score updates, highlights, injury news
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are in London to take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 9:30 AM Eastern kickoff. Entering this game at 2-2, the Birds are looking to avoid dropping below .500 for the first time since the 2021 NFL season. It’ll take a big effort to pull off the upset; Nick Sirianni’s squad is […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Jalen Hurts of Philadelphia Eagles in action during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are in London to take on the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 9:30 AM Eastern kickoff. Entering this game at 2-2, the Birds are looking to avoid dropping below .500 for the first time since the 2021 NFL season. It’ll take a big effort to pull off the upset; Nick Sirianni’s squad is 7.5-point underdogs against this Jags team that’s played well since the Liam Coen era began last year. Follow along here for live score updates, highlights, injury news, analysis, and more before this article ultimately turns into our game recap. The best place to actually discuss the game as it happens is still in our open game thread, which you can find here . FIRST QUARTER UPDATES The Eagles won the opening coin toss and decided to defer, per usual. The Jaguars took Jake Elliott’s kickoff to the house. Lol. There were flags on field after Jeremiah Trotter Jr. got in a brawl with Bryan Thomas Jr. and both players were ejected. The touchdown was also wiped out by offsetting penalties on the Eagles and Jags. Elliott kicked off again and the Jags took over at their own 26-yard line. Trevor Lawrence threw over the middle (which the Jags love to do) for a first down. Jalen Carter drew a holding penalty to knock the Jags’ offense back. Then Carter cooked the Jags’ right guard and strip-sacked Lawrence for a Jags recovery. Then a Jags false start knocked the Jags back to 2nd-and-40. What a wacky start to this game. Facing 3rd-and-37, the Jags went with a quick pass to set up a punt. Five plays, negative eight yards. Strong start by Vic Fangio’s defense. JC swatted the rock pic.twitter.com/VZ4BRSOQBb — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 11, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 42-yard line after an 18-yard Britain Covey punt return. Will Shipley got the first carry of the game. Then a Jalen Hurts pass to Dallas Goedert brought up third down. Facing 3rd-and-3, Hurts hit Goedert short again for a first down. OMG! A THIRD DOWN CONVERSION! IT’S A MIRACLE! Facing 3rd-and-3 again, Hurts ran out of bounds just short of the marker. Facing 4th-and-1 from the Jags’ 37-yard line, Nick Sirianni correctly kept his offense on the field … and did NOT go tush push … but went with a shotgun handoff to Shipley, who appeared to get enough for a first down … but virtual measurement marked him short for a turnover on downs. I get it’s a backup offensive line and the tush push hasn’t been as automatic as it used to be … but that felt like a good spot for it there. At least a better option than a shotgun run. Well, at least the Eagles were able to move the ball a little bit? Six plays, 21 yards. The Jags took over at their own 37-yard line. After two plays, Lawrence hit Parker Washington on a play-action boot for a 51-yard catch-and-run touchdown. Andrew Mukuba was trailing in coverage and missed the open field tackle. Looked wayyyyyy too easy for Washington to score there. EAGLES 0, JAGUARS 7. Drew Mukuba has rotated down from the pre-snap 2-high look WAAAY too aggressively more than a handful of times this year. Here it happens again… #Eagles https://t.co/N2gx9YTQhO — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 11, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 49-yard line after a nice 42-yard return by Britain Covey, who got lit up at the end. Hurts completed a pass to Makai Lemon, who made an impressive contested grab on a bad ball due to unblocked pressure in Hurts’ face on a boot, for no gain. Hurts’ next pass to Goedert was incomplete. Then Hurts’ third down throw to Zach Ertz along the right sideline was too high and out of bounds. Even if the pass is better, we’re really going with a go ball to a 35-year-old Ertz on 3rd-and-12? Three plays, zero yards. Terrible drive. The Jags walk into the end zone on a play-action boot. And then Jalen Hurts has a dude immediately in his face on a play-action boot. A perfect summation of this season. — Rich Hofmann (@rich_hofmann) October 11, 2026 The Jags took over at their own 9-yard line and quickly picked up a first down. Facing 3rd-and-10 after a false start, Lawrence’s third down pass was short of the sticks with Quinyon Mitchell having good coverage on a curl route. Five-and-out for the Jags. Covey was hit late of out bounds but no flag on the Jags. The Eagles took over at their own 36-yard line. Hurts hit Makai Lemon over the middle for a nice first down reception. Good route by the rookie to get open, good throw by Hurts into a tight window. Dameon Pierce took the first carry of his Eagles career for six yards to end the first quarter. Jalen Hurts' 11-yard completion to Makai Lemon at the end of the first quarter was the Eagles' first successful under-center play-action play since the second quarter of Week 2's win in Tennessee. — PHLY Eagles (@PHLY_Eagles) October 11, 2026 #Eagles have scored 3 points in the first quarter in 5 games now this season. Those 3 points were a field goal last week against the Rams. — Ed Kracz (@kracze) October 11, 2026 SECOND QUARTER UPDATES The Eagles moved into field goal range but then the offense got knocked back with a Josh Hines-Allen TFL on Pierce. Facing 3rd-and-8, Nick Sirianni called a timeout with the defense seemingly showing a look the offense wasn’t ready for. Facing 3rd-and-8 for real, the Jags brought a blitz but Hurts hit Wicks on the hot read for a quick first down. Wow, you’re allowed to do that against extra pressure? Facing 3rd-and-10, Hurts hit Wicks on a slant over the middle for a first down. Nice throw for a key conversion. The Eagles went back to the spinner look but the handoff to Pierce was botched for a loss. Facing 3rd-and-goal from the 17-yard line, Hurts went to Wicks and the receiver drew a pass interference penalty on Travis Hunter. Big flag. Two plays later, Shipley found the end zone on a run up the middle, behind Willie Lampkin creating a lane. 13 plays, 64 yards, touchdown. Nice drive by the offense. EAGLES 7, JAGUARS 7. Will Shipley finds pay dirt and gets the @Eagles on the board. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Dmgr7pJzYt — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Look at Willie Lampkin man I could cry pic.twitter.com/Ys6o4lrMqf — Brenden Deeg (@BrendenDeeg_) October 11, 2026 Nice 13-play, 64-yard TD drive by the offense to tie the game. Jalen Hurts made some really nice throws. Offense converted more third downs (3) on that drive than they did in their past 2 games combined (2). — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 11, 2026 The Jags took over at their own 35-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-21 after the Jags recovered Jalen Carter’s second strip-sack of the game, Lawrence’s third down pass was overthrown and incomplete. 4 plays, -11 yards, punt. Another good effort by Fangio’s defense. Jalen Carter had 5 career forced fumbles entering today's game, where he has 2 in the first half against the Jags. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) October 11, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 38-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-10, Hurts aired it out to Darius Cooper (the official Eagles wide receiver of Bleeding Green Nation), who made an over-the-shoulder grab and ran to the end zone for a 62-yard touchdown! EAGLES 14, JAGUARS 7. DARIUS COOPER, 62-YARD TOUCHDOWN EAGLES TAKE THE LEAD. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eKpCwhW8QZ — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 Jaguars had not allowed a TD in the first half. They just allowed 2 in the last 4 plays. #Eagles are suddenly masters of 3rd & long. — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) October 11, 2026 It’s amazing what Hurts can do when he doesn’t have a defender in his face 0.1 seconds after snapping the ball. pic.twitter.com/MrutRF3cb8 — CogginToboggan (@CogginToboggan) October…

Greenard was ruled questionable to play despite missing practice all week due to an ankle injury. The Eagles […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Jonathan Greenard #52 looks on during the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 4, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced the inactives list for their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The following Eagles players WILL NOT PLAY: Jonathan Greenard, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Marcus Epps and Hollywood Brown. Greenard was ruled questionable to play despite missing practice all week due to an ankle injury. The Eagles put him through a pregame workout on Sunday morning but they ultimately decided to hold the veteran pass rusher out. Greenard has only been available for two of the Eagles’ five games so far this season. In his absence, the Eagles will roll with Jalyx Hunt, Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa as their four edge defenders. Barkley, Smith, Kendall, Epps, and Brown were all ruled out on the Eagles’ final injury report . With Barkley out, the Eagles have three running backs active for this game: Will Shipley, Dameon Pierce, and Carson Steele. Shipley figures to lead the backfield in touches but don’t sleep on Pierce showing some juice. I don’t think we’ll see Steele touch the ball much. Smitty and Brown being out means the Eagles have five active receivers: Dontayvion Wicks, Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey. Kendall’s absence means the Eagles will be starting Jake Majors, who was called up from the practice squad, at center. He’s making his first-ever start in his first-ever NFL regular season game. Michael Carter II will replace Epps as the Eagles’ safety in nickel packages when Cooper DeJean shifts to the slot. John Ojukwu is making his Eagles regular season debut after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad for this game. Cole Payton is active for the first time in his career. He’d normally be the emergency third quarterback but the Eagles already ruled out enough players where they can just keep Payton active. We’ll see if he gets in on special teams at all. Otherwise, he’s the third QB option behind Jalen Hurts and Tanner McKee now that Andy Dalton is gone. Philadelphia Eagles inactive list EDGE Jonathan Greenard – Injury. RB Saquon Barkley – Injury. WR DeVonta Smith – Injury. OL Drew Kendall – Injury. S Marcus Epps – Injury. WR Hollywood Brown – Injury. Jacksonville Jaguars inactive list No surprises for the Jags. Depth corner Jaylon Jones was ruled out on the final injury report while starting safety Eric Murray was ruled doubtful to play. title: Steelers vs. Colts: Week 5 game picks
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers and Indianapolis Colts will square off this afternoon, as both teams will look to avoid dropping below .500. Which team will get the win? Our staff weighs in with our Week 5 picks. Mike Nicastro: The Steelers are in a bit of disarray at the moment, but the recipe for healing might […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers and Indianapolis Colts will square off this afternoon, as both teams will look to avoid dropping below .500. Which team will get the win? Our staff weighs in with our Week 5 picks. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers are in a bit of disarray at the moment, but the recipe for healing might just be Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts. Jones has been a shell of his former self since returning from his torn Achilles, and it doesn’t help that his top target, Alec Pierce, is still banged up. The Steelers aren’t exactly healthy, either. Jamel Dean’s absence will put more pressure on a secondary that of course just lost Joey Porter Jr. I’d anticipate the Steelers edge rushers to make some big time plays and if they can limit Jonathan Taylor, much like they did last year at home, they should walk away with a victory. But it won’t be as comfortable as last season. Steelers 23, Colts 20 . Ryan Parish : With the exception of the Falcons game, the Steelers are doing the exact opposite of my prediction each week. Just wanted to note that at the top. The forecast calls for rain on Sunday, but regardless the Steelers defense should be expecting a heavy dose of Jonathan Taylor, rain or shine. The Steelers should answer in kind with more calls for their own run game, but getting Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy to abandon their pass happy ways might be too much to ask. The Colts passing game is putrid, but Daniel Jones gets the ball out fast, which could once again neutralize the Pittsburgh pass rush. The Steelers should win. But based on my comments up top, I’m inclined to go with the Colts. Colts 24, Steelers 20 . Joey Bray : After previewing the game with a friend who covers the Colts, I have come to the conclusion that the Steelers and Colts are in similar spots at this point in the season. Both are teams that are underperforming to this point despite being labeled as “win-now” teams heading into the season. However, the biggest stat in this one is that Pittsburgh is 17-2 all-time at home vs. the Colts. Given the unpredictability of the weather and overall volatility of both of these teams, I feel inclined to go with a low scoring affair. This is a classic Steelers bounce back game, I’ll take them to win on a last second field goal over Indy. Steelers 17, Colts 14 . Ryland Bickley : Jonathan Taylor will be a tough matchup for a Derrick Harmon-less Steelers run defense, and the Colts’ cornerback duo of Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward could be a challenge for a Steelers wide receiver room that struggled to separate from man coverage last week. But on the flip side, the Colts’ pass rush has the league’s worst pressure rate this season, which is a good sign towards Aaron Rodgers playing comfortably in the pocket on Sunday. These are two evenly-matched teams, but I have Pittsburgh rebounding at home. Steelers 23, Colts 20. Austin Bechtold : The rain is going to make this game a mess. That plays into the Steelers hands with Daniel Jones struggling with protecting the football. I trust Aaron Rodgers more than Jones in nearly every situation. Injuries are piling up and going to be a factor, making it increasingly necessary for Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard to make an impact. I’m curious to see how the defense performs against Jonathan Taylor. The Steelers limited him to 45 yards rushing last year but without Derrick Harmon and Keeanu Benton not playing up to his new contract, the defense needs to make a statement. I expect the Steelers to bounce back after another frustrating loss in Cleveland and move to 3-2 before a trip south to Tampa Bay. Steelers 24, Colts 21 . Jarrett Bailey: It’s expected to rain upwards of an inch throughout Sunday in Pittsburgh, as the effects of Hurricane Isaias make their way north. The Steelers’ run defense has allowed 4.33 yards per carry over the last two games, and they will have to keep Jonathan Taylor at bay in a game that will be run-heavy on both sides due to the weather. In a low-scoring outing, the Steelers get to 3-2. Steelers 16, Colts 13. Let us know what you think in the comments . Warren has been on a tear during Rico Dowdle’s absence, and even if Dowdle returns Sunday, this is a lock. Given Warren’s ability to create something out of nothing and Aaron Rodgers checking the football down, this can hit after a single reception. Warren hasn’t finished with fewer than 27 yards receiving in a game, and that was Week 1. Add this prop and enjoy the win. Jonathan Taylor anytime TD Few things are as certain as a Taylor touchdown these days. Derrick Henry, Christian McCaffrey, and Taylor are as close to locks as there are in the betting space. If the Colts get into the red zone, it’s easy money and a done deal. Don’t overthink this one. Betting against your favorite team feels wrong, but making money feels better, and this has to be a part of your ticket. Taylor didn’t reach the end zone against Houston, but he has two touchdowns in each of the other three contests. Don’t go crazy and expect two, but one is as safe as it gets. full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are on the eve of Week 5 Sunday in the NFL where the Pittsburgh Steelers will host the Indianapolis Colts in a contest between a pair of 2-2 teams. Ahead of that, a quick mailbag to answer your questions ahead of Week 5. Let’s dive in. Q: Was it the right move to trade away Pickett, Jones and JPJ? And was it the right move to trade them to the Cowboys? The Steelers could have probably gotten better returns with the Bears or Lions, like they did with the Claypool trade… – Polamolecules_Dude A: The problem with comparing every trade to the Claypool trade is that the Bears ridiculously overpaid for Claypool – it was a horrible trade. As for the other three, yes, obviously they should have traded Pickett at the time and I was doing cartwheels around my house when they did. Broderick Jones made sense to move because they weren’t going to keep him, so you may as well get something for him. No, they shouldn’t have traded Porter, they should have given him a normal NFL contract where they guarantee money past the first year. But that’s Art Rooney II for you. Q: Who wins the OL/DL fight on paper? – ChippedHam A: I’d say both defensive lines are superior to the opposing offensive lines. Colts left tackle Bernhard Raimann had a tough week last week against Washington, allowing three pressures and a sack. Right tackle Jalen Travis has allowed 15 pressures this season, which is the fourth most in the league, meaning T.J. Watt, Nick Herbig, and Alex Highsmith should be able to get to Jones. The Colts don’t have elite edge rushers, but Grover Stewart and DeForest Buckner on the inside will be a handful all day. Q: How should the Steelers offense look to attack Indy’s defense in the upcoming game? Where are the Colts weakest? – SteelerSince73! A: Stopping the run. It’s going to be raining all game, meaning the Colts will feed Jonathan Taylor. The Steelers are sixth in stuffed runs and have only allowed three rushing scores this season. If they can limit Taylor and make Daniel Jones beat them, they’ll be in good shape. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Seahawks Nick Emmanwori one step closer to automatic suspension after fine from Chargers game
summary: As expected, there were plenty of fines handed out following a very ugly, penalty-laden Seattle Seahawks win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Also as expected, most of those fines went Seattle’s way, but there’s one fine that is potentially significant in the long term. Cornerback Josh Jobe and Chargers wide receiver Tre Harris were each […]
full_text: As expected, there were plenty of fines handed out following a very ugly, penalty-laden Seattle Seahawks win over the Los Angeles Chargers . Also as expected, most of those fines went Seattle’s way, but there’s one fine that is potentially significant in the long term. Cornerback Josh Jobe and Chargers wide receiver Tre Harris were each dinged for their offsetting personal foul penalties in the first quarter. It’s just a minor scuffle that sees Jobe fined more than Harris, presumably because the latter is on a rookie contract and CBA rules don’t allow for a player to be fined more than 10% of their game check for a first-time offense. Jobe’s fine is the standard first offense. This is the start of the VICIOUS exchange between Tre Harris and Josh Jobe that resulted in a fine for both men. Shocked that they got out of this one alive. That'll be $12,537 for Jobe and $9,870 for Harris. pic.twitter.com/19wcXcZ3tq — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 10, 2026 DeMarcus Lawrence was fined $17,911 for his roughing the passer penalty against Justin Herbert. He went below Herbert’s knees, which is an automatic flag even though the hit was borne out of Lawrence being tripped by the Chargers’ keystone cops routine. That’s consecutive weeks of Lawrence losing money due to hitting the quarterback illegally. By the way how the fuck does shit like this happen. Ingold is so bad pic.twitter.com/7tbrc6bL1z — cenacharger (@cenacharger) October 5, 2026 But the main story of Seattle’s fines is Nick Emmanwori. His ill-conceived headbutt of Chargers guard Cole Strange, which helped gift the Chargers a short field goal to close the first half, resulted in a $14,648 fine for use of helmet. Emmanwori’s other $14,648 fine was for an uncalled hip-drop tackle on Oronde Gadsden II, which is something to pay closer attention to for the rest of the season. The NFL fined Nick Emmanwori $14,648 for what was deemed a hip-drop tackle on Oronde Gadsden. Again, two more of those will result in a one-game suspension. Don't shoot the messenger, please. pic.twitter.com/mbfZvdbwbL — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 10, 2026 Why Nick Emmanwori is now closer to a one-game suspension The NFL has made it a point of emphasis to crack down on several types of personal fouls, implementing a new rule in 2026 that mandates a one-game suspension if there are three offenses committed for any of the following infractions: -Hip-Drop Tackle -Horse Collar Tackle -Launching -Hit on a Defenseless Player -Blindside Block Repeated hip-drop violations resulting in a suspension is not new, as Washington Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu was initially suspended for a game last season before the league rescinded the ban. What has been consistent thus far is NFL officials not flagging hip-drop tackles during the game, while the league office deals with punishment after the fact. Emmanwori can appeal this fine in hopes of getting his money back and zero strikes on his ledger. Otherwise, two more hip-drop tackle fines without any successful appeal will mean he automatically misses a game.

full_text: The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers renew their rivalry on Sunday, with first place in the NFC West on the line at Lumen Field. In both of Seattle’s Super Bowl triumphs, the Seahawks eliminated the 49ers on their way to winning the Lombardi Trophy. Pete Carroll’s final playoff game with the Seahawks ended in a blowout loss at the hands of Brock Purdy and the Niners. Sunday’s matchup is by far the most anticipated on the Week 5 schedule, and we might even see this showdown again at some point in January. This is the first of four consecutive Seahawks games either on national television or as the featured late game in the 1:25 pm PT window. With the Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers moved to the 10 am PT window, almost the entire country will get to see Seahawks vs. 49ers as the second half of the FOX doubleheader. If you’re a Seahawks fan in Arizona, Michigan, parts of Wisconsin, Minnesota, North Dakota, northern Indiana, and Toledo, Ohio, you have my sympathies. The 506 Sports map shows a lot of red for Seahawks-49ers, which is the only red I want to see on Sunday. Kevin Burkhardt, Tom Brady, Erin Andrews, and Tom Rinaldi will all be present for the NFL on FOX, which has billed this as “America’s Game of the Week.” It’s the first time the Seahawks have gotten the lead crew on either FOX or CBS this season. title: An ode to future Seahawks fans
summary: (Editor’s note: The following is a guest post by Field Gulls community member, Kasey McKillip!) This is dedicated to the fan of Seattle Seahawks’ future.  You will be interested in seeing how your team did in the days of seasons past. You’ll be proud of the 1983 team who not only made the playoffs for […]
full_text: (Editor’s note: The following is a guest post by Field Gulls community member, Kasey McKillip!) This is dedicated to the fan of Seattle Seahawks’ future. You will be interested in seeing how your team did in the days of seasons past. You’ll be proud of the 1983 team who not only made the playoffs for the first time but won two playoffs games to make it to the AFC Championship decider. That’s right – we used to be in the AFC. Weird right!? Then you will see how we made it to the Super Bowl in 2005. After this you will make your way to 2013. 2013 – what a special season and you will just absorb it in moments. Our best ever 13-3 regular season record. You will see how we strolled past the New Orleans Saints and San Francisco 49ers before dominating the Denver Broncos to finally win it all. You will see so much but yet you will miss even more. You won’t appreciate the previous year’s excruciating and unbearable Divisional Playoff loss to the Falcons that it’s still a source of PTSD just to think about it. For your own benefit, never ever go to YouTube to watch it. You will see we won the season opener over the Carolina Panthers, but the scores alone don’t reveal how anxious we were until a heads-up play from Earl Thomas saved the day. You will see we started the season 4-0 for the first time, but you won’t see the euphoria we felt after a fantastic pick six from Richard Sherman sent the Houston Texans game to overtime. You will see we finally lost to the Indianapolis Colts, but you won’t see how helpless we felt as the Colts went on an 11-0 run in the final quarter. You will see the rest of the season in seconds as your eyes scroll through the scores, but you won’t see the rising confidence we felt as we collectively realized this was a very special team. You will see the 23-17 victory in the NFC Championship Game but you won’t grasp the nerves we felt as the 49ers had the ball 1st & 10 from our 18 with 30 seconds left. Nor will you know how tense we were as that ball sailed in the air. Lastly you won’t know our pure joy when Richard Sherman made the mother of all knockdowns to send the ball into a waiting Malcolm Smith’s hands sending us to the Super Bowl. Okay this one you can watch on YouTube . No. 58: @Seahawks CB @RSherman_25 tips pass for interception in 2013 NFC Championship (Jan. 19, 2014) #NFL100 📺: NFL 100 Greatest Plays on @NFLNetwork pic.twitter.com/umTrRfDKr7 — NFL (@NFL) September 14, 2019 You won’t have to wait two weeks for the Super Bowl, you can read up about it immediately after and there you will see the perfect game unfold. You won’t see how we felt as we came to the realization we were finally going to do it. After so many heartbreakers and different ways we contrived to miss out or misfortune or bad luck conspired against that, there will be no excuses required this way. Will you shed tears of joy like we did? Probably not. And all this shows that being a sports fan is to experience every moment with the team, ride every bump and enjoy the highs while enduring the lows. To finally win it all, isn’t just about winning the final game of the season, it’s a culmination of a journey that starts the second the previous Super Bowl is over. A long spring and summer. Pre-season, regular season, playoffs. Reading about it is devoid of emotion and passion. It’s like looking at a picture of a delicious apple and thinking that is the same as tasting it. Winning a Super Bowl is the ultimate and each one is amazing in its own way but there is nothing like your first, like the team’s first. You will know what I mean when you get to experience your first Super Bowl victory live in real time!!

title: Week 5 Score Prediction: Seahawks vs 49ers
summary: The Seattle Seahawks won versus the Los Angeles Chargers in an ugly home game, and the leaders on the team held a team meeting earlier this week to emphasize cleaning up how they play. They will need to play cleaner this coming week as they are set to face the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers who […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks won versus the Los Angeles Chargers in an ugly home game , and the leaders on the team held a team meeting earlier this week to emphasize cleaning up how they play. They will need to play cleaner this coming week as they are set to face the 4-0 San Francisco 49ers who are currently first in point differential in the NFL . Can the 3-1 Seahawks beat their division rivals? What could be the score? Let’s take a look at the numbers and find out. Seahawks advanced stats rankings The Seahawks per FTN’s DVOA data are ranked 6th in total DVOA, 16th in offensive DVOA, first in defensive DVOA, and 17th in special Teams DVOA. Per EPA data, they are ranked second in total defensive EPA and defensive EPA per play, meanwhile they are 16th in total offensive EPA and offensive EPA per play. The Seahawks are sixth in point differential currently with a +32 point differential over opponents. They are averaging 26.3 points per game , with three games in which they scored 30+ points. They are holding opponents to an average of 18.3 points, which ranks fifth in the NFL. 49ers advanced stats rankings The 49ers are ranked first in total DVOA, first in offensive DVOA, fifth in defensive DVOA, and 22nd in special teams DVOA. For EPA, the 49ers are ranked first in both total offensive EPA and offensive EPA per play, and ranked 18th in total defensive EPA and defensive EPA per play. They are ranked first in point differential with a +58 point differential, and are averaging 30.5 points per game and are holding opponents to 16 points per game. Calculating the Score SEA 26.3 + SF Opponents 16 = 42.3/2= 21.15 SF 30.5+ SEA Opponents 18.3= 48.8/2= 24.4 Score Prediction: 24-21, 49ers Now in past weeks I have also taken into account how much teams general beat their opposition. Per Pro Football Reference the 49ers margin of victory is 14.5 point. Rounded up to 15, that would mean the Seahawks would only score 9 points. Second Score Prediction: 24-9, 49ers This is looking to be a close game, and historically the Seahawks and 49ers have played one another close. I went into some analytics and have a different (more optimistic, winning) take on the score prediction over on The Hawks Eye Podcast with my weekly analytics show Eye On The Numbers. I go into key players, how they have played in previous games this year, how the opposing defenses have defended skill players, to see how they would preform in this matchup. I have the Seahawks scoring four touchdowns and a field goal, and the 49ers scoring three touchdowns and a field goal. Jaxson Smith-Njiba is averaging two touchdowns a game, AJ Barner is likely good for a touchdown, and if not, Emanuel Wilson showed he can score a touchdown both as a receiver and rushing the ball into the endzone. The Seahawks could score five touchdowns and a field goal (which I would be more than happy with), but with the 49ers holding opponents to 16 points a game, let’s air on the side of caution and say four. For the 49ers, Mike Evans has two games with a touchdown so I think he could be good for one touchdown, Christian McCaffery has been averaging one rushing touchdown a game, and George Kittle is good for a touchdown. There are the 49ers three touchdowns right there. Now, the 49ers are averaging 30+ points a game, and the Seahawks have three games of 30+ points this season. Both McCaffery and Kittle have a game with two touchdowns, so they could get above 30+ points. However, their 30+ point games were versus the Dolphins and the Cardinals, both of whom have weaker defenses than the Rams and the Broncos who held them under 30 points. With the Seahawks having the number one DVOA defense, I believe the Seahawks can hold them to under 30 points. My Score Prediction: 31-24, Seahawks Victory If you would like to listen to how I came up with that score and more, you can listen to the podcast here: What are your score predictions? Who do you think will win? Leave your predictions in the comments and as always, Go Hawks!

title: 49ers’ unheralded D-Line is buying them a valuable luxury
summary: The 49ers will get a boost on the defensive line in Week 5, with last year’s first-round pick Mykel Williams primed to make his return against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Williams’ first appearance since tearing his ACL last November in a win over the New York Giants will give the 49ers much-needed extra depth […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 4: Keion White #56 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes the quarterback during the game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Broncos 24-14. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers will get a boost on the defensive line in Week 5, with last year’s first-round pick Mykel Williams primed to make his return against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Williams’ first appearance since tearing his ACL last November in a win over the New York Giants will give the 49ers much-needed extra depth up front and a starter who operate as a base end and kick inside on pass-rushing downs. And, with star edge rusher Nick Bosa seen practicing on a side field on Thursday as he targets a return in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders, the 49ers’ situation on the D-Line is looking up. When Bosa joined Williams on the sideline with a calf injury, the Niners appeared to be in something of a desperate position on the defensive side of the trenches with C.J. West, Alfred Collins (out for the season) and Sam Okuayinonu all on injured reserve. The injury issues the 49ers have dealt with on the defensive line furthered the perception of it being a position group in need of reinforcements via the trade market. But the 49ers have pieced things together extremely well without a host of players expected to be D-Line contributors, with several unheralded players stepping up in hugely impressive fashion to aid both the pass rush and the run defense. Height leads surprising pass rush performance After missing the Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals due to surgery on a broken hand, rookie edge rusher Romello Height returned in the Week 4 victory over the Denver Broncos with a club on that hand and produced the best performance of his young career. Indeed, Height had the sixth-highest pressure rate among all edge rushers with at least 20 pass rush snaps last week, his performance with the club drawing praise from defensive coordinator Raheem Morris. Morris told his press conference on Thursday: “He had a couple of really good rushes. Was able to get around there and do some really good things. Obviously it’s hard to get on and off blocks sometimes. He got caught up with that [Denver Broncos OL Quinn Meinerz] 77 for that Denver team, that’s a pretty tough guy, a couple of times in there and got him in a vulnerable position. But, Romello’s a dog and I love the way he competes, the way he plays. He’s going to go out there regardless. He might have two clubs on and go out there. He’s that kind of guy. So, I’m just fired up he was able to compete and go out there and help us get a win.” Best game to date for Romello Height. He finished with the 6th-highest pass rush win % among all EDGE rushers with at least 20 PR snaps in Week 4. This is why the 49ers drafted him. FWIW, Keion White was 13th. They were winning. The ball was just coming out hot. pic.twitter.com/Ny2SlSvlCI — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) October 5, 2026 In addition to the impressive showing of Height, the 49ers got some value edge rush production from Ogbo Okoronkwo as he registered two pressures against the Broncos, per Pro Football Focus. Okoronkwo was released by the 49ers this week to make room on the 53-man roster for Williams before being re-signed to the practice squad. Osa Odighizuwa and Keion White also stood out. Defensive tackle Odighizuwa had two pressures, with White — whose ability to operate effectively inside and out has proven a huge plus for San Francisco to start the season — had three. The 49ers obviously need Nick Bosa (and Mykel Williams) back asap. But they're getting some good stuff from the guys they do have in the rotation. Nice, clean win from Okoronkwo here. pic.twitter.com/pnrGxnrswi — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 7, 2026 Though there were expectations around Odighizuwa following his offseason trade from the Dallas Cowboys, without Bosa on the field for the last two weeks the 49ers have largely had to lean on unheralded defensive linemen for pass rush production, and the success of those lesser-known players is reflected by the fact the 49ers ended Week 4 tied fourth in the NFL with a team ESPN pass rush win rate of 56 percent . The primary individual contributors to that number are Height, who finished Week 4 tied-sixth among all edges with 29%, and Odighizuwa, who was seventh among all defensive tackles with a win rate of 22%. However, the efforts up front have also been supplemented by the aggressiveness with which Morris is willing to use his linebackers. Dre Grenenlaw led the 49ers with four pressures against the Broncos as he was continually sent as an extra rusher, while Fred Warner has rushed the passer at his highest rate since the 2020 campaign . More Osa and White playing together as IDL with a healthy Bosa on the edge and the sacks will come. pic.twitter.com/JRZ0jilAlc — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 7, 2026 Where the performance on the defensive line has not been quite as strong is in run defense. Valdez provides reason for run D optimism The 49ers rank 27th in run stop win rate, yet two members of their defensive tackle rotation provided significant reason for optimism in that area last Sunday. Sebastian Valdez and, to a slightly lesser extent, Naquan Jones both stood out for their play in run defense as the Broncos were limited to just 82 yards on the ground. Both Valdez and Jones showed an ability to hold ground and violently disengage from blocks that has too often been lacking from the 49er run defense in recent times, with each player making a case for regular snaps even when the 49ers get more players back at defensive tackle, with James Thompson Jr. still out through injury. Sebastian Valdez was an absolute force against the run on Sunday. Also some really nice stuff from Naquan Jones, Gracen Halton and Khaliad Kareem. Also, Dre Greenlaw at the second level on the first play. Whew. pic.twitter.com/07prPAUYlm — Nicholas McGee (@nicholasmcgee24) October 7, 2026 Williams should greatly improve the 49ers’ run defense with his edge-setting prowess, while Bosa will be expected to supercharge the pass rush when he returns. Though the displays of those who have filled the void amid injuries in recent weeks have been far from spectacular, their play has helped reduce the need for panic around the situation on the D-Line. The 49ers don’t have any stars up front outside of Bosa, but the past two games have established that they do have a solid cast rotational defensive linemen — with Odighizuwa, White and Height the standouts — who can have enough of an impact rushing the passer and defending the run to deliver a game-winning effort. It would be unfair not to note that the outstanding play in the back seven through the first four weeks, for which Morris deserves great praise, has clearly had an impact in minimizing the deficiencies of injury-depleted front. But at the same time Morris and defensive line coach Kris Kocurek have found ways to get the best out of their depth guys on the D-Line, and their ability to do so has bought the 49ers a valuable luxury: patience. The 49ers don’t have to panic. They don’t have to rush to strike a trade that gives them the extra edge rusher or interior defender they may well eventually need. John Lynch and his front office can afford to wait it out a little, safe in the knowledge that Williams and Bosa are on the way back and that the less prominent guys in the D-Line group are capable of contributing to the defensive improvement that has been obvious through the first four weeks of the season. San Francisco probably will need to do a deal for another defensive lineman at the deadline to give the group the extra bump it may require in order for the 49ers to make a deep run in the postseason. However, the level of play they have elicited from a group that is not externally highly thought of…

title: 49ers vs. Seahawks: How to watch, game time, and betting odds
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will be playing their most important game yet this year in Week 5 as they travel to face the Seattle Seahawks. This can be seen as “Part 2” of a test for the 49ers offense going up against respectable defenses. The Denver Broncos were first, and might not have been the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers avoids a tackle by Uchenna Nwosu #7 of the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter in the NFC Divisional Playoff game at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will be playing their most important game yet this year in Week 5 as they travel to face the Seattle Seahawks. This can be seen as “Part 2” of a test for the 49ers offense going up against respectable defenses. The Denver Broncos were first, and might not have been the best test since several players were injured. The Seattle Seahawks are a defense that has given the 49ers fits in the past. Brock Purdy has entered the MVP conversation, and this game can make or break that conversation continuing past Week 5. This will be an afternoon game on Fox. Kevin Burkhardt has the play-by-play, and Tom Brady will be doing color. The 4-0 49ers head to Seattle 2-0 in their division. A win here could impact the NFC West as a whole. For the 49ers specifically, starting the season 3-0 in a competitive NFC West is something anyone would sign up for. Last week, the 49ers faced the Broncos, and that defense gave the 49ers all they could handle for three quarters. Brock Purdy eventually found the cracks and put the game out of reach, but it was a nail-biter for most of the game. Most of that was due to an inept Broncos offense, which left several plays on the field. The Seahawks didn’t leave plays on the field in their game last week; rather, they just took their foot off the gas, letting the Los Angeles Chargers back into things when it should have been over. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert threw a costly interception at the very end, but the Seahawks were definitely playing with their food towards the end of the game. They have only one loss on the year, coming against the Washington Commanders. The 49ers start a difficult stretch of their schedule, traveling to face the Broncos, hosting the Kansas City Chiefs, and then facing the Chicago Bears. The 49ers can happily get them prepped up for that schedule by handing them another “L”. In 2025, the 49ers failed to score a single touchdown against the Seahawks in their last two meetings. This was due to the injury bug decimating the roster and the Seahawks defense having Shanahan’s number. The biggest issue was the wide receivers, but the 49ers have improved a lot. Brock Purdy has yet to take a sack in 2026, so the offensive line is much improved from last year as well. We’ve seen nothing but good things from the 49ers thus far, but to be the man, you gotta beat the man. In this case, with the 49ers being at the top of several power rankings, they need to prove that legitimacy by beating the reigning Super Bowl champions. The 49ers will be without fullback Kyle Juszczyk, who suffered a knee sprain last week. They also will be without defensive lineman Nick Bosa (calf), James Thompson (ankle), and safety Marques Sigle. Mykel Williams, who began the season on the PUP list, will start his first game for 2026 after returning from a knee injury. However, he is listed as questionable along with cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder). The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet, cornerback Julian Neal (hamstring), and linebacker Chazz Surratt (calf). Running back George Holani (ribs) and wide receiver Irvin Charles (knee) are questionable. full_text: The San Francisco 49ers got some good news on the injury front this week, as Mykel Williams was activated off the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List after a good week of practice. To accommodate Williams, the 49ers made a number of roster moves. They initially released Ogbonnia Okoronkwo, who had played in all four games so far this season. Then, they re-signed Okoronkwo to the practice squad and elevated him as well for Sunday’s game. Now, with their defensive line health improving, the 49ers made one more move on Saturday: releasing Matt Judon. Judon, 34, signed with the 49ers practice squad on September 29th and played for the 49ers in Week 4. He suited up for 14 defensive snaps after being elevated from the practice squad, recording one tackle. The 49ers could also potentially get some reinforcements next week. Nick Bosa and James Thompson Jr. are two defensive linemen who did not practice this week, but could potentially get into the mix ahead of the Washington Commanders game next Monday. But for now, San Francisco will have Williams, Keion White, Osa Odighizuwa, Gracen Halton, Okoronkwo, Romello Height, Sebastian Valdez, and Khalid Kareem as options for Sunday on the defensive line.
