title: NFL predictions: 49ers and Seahawks feel like a low-scoring game
summary: An early game of the year contender is approaching us here in Week 5, as the San Francisco 49ers are traveling to Lumen Field to take on the Seattle Seahawks in an NFC West showdown. The 49ers have been off to a great start, going 4-0 with wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images An early game of the year contender is approaching us here in Week 5, as the San Francisco 49ers are traveling to Lumen Field to take on the Seattle Seahawks in an NFC West showdown. The 49ers have been off to a great start, going 4-0 with wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, and Denver Broncos. The Seahawks, meanwhile, are 3-1, with wins over the New England Patriots, Cardinals, and Los Angeles Chargers, but they lost to the Washington Commanders on the road in Week 3. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Both teams have been playing at a high level lately. The 49ers have the league’s best offense, and Brock Purdy is a clear MVP contender. The Seahawks are fourth in EPA allowed per play, and they’ve been strong against the pass and the run. This is shaping up to be a key early-season game for both teams and could play into the division race late in the season. Let’s get into our three predictions for Sunday. Last Week 49ers get off to a fast start Turnovers on both sides 49ers target middle of field Last week was a much different game for the 49ers. I thought they could start fast, given their first three weeks and how much Denver struggled in the first halves of their first three games. Well, the 49ers offense could only conjure three points in a grind-out game in the first half, but the defense also held the Broncos to three points through 30 minutes. I also thought there could be turnovers on both sides with the opportunistic defenses. I noted how inconsistent Bo Nix had been to start the year, and his conservative play continued in Week 4. The 49ers did force a turnover, but it came on special teams and ended up being a big turning point. With Denver’s linebackers struggling to start the year, that felt like a matchup Kyle Shanahan would look to exploit, especially with the cornerbacks on the outside. Brock Purdy saw most of his success between the numbers, completing 11 of 16 passes for 148 yards and a touchdown. It was a ton of quick throws, as Purdy averaged a 2.35-second time to throw when kept clean (22 of his 30 dropbacks). Now, let’s move on to this week. It’s a day for the 49ers linebackers Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw have been quite good this season, with Warner looking like a Defensive Player of the Year candidate. But this game feels like it really could be a day for the 49ers linebackers. The Seahawks want to establish the run, and they’re going to try to do so behind their offensive line. They’ve got the sixth-highest rush rate so far, even though their EPA per rush ranks 26th in the NFL and their rush success rate ranks 21st. The 49ers will hopefully get Mykel Williams back, but this feels like a day where the 49ers linebackers will have to be playmakers. They could also be key for Raheem Morris’s blitz packages to make Sam Darnold uncomfortable and get the ball out quickly. San Francisco is 31st in rushing success rate allowed. This game has a similar feel to last weekend’s as a slower-paced contest that could drag out into a physical slugfest. That puts even more responsibility on Warner and Greenlaw to produce. So far, that duo has 49 tackles and 17 defensive stops, according to PFF. Their fumble-forcing ability could also be a big factor in a game where a turnover could make the difference. 49ers will have to rely on banged-up Mike Evans Without Kyle Juszczyk, the 49ers may be forced to go into lighter packages with more 11 personnel. Mike Macdonald’s defense already is adept at getting pressure, and they’ll be looking to get the ball out of Brock Purdy’s hands quickly. An issue against the Broncos last week was that the 49ers’ banged-up receiver core could not get separation, outside of Mike Evans. It feels like a similar script against Seattle’s secondary this weekend. Evans was clearly lingering last week, and is highly unlikely to look 100 percent on Sunday. But if the 49ers are to find some consistency on offense, they’ll need to keep funneling him the ball and finding ways to keep him fresh enough to make plays. Otherwise, it’ll be up to Brock Purdy to make magic out of a hat. The under comes true Currently, the total on this game sits at 45.5 points on FanDuel Sportsbook . As I mentioned above, this game feels very similar to last weekend’s contest against the Rams. Both teams want to run the ball. The Seahawks and 49ers are sixth and seventh, respectively in rush rate this season. However, both teams haven’t been very successful running the ball or creating explosives on the ground. They also face quality opposing defenses that have done a terrific job of limiting explosive plays. This feels like a time-of-possession battle where both teams will try to run behind their strong offensive lines, leading to a lower-scoring game. I think both defensive play-callers will have a pressure plan up their sleeves to force the quarterbacks into tough situations, and see the under play out on Sunday.

title: That one time Kyle Shanahan forgot about Jaxon Smith-Njigba
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are getting ready for Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks in what is the most important game of the season thus far. If you take the rosters and make a list of the top 10 players between the two of them, Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba would definitely be on that […]
full_text: PASADENA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 01: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Ohio State Buckeyes catches a touchdown pass as Malone Mataele #15 of the Utah Utes defends during the fourth quarter in the Rose Bowl Game at Rose Bowl Stadium on January 01, 2022 in Pasadena, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are getting ready for Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks in what is the most important game of the season thus far. If you take the rosters and make a list of the top 10 players between the two of them, Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba would definitely be on that list. Turns out, he was on Shanahan’s radar for a brief moment in 2021. During his Friday press conference , Shanahan repeated a story about when he got his first glimpse of Smith-Njigba—when the wide receiver was playing at Ohio State. 2021 was the year the 49ers traded three first-round picks and change to move up to pick No. 3 in the 2021 NFL Draft. While the 49ers ultimately went with Trey Lance, Buckeye quarterback Justin Fields was seen as a distant possibility. “We were going to Pro Days looking at Fields,” Shanahan recalled. “I just remember that it was a long workout and there was a freshman running all over the place.” That freshman was Smith-Njigba. Upon seeing the wide receiver, Shanahan might have been less interested in the quarterbacks. “I just ended up asking [John] Lynch halfway through the end; I was just like, ‘Who the hell is that kid?’ And they’re like, ‘Oh, it’s some freshman.’” Knowing that was a freshman might have been the end of it. A freshman isn’t going to declare for the draft, and Shanahan’s primary focus was on what quarterback to select from what was (thought at the time) an impressive draft class for the position. “We got his name and I had forgot the name at the time, like I usually do.” Smith-Njigba was drafted in the 2023 NFL Draft. There was little Shanahan could have done to snag the player if he wanted to; that was the final year of the 49ers not having a first-round pick due to the Lance trade, and they wouldn’t make a selection in the third round. Their third-round pick, 87th overall, went to safety, Ji’Ayir Brown. You know the 2023 draft as the “Jake Moody Draft,” because he was the next pick of the 49ers, also in the third round. All Shanahan could do was recall watching him a few years earlier. Lynch pointed out who Smith-Njigba was to Shanahan, and Shanahan didn’t forget. “He was just running around everywhere, catching everything, and that was extremely impressive.”

They also don’t play on defense and special teams. This week’s lineup in those two phases is quite the conundrum. For more from Ben Standig, click here The Athletic (paywall) Commanders can prove Dan Quinn right at 1pm vs Giants With 13 losses in their last 16 games, the Commanders’ mantras shouldn’t be printed on T-shirts. They should be scribbled on scraps of paper, crumpled up and tossed in the trash can. When you’re rolling toward the postseason, being connected by shared values and channeling a good fire toward a common goal—all those sayings, and many more that have come and gone—can seem foundational. It’s also true that the connection Quinn feels with his players and staff, and fosters among them, is real. [I]t’s fair to acknowledge that the New York Giants — this week’s opponent — are 3-1 because they have faced Dallas, Tennessee and Arizona at home. The Commanders have faced Dallas and Philadelphia on the road, and Indianapolis in London with a third-string quarterback, and lost to all three. Washington faces the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals later in the year. Flip the schedule, and despite all the injuries, Washington’s early-season narrative might be different. ready to get rolling @BankofAmerica | #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/fQjYKMVAIJ — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 10, 2026 It’s easy to understand the eye rolls and pulled-out hair when Quinn says his belief isn’t wavering, because the results stink. The slogans feel like hollow catchphrases, desperate grabs at a winning process. The players and staff, though, have bought in and appreciate what they see as an honest assessment of their flaws. The process is Quinn’s. He has sold it to his Commanders. What matters now is not whether it fits on a T-shirt or can be painted on a wall in Ashburn. What matters is whether the Commanders beat the Giants and take a step toward salvaging their season. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Washington Gets Roster Help, but One Move Stands Out The Commanders announced several roster moves Saturday, beginning with the activation of defensive end Deatrich Wise Jr. from the Reserve/PUP list. Wise was also removed from the injury report, giving Washington another defensive lineman to work with against New York. Linebacker Austin Keys was signed to the active roster, while safety Darren Hall and receiver Van Jefferson were elevated from the practice squad. Jefferson’s elevation is particularly interesting with Stefon Diggs already ruled out and Terry McLaurin questionable with a hamstring injury. Washington also downgraded cornerback Trey Amos and running back Jeremy McNichols to OUT, ending any possibility of either making his return Sunday. Washington Has an Opportunity on Third Down Here’s something worth watching Sunday. Washington’s offense ranks 30th in the NFL on third down, converting just 31.6% of its opportunities, while the Giants’ defense also ranks 30th, allowing opponents to convert 48.9%. That’s an opportunity the Commanders have to take advantage of, especially with Jayden Daniels returning. His ability to extend plays gives Washington another option, although missing Diggs and potentially McLaurin certainly doesn’t make the job any easier. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders are making Jayden Daniels the savior again, and the risk is high It’s the same story the Commanders faced last year when they repeatedly rushed Daniels back to the field in difficult situations to try to save their season. This time, the outcome needs to be different. It’s a miracle Daniels missed only two weeks with an injury that initially had everyone questioning whether it was season-ending. And after Marcus Mariota got hurt against the Indianapolis Colts , the Commanders didn’t have much of a choice. But is this a good thing? Even though the injury is to Daniels’ non-throwing arm, we saw what happened last year when he willed himself back from this same injury. He aggravated it against the Minnesota Vikings and missed the rest of the season . Last year, Daniels played recklessly and exposed himself to far too many big hits. That’s partially on him and partially on his lack of protection, and Washington’s offensive line is no better now . Daniels will have the world on his shoulders. With sub-optimal protection and a depleted receiving corps, making the offense click will all be up to him and coordinator David Blough. More than that, this is a game the Commanders can’t afford to lose in the grand scheme of their season. The Giants are 3-1 but haven’t beaten any good teams, and Washington is favored in the matchup. The Commanders won’t be next week, when they hit the road to face the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football . If head coach Dan Quinn’s squad loses this one, they’re probably 1-5 at the bye . Daniels is in an impossible situation. He needs to do all he can to put his team on his back, but he also can’t overwork himself to the point of burnout. Washington has struggled to find that balance with him, and it has done little to make his life more manageable. But all Daniels can do is complete the task at hand. title: Where in the world are the Washington Commanders’ tight ends?
summary: In December of 2024, I wrote a Hogs Haven fanpost investigating Ben Sinnott’s lack of production during his rookie season. In the article, I referenced the classic edutainment game Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego? and analyzed the statistics and circumstances surrounding the second-round tight end’s exclusion from the offense. At the conclusion of the […]
full_text: In December of 2024, I wrote a Hogs Haven fanpost investigating Ben Sinnott’s lack of production during his rookie season. In the article, I referenced the classic edutainment game Where in the World is Carmen Sandiego? and analyzed the statistics and circumstances surrounding the second-round tight end ’s exclusion from the offense. At the conclusion of the investigation, the mystery remained unsolved. Fast forward to the present, where an even greater conundrum now presents itself for the ACE detective company. The entire tight end group is missing from Washington’s offense. The Commanders' TE production through four weeks (via @TruMediaSports ): Receptions — 10 (Tied for 31st/last) Targets — 17 (tied for 31st) Yards — 65 (32nd*) Rec. TDs — Zero (one of four teams without a TD) Air yards per target — 2.30 (28th) YAC — 42 (31st) — Ben Standig (@BenStandig) October 6, 2026 There’s a lot to investigate, so let’s dust off the magnifying glass and try to find the culprit. Offensive Coordinator Is David Blough not utilizing his tight ends enough? There were several articles written during the offseason hypothesizing that Blough would mirror Ben Johnson’s offense and use heavier personnel; with 12 and 13 looks, in fact, I wrote one of them . Most thought we would see a mix in the neighborhood of 60% 12-personnel, 30% 11-personnel and right around 10% use of 13-personnel groupings. Were we all wrong? Not completely. Below is Washington’s personnel usage through the first four weeks of the season, provided by SumerSports. 11 Personnel – 63.46% 12 Personnel – 21.92% 13 Personnel – 10% As you can see, the amount of 12 personnel utilization so far was vastly overestimated and is flip-flopped with the rate of 11 personnel, but there seems to be multiple reasons for this distribution. The first is Chigoziem Okonkwo’s hamstring injury, which sidelined him for much of the last three weeks. His absence did clear the way for Colson Yankoff — who shined in training camp this summer — to play more, and the undrafted free agent has played 23% of the total snaps so far this season . While developing, Yankoff just isn’t on the same level as Chig. He has only drawn four targets on 37 routes. Ben Sinnott currently leads the team in routes run by Washington’s tight ends with 49 but he’s last in targets with two and is already followed closely by Chig, who has 46 routes run with seven targets so far. We can expect those numbers to increase for Okonkwo when the Commanders host the Giants on Sunday. Antonio Williams Another reason is the emergence of rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams. Considered pro-ready coming out of the college, Williams was incredibly effective right away and won the NFL Rookie of the Week in his debut. Williams has been close to hitting on several big plays, but untimely drops and penalties have negated them. It is hard to take a player like that off the field for the receiving talents of John Bates and Ben Sinnott. It will be interesting to see what their personnel usage looks like on Sunday versus the Giants, as Stefon Diggs has been ruled out and Chig will be a full go. However, in order to use more heavy personnel, Washington’s offense must become more effective at it. Offensive performance in heavy personnel (2 or fewer WRs) and in lighter groupings pic.twitter.com/5s395h3pQb — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) October 8, 2026 Inefficient run game As you can see from the graphic above, Washington’s offense hasn’t been particularly productive in either heavy (two or fewer WRs) or light groupings. They have an approximate 42% success rate out of both, with similar rates of explosive plays and EPA ratings. A big reason for that has been the ineffectiveness of the run game. Looking at the table from SumerSports again, we can see additional heavy personnel is not making the run game more effective, as the EPA per rush is actually lower when using heavy personnel. Therein lies a big part of the problem. The current group of tight ends, while talented, lacks players that can create separation the way Zach Ertz did during his time in Washington. The effectiveness of both Okonkwo and Sinnott depends on creating mismatches. One way of doing so is using heavy looks by forcing the team to honor the run with slower, bigger-bodied defenders that the more athletic tight ends can exploit in coverage. Since Washington does not have an effective running game, defensive coordinators aren’t being forced to deploy more linebackers and bigger hybrid players to stop it. You can see how effective teams with impressive rushers like Derrick Henry, Bijan Robinson and James Cook have been out of heavy sets this season. To be multiple out of the same look, you must have a balanced attack and use the run game to set up play-action. Play-action is critical to the success of tight ends like Sinnott. As the second-round tight end said during the offseason, he is better in an offense that uses outside zone play-action or other misdirection in order to create plays. Ben Sinnott just got his first target of the day (inexcusable) and made a career-long 36-yard catch. It happened! He flashed! pic.twitter.com/xlbxec0fPU — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) December 14, 2025 Without the running game play-action is not very effective. Washington has gone away from it early as they struggle to generate a rushing attack with their running backs. Per ESPN’s John Keim , Washington ranks 19th in play-action pass attempts, a number that many thought would be higher this season. While Okonkwo has the ability to get open in the short underneath, more play-action would allow him to use his speed to stretch the field vertically. But, in order to sell it, the team needs to be able to rush the ball effectively. Perhaps the return of Austin Ekeler running behind guard Sam Cosmi and newly appointed starting center Lucas Patrick will ignite the running game and allow Blough to utilize more play-action to create plays like this one. Chigoziem Okonkwo vs Baun and DeJean. Is the next match up I am going to talk about. The outside is already spoken for. That leaves the middle. Insert Chig. Williams works that same space from the slot. That’s the next piece. This one is about the tight end. Chig is 6-3, 238.… — TheJoesList (@TheJoesList) September 8, 2026 Injuries Finally, Washington just hasn’t had all their talent on the field at the same time. When Chig did return against the Colts, the majority of his snaps were played with seventh-round selection Athan Kaliakmanis behind center. The rookie quarterback was under siege and didn’t have time to find Okonkwo on several open looks in Week 4. To close our case, the real culprit behind the disappearance of the Washington Commanders’ tight ends has been the personnel, but not entirely those in the tight end room. Either due to injuries or performance, Blough hasn’t had the players to run the offense the way he prefers on game days. Starting on Sunday, with the return of several key players including quarterback Jayden Daniels and Cosmi, the rookie offensive coordinator could get his first chance to change that since Week 1. We will see if that means the return of the tight end to Washington’s offense.

title: Washington Commanders make several roster moves before Giants game
summary: The Washington Commanders announced a few roster moves before they host the New York Giants tomorrow. Three players had their 21-day practice windows opened this week, but only one of them has been activated. DE Deatrich Wise Jr. has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list due to a quad injury from last season. […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders announced a few roster moves before they host the New York Giants tomorrow. Three players had their 21-day practice windows opened this week, but only one of them has been activated. DE Deatrich Wise Jr. has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list due to a quad injury from last season. He has been activated and added to the Commanders 53-man roster. He can be active this week, and could be needed due to injuries to other players, including Charles Omenihu. LB Austin Keys was also signed from the practice squad, and will likely be available for special teams. CB Trey Amos (ankle) and RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) weren’t activated and remain on injured reserve for another game. The Commanders are elevating two players for Sunday’s home game against the New York Giants. The inactives list won’t be much of a mystery this week with six players already ruled out. The team had 23 players on Wednesday’s injury report, an insane number for a 53-man roster. Injuries continue to limit the Commanders early in the season, leading to decisions like waiving rookie RB Kaytron Allen to try to get him to the practice squad, only to see him get claimed by another team (Dolphins). The Commanders elevated WR Van Jefferson and S Darren Hall for today’s game. Stefon Diggs is out and Terry McLaurin is questionable, with both receivers dealing with hamstring injuries from last week. McLaurin “looked good” at practice, per head coach Dan Quinn, and he could be available on Sunday, but the team might want to limit him due to the nature of the injury. Jefferson is a vet and will provide another potential target for Jayden Daniels’ return to the field. The Commanders released their injury report Friday and ruled out six players: QB Marcus Mariota (knee), WR Stefon Diggs, S Percy Butler (hamstring), S Nick Cross (illness), DE Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle), and S Tyler Owens (hamstring). We have made the following roster moves: – Activated DE Deatrich Wise Jr. off the Reserve/Physically Unable to Perform List and removed him from the injury report – Signed LB Austin Keys from the practice squad – Elevated S Darren Hall and WR Van Jefferson from the practice squad… pic.twitter.com/yVnaXgA717 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 10, 2026 Should the Commanders have elevated different players? title: Five Washington Commanders players key to beating New York Giants
summary: Jayden Daniels is back. The Commanders quarterback will return from a two-game absence wearing a brace that should protect his left elbow from yet another dislocation, with the last incident coming in Week 2.   The Commanders have worked to fit the brace just right, to provide the proper protection and non-throwing-arm function to perform […]
full_text: Jayden Daniels is back. The Commanders quarterback will return from a two-game absence wearing a brace that should protect his left elbow from yet another dislocation, with the last incident coming in Week 2. The Commanders have worked to fit the brace just right, to provide the proper protection and non-throwing-arm function to perform like JD5. Daniels believes the brace won’t hinder him, nor will the fear of another dislocation. If that’s actually the case, the Commanders can compete with anyone. Their franchise quarterback has that effect on NFL games, as we’ve seen so many times before. He can’t, as we’ve also learned, do it alone. He’ll need help from these five Commanders to beat the New York Giants and remain competitive in a suddenly wide-open NFC East. WR Antonio Williams We know Stefon Diggs won’t play on Sunday . Terry McLaurin’s status remains up in the air. That’s a troubling development creating the need for others to step up. This won’t be all on third-round rookie Antonio Williams, but we’ve seen the flashes of explosiveness and quality routes that suggest Daniels could use him as an asset in the passing game. Expect some mistakes as he continues to develop, but Williams should have an opportunity to see more targets in this one as Daniels gets revved back up. RB Austin Ekeler Washington signed the veteran running back last week and played him against the Colts just a few days later. The production was solid, to the tune of 29 yards on just four carries. Head coach Dan Quinn said Ekeler will be more “embedded” in the game plan this week, so it’s fair to expect him to receive more touches in his second game back after suffering a torn Achilles’ tendon early in Washington’s 2025 campaign. The run game will be important on a game with inclement weather, and Ekeler will be key in the effort to get the ground game going strong. S Quan Martin Expect to see a ton of Quan Martin (and Jeremy Reaves) considering three active safeties in Nick Cross, Tyler Owens and Percy Butler have all been ruled out . The Commanders still must stay away from explosive plays, and Martin will often be playing deep in this one. And, as we all know, Giants quarterback Jameis Winston is not afraid to chuck it. He’ll also put the ball in danger, so Martin and the secondary needs to take some errant passes away when they’re available. We all know Martin has had his struggles – he has a 103.6 passer rating when targeted – but Washington needs a consistently solid game from Martin in coverage. LB Sonny Styles Sonny Styles has played quality football the past two games , with a combined 13 tackles, an interception, two passes defensed, a forced fumble, three quarterback hurries and a knockdown in that span. The No. 7 overall pick has proven he can do it all, as a pass rusher, cover man and run defender. They’ll need all of that quality on Sunday, slowing Giants running back Cam Skattebo and tight end Isaiah Likely . He’s quickly becoming the defensive centerpiece even at this early stage. Considering how he has played, it’s fair to expect another big game on Sunday. DC Daronte Jones We’ll all seen the stat by now highlighting how much the Commanders blitz and how bad Winston is when blitzed. Washington brings pressure 44% of the time. Winston has a 36.8 passer rating against it. Jones blitzes a ton and generally plays zone behind it, which can be an effective way of creating turnovers against a gunslinger-type of passer like Winston. Jones must dial up the right blitzes at the right times and confuse the heck out of Winston and force him to make the mistakes he’s prone to making. Player execution is always paramount, but coaching can help the Commanders get to 2-3 and right back into the mix in the NFC East. Which other Commanders (not named Jayden Daniels) are essential to a victory over NYG? Let us know in the comments below:

summary: The emotional whiplash of following the Washington Commanders football team hasn’t relented in the first quarter of the season. full_text: The emotional whiplash of following the Washington Commanders football team hasn’t relented in the first quarter of the season. Just when the Week 3 gritty home upset win against Seattle appeared to stabilize the ship and reignite optimism, a dreary, injury-filled and mistake-prone Sunday game in London last week against Daniel Jones and the Colts sent fan confidence careening back down the hill. In this week’s Reacts survey , we asked, as we do every week, about fan confidence, and we looked at the schedule for the coming month to see what fans expect from a critical three-game stretch that includes 2 games before, and one game after, the Week 7 bye. The poll results reflect a fanbase that is feeling thoroughly beaten down by injuries and inconsistent play — though a closer examination of the upcoming schedule suggests things might not be quite as dire as these results imply. Here is how the Hogs Haven community voted. Question 1: Are you confident the Commanders are headed in the right direction? The weekly roller coaster ride continues. After sitting at 70% in Week 1, confidence peaked at 83% after Week 2. It then dropped like a stone to 20% in Week 3 after the Jayden Daniels injury in the loss at Dallas, but surged back to 76% following the Seattle win. Now, fan confidence has cratered again, dropping 47 points to just 29% in the wake of the loss in London in which third string rookie QB Athan Kaliakmanis was forced to step up to the plate when injuries sidelined both Jayden Daniels and his backup Marcus Mariota. The volatility in responses and its connection to the results of the latest game played are pretty obvious. For others, the skepticism runs deeper than a single Sunday result — underlying the lack of confidence is consistent lack of to overarching sideline execution and preparation: Still, not everyone in the community is ready to throw in the towel on the coaching staff. As commenter SSP pointed out when looking at the bigger picture: “There was big risk in choosing both a rookie OC and DC, is it any wonder it might take a few games for them to hit their stride? We beat the defending SB champs, are we there? No, but it feels like there is a plan and we aren’t looking for a quick fix that will fade just as quickly… injuries will happen as well, in the end I don’t see how any long time fan can’t be happy with the direction of the team.” Question 2: What will the Commanders’ record be over their next 3 games? Visit our partners at FanDuel When asked to project the upcoming four-week, three-game stretch that includes the bye week — featuring home games against the Giants and Eagles sandwiched around a road trip to San Francisco and the bye — the pessimism carried over directly. A combined 62% of respondents believe Washington will post a losing record (winning one or zero games), with more than a quarter of those fans bracing for a complete 0-3 shutout. That apprehension seems extreme, but may be understandable given what fans saw in the first four weeks of the season. Yet, while dropping a road contest against a powerhouse 49ers squad out west is a very reasonable expectation, writing off both home NFC East matchups seems, to me, to ignore several matchup advantages working in Washington’s favor. The case for 2-1 and home optimism Weeks 5 & 8 Consider Week 5 against the New York Giants . Washington is actually favored by 3.5 points , and for good reason. New York lost starting rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season to injury, forcing them to turn to an erratic Jameis Winston as the starter (with JJ McCarthy waiting in the wings). While New York currently sits at 3-1, all three of their victories came at MetLife Stadium against opponents with a combined record of just 3-6. They have not proven they can win away from home, having lost their only road game of the season. Furthermore, Dan Quinn has owned this divisional rivalry since arriving in Washington, posting a clean 4-0 record against the Giants over the past two seasons. With a Commanders win on Sunday, the Giants would fall to 3-2 while the Commanders climb to 2-3, just a game out of first place in the division. Even Giants fans don’t buy the hype of the team’s 3-1 start The return of JD5 Also, the cavalry appears to be coming over the hill for Washington’s roster. The team said Jayden Daniels will to return under center this Sunday after missing time with his elbow injury. The offensive front—which struggled heavily in London with pass protection and opening run lanes—is also tracking to get cornerstone right guard Sam Cosmi back into the starting lineup alongside other potential reinforcements on both sides of the ball . The evidence of the win over Seattle Washington is undefeated in its only true home appearance at Northwest Stadium this season, having grinded out that 33-31 win over Seattle – a game in which Seattle never held the lead, and in which the Commanders offense sat on the ball and watched the final two minutes tick down to 00:00 and victory without trying to advance down the field or score. Washington beat Seattle more comprehensively than the scoreboard or box score would indicate. Looking ahead to Week 8 against Philadelphia , Washington will have the immense advantage of playing at home coming directly off their bye week, giving the coaching staff an extra week of prep and battered players an extra week of recovery. Meanwhile, Philadelphia has been looking pretty vulnerable through the first month of the season. Under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, the Eagles’ offense has sputtered through disjointed series, and struggled with third-down efficiency. Their once-dominant offensive line took a crushing blow with the sudden, unexpected retirement of All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson, and the rest of their roster, already depleted with the trade of AJ Brown to New England, has been plagued by a rash of injuries that may be at least as extensive as those that have struck Washington’s roster. In the trenches and along the perimeter, they simply are not the terrifying juggernaut that rolled into the NFC Championship two seasons ago. Fans and media in Philly are once again calling for Nick Sirianni’s head , and this time, I get the sense that they might actually get it. My expectations for what lies ahead The next 4 weeks A 2-1 mark across the upcoming three-game block in October and early November simply does not strike me as wishful thinking; in my mind, it is a very realistic outcome if Washington takes advantage of (finally) enjoying the benefits of playing at home and getting some time to rest and recover in Week 7. Weeks 9 to 16 There is a compelling argument that Washington can successfully defend its home turf in Weeks 5 and 8 and enter the ninth week of the season just one game below .500 and facing a string of at least 7 winnable games that include the Giants (again), Bengals, Cardinals, Titans, Texans, Falcons, and Vikings. It doesn’t take much imagination to see the Commanders heading to Jacksonville in Week 17 with a winning record and in the hunt for a playoff berth. It starts this weekend In any event, the turnaround begins this Sunday, when the Commanders host the New York Giants at Northwest Stadium in Landover. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. Per FanDuel, the Commanders are favored (-3.5) with the over/under set at a very low 43.5 points. Pack the stands, get loud, and let’s see if the burgundy & gold can take care of business at home. Visit our partners at FanDuel

title: How to bet Ravens-Falcons on SNF: Analysis, tips and top prop plays
summary: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Ravens-Falcons on "Sunday Night Football."
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens and Atlanta Falcons both come into Sunday night playing well, but Atlanta has looked like a different team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr . returned. The Falcons have scored 80 points over their last two games, with Penix completing 73.3% of his passes. Bijan Robinson has been a big part of that success, rushing for 349 yards and four touchdowns during that stretch. Baltimore will have its hands full trying to slow him down.

 

 The Ravens will be without Lamar Jackson because of an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley gets the start against a Falcons defense allowing a league-low 48.3 rushing yards per game. That doesn't bode well for Derrick Henry , despite his seven rushing touchdowns this season. Baltimore is also dealing with injuries along its offensive line, which could make things even more difficult.

 I'm interested to see how Baltimore approaches defending Atlanta's running game. If the Ravens commit more defenders to stopping Robinson, Penix could have opportunities to make plays downfield. With OLB Trey Hendrickson also ruled out, that becomes an even bigger concern for Baltimore.

 

 

 

 Betting outlook 
 I like the Falcons against the spread more than the total in this matchup. Atlanta is favored by three points after Baltimore opened as a 4.5-point favorite earlier in the week. Lamar Jackson being ruled out has a lot to do with that movement, but the Falcons have also played well enough to earn some respect from oddsmakers.

 

 Atlanta has averaged 40 points and 459 total yards per game over its last two. The defense has also played well, especially against the run. That could be a problem for a Baltimore offense likely to rely heavily on Derrick Henry with Tyler Huntley starting at quarterback.

 Atlanta has home-field advantage, a healthy starting quarterback, and a defense that should make life difficult for Huntley. I'm backing the Falcons.

 

 Notable player props, bets 
 

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 Bijan Robinson rushing yards OVER 87.5 (-114) 

 Robinson has cleared this line in each of his last two games, with at least 19 rushing attempts in both. Atlanta's offensive line has also played well, ranking 12th in run block win rate. The Ravens will be without OLB Trey Hendrickson , a significant loss for their defense that should benefit Robinson and the Falcons' running game.

 

 Drake London receiving yards OVER 80.5 (-111) 

 London has been excellent since Penix returned, catching 14-of-16 targets for 290 yards over his last two games. He has accounted for 48.2% of Atlanta's receiving yards this season. The matchup against Baltimore is favorable, with the Ravens allowing the sixth-most yards to wide receivers. Penix has been effective in the vertical passing game, and Baltimore's defense has struggled to defend those throws this season.

 Mark Andrews OVER 32.5 receiving yards (-115) 

 Andrews currently ranks as the TE16 in receiving yards with 149, having failed to reach 30 receiving yards in each of his last two games. However, he historically thrives when paired with quarterback Tyler Huntley , averaging 63.8 receiving yards across 10 career games played together. This week's matchup at Atlanta is highly favorable, as the Falcons' defense has allowed an opposing tight end ( Pat Freiermuth , Darren Waller , and Juwan Johnson ) to surpass that 30-yard mark in three of the past four weeks. -- Liz Loza

title: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Stroud, Washington among top options
summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
full_text:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues. 

 Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions. 

 The Week 5 NFL schedule features some really tough matchups for fantasy football, starting with the quarterback position. However, I still have four options -- in the QB2 range -- who have some upside. There are also a handful of wide receivers below, including deeper-league fliers you can take a chance on. As always, we'll hit on the running back and tight ends, and I have two available defenses to stream this week.

 

 Quarterbacks 

   Kirk Cousins , Las Vegas Raiders (33.3% rostered; at Patriots) 

 Cousins has scored 20 or more points in three straight games, and he has thrown two or more touchdown passes in all four games. Now, Cousins isn't going to provide any upside as a runner. We know that. But in Klint Kubiak 's offense, one that leans on tight end usage, Cousins can play on rhythm. And the Raiders are going to throw the ball in scoring position, as Cousins' eight red zone touchdown passes are tied for second most in the league. He's a superflex starter in the road matchup versus the Patriots.

   C.J. Stroud , Houston Texans (41.1% rostered; at Titans) 

 

 Stroud benefited from the return of wide receiver Nico Collins in Week 4, producing a season-high 23.08 points in a prime matchup versus Dallas. Collins had 118 yards receiving, plus he scored two touchdowns on end zone throws. It's a much tougher matchup this week versus the Titans, but Stroud is scoring 17.1 PPG, and Collins is the difference-maker in the Houston route tree. Stroud has value here as a QB2 in superflex formats.

   Jordan Love , Green Bay Packers (48.9% rostered; vs. Bears) 

 Love averages 16.2 fantasy PPG and has thrown two touchdown passes in all four games played. And due to a subpar rushing attack in Green Bay, Love is attempting 38.5 passes per game. Yes, the Bears defense ranks in the top 12 versus quarterbacks, but I do see positive perimeter matchups here for Packers wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . If you need a QB2 this week, Love does have some value.

   Deshaun Watson , Cleveland Browns (15.7% rostered; at Jets) 

 Watson (16.7 fantasy PPG) has scored 19 or more points in two of four games played, and he's averaging 31.8 rushing yards per game. The Jets defense ranks in the top five versus quarterbacks, so I don't love the matchup. However, if you need a QB2 with dual-threat upside Watson fits. We've seen the Browns take vertical shots in the pass game, so there is big-play potential for Watson.

 Wide receivers 

 

   Dohnte Meyers , Cincinnati Bengals (12.2% rostered; at Dolphins) 

 With Tee Higgins (adductor/neck) and Ja'Marr Chase (concussion protocol) both questionable for Sunday's game vs. Miami, managers can pivot to Meyers if either is unable to go. In the Week 4 loss to Jacksonville, Meyers scored 15.2 fantasy points, catching seven of nine targets for 82 yards. We saw the quicks and screens underneath, plus Meyers got loose on a deep over route for a 29-yard reception. He would be a WR3/flex option if one of the above stars is out, and he would have even more upside if both are inactive.

   Malik Washington , Miami Dolphins (33.4% rostered; vs. Bengals) 

 I really like the tape on Washington, along with his versatility in the Miami offense. Very similar to what we see with Deebo Samuel Sr . in San Francisco. Washington has scored 11 or more points in back-to-back games, and he's averaging seven targets per game (27% team target share). Plus, he's had at least two carries in two straight. I'd have him in the lineup as a WR3.

 

   Keenan Allen , Indianapolis Colts (38.5% rostered; at Steelers) 

 Allen (groin) missed the Week 4 win over the Commanders, but he is expected back for Sunday's game in Pittsburgh. In Week 3, Allen scored 18.3 points versus the Texans, catching six of nine targets for 63 yards and a score. He can still uncover and work the dirty areas of the field, which is a fit for a Colts pass game lacking a vertical element with Alec Pierce (heel) on IR. You can play Allen as a WR3.

   Darius Cooper (6.0% rostered) and  Dontayvion Wicks , Philadelphia Eagles (47.6% rostered; at Jaguars) 

 It's a tough matchup here versus the Jags defense, but with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still out, both Cooper and Wicks are deeper-league fliers this week. Cooper saw seven targets in the Week 4 loss to the Rams, catching three passes for 33 yards and two touchdowns for 18.3 fantasy points, and Wicks has produced two games this season with 12 or more points.

   Malachi Fields , New York Giants (7.3% rostered; at Commanders) 

 Fields is a matchup play versus a Commanders defense ranking in the bottom five versus wide receivers. Fields, who scored a season-high 13.1 points in Week 4, is averaging only 3.8 targets per game, but he did catch a touchdown pass in the win over the Cardinals on a red zone throw. Fields also has the physical tools to win one-on-ones as a boundary option. He's a deeper-league flier.

   DeMario Douglas , New England Patriots (2.2% rostered; vs. Raiders) 

 With Mack Hollins (calf) expected to miss Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Douglas should see an expanded role in the Patriots' offense. Douglas' usage has been down this season (nine receptions on 17 targets for 82 yards), but he could be in a position to operate as the outlet out of the slot for Drake Maye  on Sunday.

 Running backs 

   Brian Robinson Jr ., Atlanta Falcons (44.2% rostered; vs. Ravens) 

 Robinson scored a season-high 25.7 points in the Falcons' blowout win over the Saints in Week 4, rushing for 62 yards and three touchdowns. As the No. 2 behind Bijan Robinson , Brian has seen 10 or more carries in three straight games, posting at least one rushing touchdown in two of them. Steady volume here in an offense averaging 181 rushing yards per game (second most). Brian is a deeper-league flex this week versus the Ravens.

 

   Keaton Mitchell , Los Angeles Chargers (23.5% rostered; vs. Broncos) 

 The winless Chargers moved to a three-man backfield committee in the Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, and it was Mitchell who paced the position with 15 touches, compared to Omarion Hampton 's 11 and Kimani Vidal 's seven. Mitchell rushed for only 39 yards on 10 carries, but he did catch five passes for 24 yards. Mitchell has scored 11 or more points in two straight, and he brings more receiving upside to the lineup.

   Will Shipley , Eagles (37.8% rostered; at Jaguars) 

 With both Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (IR) down this week, Shipley is in line to see a bump in volume. However, the Eagles' No. 3 running back hasn't had more than nine touches in a game this season, and Philly is also going through major transitions on the offensive line. Plus, Dameon Pierce could also factor into the run game. Shipley should be viewed as a deeper-league option only in this matchup with Jacksonville.

   MarShawn Lloyd , RB, Packers (46.9% rostered; vs. Bears) 

 Lloyd should split touches with Kaleb Johnson this week, as Chris Brooks is dealing with an ankle injury. Lloyd's lack of rushing efficiency (2.7 YPC) remains an issue, but he does provide some value as a pass catcher. He caught five balls for 36 yards in the Week 4 win over Tampa Bay, and he has at least two receptions in three straight games, adding a touchdown grab back in Week 2.

 Tight end 

   Brenton Strange , Jacksonville Jaguars (24.8% rostered; vs. Eagles) 

 Strange scored a season-high 16.5 points in the Week 4 win over the Bengals, catching seven of eight targets for 95 yards.…

title: NFL Week 5 betting guide: Analysis, best bets, TD predictions for Sunday
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 5 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

 Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 5.

 From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, the top game to bet, favorite defensive props to play and the top predicted TD scorers.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's Game of the Week 
 Solak's plays  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 

 Bowen's Game of the Week 

 Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 44.5) 
1 p.m. ET on CBS, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh

 

 We need to have a bounce-back week here after betting on the Bills last Sunday. So, let's pivot to a rested Pittsburgh team that played Thursday night in Week 4 at home against an Indianapolis team straight off a London trip. We'll look at both sides of the ball, then hit some props from this game and across the league in Week 5.

 

 When the Steelers have the ball: Running back Jaylen Warren has seen his usage (and production) elevate over the past two games. During this stretch (against Cincinnati and Cleveland) Warren has averaged 6.5 yards per carry, 21 touches and 151 scrimmage yards. He's also playing fast on the tape, and there's a lot of outside zone here, with Warren finding daylight. Plus, he's getting the ball on swings, screens and checkdowns. This is a good matchup for Warren against a Colts defense giving up 131 rushing yards per game (28th in the league). I expect a volume day for the Steelers' lead back.

 The Colts' defensive numbers in the pass game point to a Pittsburgh edge as well, as the Colts are giving up 261.3 yards per game through the air and are pressuring the QB at a rate of only 28.3% (29th in the league). But can the Steelers protect and give Aaron Rodgers time and a clean pocket? Rodgers has three touchdown passes and six completions of 15 or more air yards in each of his past two games, but he has been sacked seven times during that stretch and a total of 13 times on the season (tied for most in the league). Rodgers' declining mobility also plays a role, but he needs the pocket to throw vertically to  DK Metcalf  and work the play-action pass game in Mike McCarthy's offense.

 When the Colts have the ball: This offense runs through Jonathan Taylor . The Colts' running back ranks fifth in the NFL at 88.3 rushing yards per game, and his 86 carries are the third most through four games. He's a volume back with home run ability. Taylor has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season, and he gets a Steelers defense that is giving up 4.3 YPC (20th). I'd expect a run-heavy approach from the Colts to start this one, but the Steelers should counter with more single-high coverages, spinning down from their split-safety shells to get numbers in the front.

 Look for quarterback Daniel Jones to lean on play-action throws that mirror the run game. Jones ranks fifth in play-action attempts this season, and the Colts will look to open intermediate windows against a Steelers defense that plays heavy zone coverage (75.4% of coverage snaps). And without wide receiver Alec Pierce (IR/heel), there is a missing vertical element for the Colts, as Jones' 5.7 YPA ranks 28th. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen need to uncover and make themselves available to the QB in this one, and I would like to see tight end Tyler Warren featured more on seams and corner routes to create chunk plays.

 Picks: Steelers -2.5 (-118), Under 44.5 (-118)

 Prop bets: Jonathan Taylor rushing + receiving yards OVER 105.5 (-114) 

 I'll trust the anticipated volume for Taylor, who has had at least 21 touches in all four games played this season, producing at least 110 total yards in two. With the rushing totals and targets on screens and check downs, Taylor should hit the over.

 Jaylen Warren rushing yards OVER 62.5 (-112) 

 Warren has rushed for at least 93 yards in two straight games, with 17 carries in each. Take Warren's recent run on production in a matchup versus a Colts defense allowing 4.8 YPC (sixth highest in the league).

 

 Now, let's get to some other bets I like ...

 Christian Watson anytime TD (+195) 

 Watson has scored at least one touchdown in three of four games played, and he has four end zone targets on the season. Plus, we know Watson can separate over the top. I like the matchup here for the Packers' receiver against the Bears' cornerbacks, and Matt LaFleur can also scheme zone-beaters for Watson.

 San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks total points UNDER 45.5 (-105) 

 In the two games these clubs played last season, the totals hit 30 and 16. Mike Macdonald has the scheme (and personnel) to limit the 49ers' offense. I'd take the under in this one.

 Three-team parlay (+638) 

 Jacksonville Jaguars -7.5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles 
 Cleveland Browns +1.5 at New York Jets 
 Las Vegas Raiders +3.5 at New England Patriots 

 The Jaguars might be the best team in football, and they get an Eagles squad that is going through major in-season transitions on the offensive line. Plus, Philly will be without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith .

 Cleveland also is playing good ball. Todd Monken's offense can take vertical shots in the pass game, and the downhill rushing attack is a foundational approach with Quinshon Judkins . The Browns can run the ball against a Jets defense that just gave up 232 yards on the ground to the Bears in Week 4.

 Let's finish this parlay with the Raiders getting points on the road in New England. Las Vegas features a top-10 passing defense, and quarterback Kirk Cousins is an easy fit in Klint Kubiak's schemed-up system. The Raiders need more here from Ashton Jeanty and the run game, but I like them to cover.

 

 

 
 Solak's plays 
 

 Washington Commanders -3.5 vs. New York Giants 

 The 1-3 Commanders welcome Jayden Daniels back to the starting lineup with the 3-1 New York Giants -- who still have Jameis Winston starting at quarterback -- coming to town. The Giants' 2-0 run with Winston has been extremely unimpressive. They beat the Titans 12-7 on a rainy and windy day in MetLife Staduim thanks to a game-sealing end zone pick from Jevon Holland . They beat the Cardinals 36-24 thanks to a 98-yard pick-six by Deonte Banks on fourth-and-goal. With a little bit better red zone execution from two of the league's worst starting quarterbacks, the Giants are 1-3.

 

 As it is, the Giants are 27th in EPA per drive and in success rate during Winston's two starts, and they draw a plucky Commanders defense that can bring out the worst of Winston by blitzing heavily (second only to the Vikings in blitz rate) and forcing turnovers. Star receiver Malik Nabers  sat out Wednesday's practice because of a sore knee, and if he is at all limited, the Giants' lack of pass-catching depth makes it challenging to move the ball with any consistency.

 Washington is enduring a slew of its own injuries. Receivers  Terry McLaurin  and Stefon Diggs were both absent from Wednesday's practice, and their top two running backs ( Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt ), two tight ends ( Chig Okonkwo and Ben Sinnott ), and both starting linebackers ( Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu ) were all limited. title: Eagles vs. Jaguars, NFL London preview: ESPN experts on key players, matchups and predictions
summary: The NFL rolls into London this begin with a clash between the Indianapolis Colts and the Washington Commanders -- so we asked ESPN reporters Stephen Holder and John Keim for a preview.
full_text:
NFL London continues with Game Two of Three this Sunday as the Philadelphia Eagles look to bounce back with a much-needed win against the in-form Jacksonville Jaguars . Ahead of the game, ESPN asked Eagles reporter Tim McManus  and Jaguars reporter Michael DiRocco  to assess their respective teams, the players UK fans should watch and where Sunday's matchup could be won and lost... 

 

 How would you sum up the season so far? 
 

 TM: Troubling. The offense leads the league in three-and-outs (15) and ranks in the bottom 10 of the league in a number of categories, including yards per play (4.7, 27th) and sacks allowed (12, T-4th-most). They have struggled to find an offensive identity and that task becomes even harder now that right tackle Lane Johnson has retired and interior lineman Cam Jurgens has been traded to the Ravens. 

 -  NFL International Games: Schedule, UK times for matches in London, more 
 - Eagles vs. Jaguars: NFL London kick-off time, how to watch in UK 

 

 MD:  Taking down QBs. One of the criticisms of the Jaguars' late-season run in 2025 was the lack of quality quarterbacks they beat. They've already beaten Drake Maye , who was the MVP runner-up last season, and Joe Burrow . Deshaun Watson has been solid in three of his four games, with the exception being Week 1 against the Jaguars. They're beating good QBs. Now they face Jalen Hurts , who has been to two Super Bowls and won one.

 What's the biggest thing we've learned about this team that we didn't know coming into the season? 
 

 TM:  That the defense faced a bigger learning curve than we thought. There have been some communication breakdowns in the absence of linebacker Nakobe Dean (Raiders) and safety Reed Blankenship (Texans). Vic Fangio's group looked more buttoned up against the Rams last week before wearing down under the weight of playing 77 snaps and giving up a pair of touchdowns late.

 

 MD:  The Jaguars are established as one of the AFC's best teams and are a legit Super Bowl contender. The offense skyrocketed in the second half of last season and that helped them win their last eight games and an AFC South title. The big question was whether that was lightning in a bottle or would they pick up where they left off in 2026. In four games they twice scored more than 30 points and are averaging 26 per game. The defense is again forcing turnovers (eight, second-most in the NFL), and many wondered if what it did last year (31 turnovers) was a fluke, too. Looks like none of it was. 

 

 

 What's the mood around the team about travelling to London? 
 

 TM:  Given the early adversity, coach Nick Sirianni said his messaging is about "locking arms, staying together and just having each other's backs in a situation." Sirianni referenced the start to the 2024 season when they began 2-2, made some adjustments and went on to mount what proved to be a Super Bowl run. "I think sometimes we conveniently forget those things," Sirianni "We don't up here."

 

 MD:  There are a lot of players who have made this trip multiple times -- including punter Logan Cooke , who will be playing in his NFL-record 10th international game -- so there's a normalcy about it for much of the team. That makes it easier to treat it as a business trip, which is what multiple players called it earlier this week.

 

 Who's been the standout player so far -- and who should UK fans watch out for? 
 

 TM:   Quinyon Mitchell hasn't been perfect but continues to flash his lockdown corner abilities. His absence late in the game against the Rams because of a knee injury was another major factor in why Matthew Stafford was able to mount a late attack.

 

 MD:  Liam Coen has Trevor Lawrence playing at a consistently high level -- in his last 12 regular season games he's thrown 27 touchdown passes and seven interceptions and the Jaguars are 11-1 -- and as a result the offense is churning out yards and points. The last time the Jaguars were in the UK Travis Hunter was mainly playing offense and he caught eight passes for 101 yards and a touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams . Now he's mainly playing cornerback and he may only play a handful of offensive snaps against the Eagles. Hunter has an interception, three pass breakups, and eight tackles in the last two games.

 

 
 Where do you think Sunday's game will be won and lost? 

 

 TM:  In the trenches. It will be a big challenge for this new-look oline to slow down Jacksonville's respectable front, and equally challenging for Hurts to trust that his protection will hold up amid so many moving parts.

 

 MD:  The Jaguars' offensive line has had trouble with disruptive defensive linemen and the Eagles have two really good ones in Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis . The Jaguars must keep those two from wrecking the game, whether that's pressuring Lawrence or stuffing the run. The Jaguars have also avoided turning the ball over (just two, tied for second-fewest in the league) but that could be an issue if they don't at least limit Carter and Davis.

 Who wins and why? 
 

 TM:  The Jaguars. They are the healthier and more complete team right now. The Eagles defense will have to generate multiple takeaways (they had two against the Rams after being blanked the previous three weeks) if Philadelphia intends to pull off the upset.

 

 MD: It's a good matchup between Coen and Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio. The Jaguars have more playmakers on both sides of the ball, Lawrence is rolling, and some of the Eagles' key players are banged up. Jaguars win.

title: Patriots to honor the 2001 Super Bowl team: Can the 2026 squad learn from them?
summary: Robert Kraft talked about the similarities between the two teams as he prepares to honor the 25th anniversary of the Patriots' first championship.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

 1. Learning from 2001: The Patriots are honoring former kicker Adam Vinatieri at halftime of Sunday's game against the Las Vegas Raiders ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ) for his contributions to their first three Super Bowl championships, which coincides with more than 30 of Vinatieri's former teammates and coaches returning to celebrate the 25-year anniversary of the franchise's first title.

 It's no wonder owner Robert Kraft was nostalgic this week, drawing a link between what he hopes the 2026 team might take from the magical out-of-nowhere 2001 squad.

 "What the '01 team had was that everyone put team first, which was represented by how they came out of the locker room at the Super Bowl," Kraft said of the squad led by coach Bill Belichick, quarterback Tom Brady and a battle-tested defense that upset the Rams  20-17 in Super Bowl XXXVI . "When that happens, great things happen."

 Another obvious link is that the current head coach, Mike Vrabel, was a linebacker on the '01 squad. Vrabel said this week that he was looking forward to connecting with former teammates at a Saturday dinner hosted by Kraft. The Patriots owner noted that what unfolded last week in Orchard Park, New York -- when the Patriots recorded a 29-26 win over the Bills -- felt like '01 vibes to him.

 "There was no way anyone thought we were going to win that game, and our guys put team first," he said. "Drake [Maye] did some things that were spontaneous, like his runs, and we had some of our top players injured, in a tough place to play -- and we win.

 

 "When you go back to this [2001] Super Bowl, we played the 'Greatest Show on Turf,' who had won the Super Bowl the year before, and we were the largest underdogs in the history of the game. No one gave us a chance, and there were these magical moments that happened." 

 Prior to the Super Bowl, Vinatieri delivered one of the most magical moments in Patriots history: a 45-yard field goal in the snow with 27 seconds remaining to tie the Raiders in the AFC divisional round of the playoffs, before kicking the game-winning 23-yarder in overtime.

 Given that history, the Patriots chose Sunday's game against the Raiders to honor Vinatieri.

 "He made those kicks and we couldn't even get the snow cleared out," Kraft said, calling it the greatest game ever hosted in the old Foxboro Stadium. It was also the last one, because the Patriots went on to beat the Steelers on the road in the AFC Championship Game before conquering the Rams one week later in New Orleans -- then opened Gillette Stadium the following year.

 Kraft said he's looking forward to seeing Vinatieri and other players, coaches and their spouses this weekend, while hoping the current team can build off last week's upset win -- perhaps taking a cue from the special '01 celebration.

 

 "We have a very young team now," Kraft said. "It's a wonderful thing for the future, but there is a big learning curve. People are putting team first, winning first.

 "It's like the [Efton] Chism catch [last week] -- nobody would have dreamt that. Here's an undrafted free agent from last year who comes in early every morning and is working hard. A lot of our players are doing that. There's a camaraderie in the locker room that's unique with both of these teams. That's really encouraging."

 2. A.J.'s presence: One thing that stood out from the Patriots' locker room last week was veteran receiver A.J. Brown 's presence. He was more visible than he had been in prior weeks. Brown was wearing cleats, indicating he had been doing rehab work on the field as he works to return from a right high ankle sprain , and seemed to be in good spirits as he chatted with locker mate Drake Maye and others. Brown is eligible to return from the injured reserve list after Sunday's game against the Raiders.

 3. Gonzalez's absence: Top cornerback Christian Gonzalez , who will miss his second straight game due to a shoulder injury , made a brief appearance in the locker room late Friday. Gonzalez, who wasn't wearing a sling, respectfully declined to share details on the injury that occurred during a Sept. 27 loss in Jacksonville that he played through that day. Gonzalez had said he was "good" after the game, but he might have been feeding off adrenaline.

 4. Maye and Mendoza : Much like Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 pick in the NFL draft who is backing up Kirk Cousins , Maye spent the early part of his first NFL season as the backup to a veteran in  Jacoby Brissett . He reflected on how critical that was to his career this week -- watching how Brissett handled adverse situations, the media, locker room relations, etc. -- saying he's still in contact with Brissett regularly and considers him one of his best friends.

 

 Maye also made it a point to salute Cousins, even though that wasn't the initial question, saying, "First off, I want to speak on Kirk. I got to know Kirk a little bit and it's fun to see a guy who has been through the battles on different teams playing great football."

 5. Stat check: Here are some key numbers highlighting areas the Patriots are working to improve:

 
 They have multiple turnovers in five straight games (including playoffs), which is the longest active streak in the NFL and the franchise's longest streak since 1996 (five straight). 
 Maye's nine turnovers are the most in the NFL and tied for most by any player in the first four games of a season in the past 10 years ( Will Levis in 2024, Trevor Lawrence in 2021, Jared Goff in 2019, DeShone Kizer in 2017). They are the most turnovers by a Patriots' player in the first four games of a season since 1992 (Hugh Millen, 11). 
 Maye has been pressured on 44% of dropbacks this season, per ESPN Research, which is the second-highest rate in the NFL ( Jalen Hurts  leads with 48%). 
 
 6. Williams' time: If not now, then when for 2025 third-round pick Kyle Williams ? The Patriots are thin at wide receiver this week without A.J. Brown and his replacement Mack Hollins (calf), leaving Romeo Doubs , DeMario 'Pop' Douglas , Efton Chism III and Williams as the only healthy receivers on the roster. That should mean Williams sees more snaps than the norm (64 snaps, 24.2%).

 Williams has two receptions for 44 yards this season after totaling 10 for 209 yards and three touchdowns last year. Vrabel said Williams continues to improve, acknowledging "sometimes it's hard to hear that or believe that when you have to be able to see the football and get it."

 7. Defensive goals: Veteran safety/captain  Kevin Byard  was buoyed by the defense forcing and recovering a fumble last week (linebacker Robert Spillane /outside linebacker Elijah Ponder ), in addition to a late-game interception (safety Craig Woodson ), but he noted the unit still hasn't met its standard. The Patriots have forced five turnovers this season.

 

 "The goal every week is to get at least three. Haven't got there yet," he said.

 8. TreVeyon's number : Sometimes a jersey number tells a meaningful story, and such is the case with second-year Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson . He said he wears No. 32 in honor of the memory of his grandfather on his mother's side, Albert Harris, who donned that number in high school and went by the nickname "Airplane." It's fitting because the speedy Henderson can fly .

 "He passed away when my mom [Lakeesha] was really young," Henderson said. "I do it to honor my mom as well."

 9. OL dinners: The weekly Patriots' offensive line dinner took place Thursday at Mooo...., a steakhouse in Boston. And as is often the case, Maye joined the group. Past locations this season included Karma Sushi, Luciano's Italian Restaurant and Capital Grille. Among the menu items that landed on the table this week were an American Wagyu Cap (served with lobster) and a Tomahawk steak that Maye and veteran Greg Van Roten enjoyed.

title: HOFer Ronnie Lott offers words of encouragement to Aaron Glenn as losses pile up
summary: Glenn is 4-17 in New York and hasn't beaten a team with a winning record with the 3-1 Browns up next.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- A look at what's happening around the New York Jets :

 1.  Pressure point: It's not an overstatement to say Sunday is one of the most important game of the Aaron Glenn era. He needs a win -- badly.

 Glenn has lost 17 out of 21 games, including three in a row and eight of nine, dating back to last season. He has yet to beat a team with a winning record -- 0-8 in those games. That can change against the better-than-expected Cleveland Browns (3-1), who have a three-game winning streak for the first time since 2023.

 

 If the Browns win, first-year coach Todd Monken will have as many wins in five games as Glenn would have in 22. That would be a bad look for Glenn, who defeated the Browns last year with rookie Dillon Gabriel at quarterback after Cleveland traded their Week 1 starter,  Joe Flacco , and Deshaun Watson  being out for the season with an injury.

 Three of Glenn's four wins have come against backups, but Watson's back this season leading the charge in Cleveland.

 "Sometimes you have to go to dark places, and that's tough," Pro Football Hall of Famer Ronnie Lott told ESPN this week, commenting on the Jets.

 Lott and Glenn were teammates in 1994, Glenn's rookie year. Lott remembers Glenn as a precocious cornerback with a desire to be great. Watching from afar, Lott, one of the greatest winners in NFL history, roots for Glenn to turn around the Jets.

 "When they get it right, it's going to be special," said Lott, a four-time Super Bowl champion with the San Francisco 49ers . "It's when everything starts to click and it feels right. He knows what it feels like and what it smells like. He's been around it in places like Detroit."

 Glenn inherited a 14-year playoff drought, not to mention a slump of nine straight losing seasons. This wasn't going to be an overnight fix. At the same time, it doesn't help Glenn's cause when a team like the Browns, whose star-crossed history rivals that of the Jets, seem to be moving in the right direction in Year 1 of a rebuild.

 "One of the most difficult things is, how do you get people to not accept losing anymore?" Lott said. "Aaron, knowing what I know about him, is trying to accomplish that. Some people can get it done. Some people can't. I hope Aaron gets it done."

 Glenn is one of 16 coaches since the 1970 merger to have four or fewer wins in his first 21 games with the same team, per ESPN Research.

 

 2. Arms race: The Jets and Browns could be competing again in the offseason -- in the college draft.

 Both are expected to be in the quarterback market, and both have the ammunition to make moves. The Jets have three first-round picks, the Browns two. Browns owner Jimmy Haslam is close to the Manning family, fueling speculation he will make a play for Arch Manning .

 Meanwhile, Eli Manning, Arch's uncle, made headlines this week, telling the Barstool Sports podcast "Pardon My Take," "For purely selfish reasons, I wouldn't mind if he went to the Jets, just because I live right there. I could go to games, I could have dinner with him during the week a little bit. I think it'd be great for him to have some family nearby, so I wouldn't mind him going to the Jets, being up in New York."

 Draft season should be fun.

 3. Poised for a breakout? Rookie edge rusher David Bailey isn't racking up big numbers -- only three QB hits and two sacks in 90 pass-rushing opportunities.

 His two sacks barely registered losses -- a combined minus-2 yards. He got credit for a sack when he shoved Cam Ward out of bounds on a scramble. His other sack came when Jordan Love pulled the ball down when Bailey obstructed a designed screen to a wide receiver.

 Not the kind of plays that will make "SportsCenter" highlights. Even Bailey joked that his first NFL sack wasn't how he dreamed of it as a kid.

 

 "I would say he's still learning, he's still growing," Glenn said. "He's going to be a damn good player in this league."

 Overreaction is part of the deal in the NFL, so it's not surprising that some fans are concerned, especially with  Arvell Reese  thriving with the New York Giants . The Jets opted for Bailey over Reese with the second overall pick because they felt he was a pro-ready pass rusher. That said, patience is required.

 "These last couple of weeks, you wouldn't think you'd have tight ends and running backs chipping the rookie, but he's getting that work," defensive line coach Karl Dunbar said. "We're trying to let him understand how he has to work with other guys and just can't be trying to beat everybody by himself. It's a four-man rush. It's not a one-man rush or two-man rush."

 One opposing scout said Bailey relies too much on his speed and needs to be better with his hands. He has a chance for a breakout game against Browns right tackle Tytus Howard , who is shaky in pass protection.

 4. When it rains ...  The forecast calls for rain throughout the day Sunday. Sound familiar? From 2022 to present, the Jets have played more rain games at home (nine) than any other team (based on weather conditions at kickoff). The Seattle Seahawks , who play in the rainy Pacific Northwest, are the next-closest team (five). Oddly, the Giants have played only three rain games at home. Same stadium, different weather. No, the sun isn't shining on the Jets (in more ways than one), but at least they have a winning record (5-4) when it's wet in Jersey.

 

 5. Motion sickness? Offensive coordinator Frank Reich's return after two seasons out of the NFL prompted questions about whether he'd be able to adapt to the current offensive trends. It's early, but here's one observation: Reich, who didn't use a lot of pre-snap motion in the past, still doesn't.

 The Jets have used motion on 56% of their snaps, ahead of only the Pittsburgh Steelers (54%), per Next Gen Stats. (That the Steelers are last isn't a surprise, considering  Aaron Rodgers ' well-documented disdain for pre-snap motion .) The use of motion across the league is at an all-time high. Coaches like it because it can create favorable matchups and force defenses to reveal coverage before the snap. Reich seems hesitant to join the crowd.

 6. Did you know? The Jets have committed only one turnover, which matches 2010 for the fewest through four games in team history.

 7. A real sleeper: On Tuesday, edge rusher Nate Lynn worked out and took a nap. When he woke up, he had 20 messages on his phone, including messages from his mother, his agent and the Jets, who wanted to sign him to the 53-man roster.

 "I rushed over there with a smile on my face and was able to sign," said Lynn, who had been a member of the practice squad.

 Lynn was one of the feel-good stories of the preseason. He was a mid-camp addition and wound up making three sacks in two preseason games, enough to win a job on the practice squad. Braiden McGregor's season-ending pectoral injury opened a spot on the active roster.

 

 8. A what-if story: In January 2021, there was media speculation about the Jets' possible interest in Watson.

 At the time, he had requested a trade from the Houston Texans . It wasn't reported back then, but then-general manager Joe Douglas did have interest in Watson, according to a person familiar with the situation. A serious pursuit never materialized, though.

 That March was the beginning of nearly 30 civil lawsuits by women accusing Watson of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct -- and Watson sat out of the 2021 season.

 Douglas went in a different direction, trading Sam Darnold and drafting Zach Wilson  with the No. 2 pick that year. That, of course, didn't work out.

 9. Still standing: The sudden retirement of Philadelphia Eagles tackle Lane Johnson leaves only eight active players from the 2013 draft. One of them is Jets quarterback Geno Smith , the second-highest drafted player still playing. The highest is tight end Zach Ertz (No. 35 overall). Smith was picked four spots later by the Jets.

title: Christian McCaffrey, Olivia Culpo announce birth of second child
summary: McCaffrey and his wife, Olivia Culpo, announced the news of the birth of their second child in a joint post on Instagram on Saturday.
full_text:
Christian McCaffrey and Olivia Culpo have welcomed their second child, the couple announced Saturday.

 

 McCaffrey, a running back for the San Francisco 49ers , and Culpo, an actress and former Miss Universe, made a joint post on Instagram announcing the news, with the carousel including 10 photos of the newborn, the couple and their eldest child, Colette Annalise, who was born in July 2025 . The post's caption reveals the baby boy's name -- Roman Augustus McCaffrey -- and his date of birth: Sept. 29.

 The couple had announced back in May that they would be expecting another child -- the "best birthday gift" for Culpo.

 

 McCaffery and Culpo have been married since 2024, with the two having met on a blind date in 2019 .
